docs.title: Use Mustache Templates for Prompt Projection
docs.text:
Control exactly how retrieved knowledge and instructions land in the prompt by writing a Mustache template on your Generate node's template parameter and choosing a placement.

Prerequisites

  • A working agent — see Build a chat agent with a graph.
  • For RAG templates: a RAG agent that retrieves chunks — see Create a Simple RAG Assistant.

docs.title: How projection works
docs.text:
Before each Generate call the server builds a Mustache context from the current turn's data and renders the node's template string. The rendered text is then spliced into the prompt according to placement.

The context contains:

Variable Type Contents user_message string The raw user-message text for this turn. slot.<name> string Direct lookup for any slot written so far this turn, by node/output_name, e.g. {{slot.greeter}}. Works for instruction slots, Transform output, and any other producing node's slot. var.<name> string Direct lookup for a declared Agent Variable, e.g. {{var.mood}}. Scalars render as their value (bool as true/false); a set<string> renders sorted and comma-joined (a single string, not an iterable). instructions list of {name, text} Every kind = Instruction slot on the current interaction (one per Instruction/IntentToInstruction node that ran). knowledge list of {name, has_chunks, chunks:[{id,text,distance}]} All KnowledgeComponents from the current interaction (one per Retrieve node). knowledge_<source> list of {id,text,distance} Direct lookup for one retriever's chunks by source label, e.g. {{#knowledge_rag}}.

Each knowledge item carries a has_chunks boolean that is true when the retriever found at least one chunk and false when it returned nothing. Use it to gate the context preamble without the preamble accidentally repeating once per chunk:

{{#knowledge}}
{{#has_chunks}}Context from {{name}}:
{{#chunks}}- {{text}}
{{/chunks}}{{/has_chunks}}
{{^chunks}}No relevant information was found for this topic.{{/chunks}}
{{/knowledge}}

No HTML escaping

All variable values are inserted verbatim — apostrophes, quotation marks, and ampersands are never HTML-encoded. You do not need triple-brace syntax ({{{variable}}}).

Classifier system prompts are a different context

ClassifyIntentLLM also renders its system_prompt as Mustache, but against its own two-variable context — {{intents_block}} (required) and {{letters}} (optional). None of the variables in the table above resolve there, and none of the classifier variables resolve here. See Design an intent-classifier prompt.

docs.title: Placement values
docs.text:
template and placement frame the node's resolved input (the slot input selects, or user_message by default — see Slots and inter-node value passing). The rendered template never replaces the resolved input directly; it is inserted as a separate message around it:

Value string Effect before_user_as_user Emitted as an extra user turn before the resolved input. before_user_as_system Emitted as a system turn before the resolved input (default). after_user_as_user Emitted as an extra user turn after the resolved input. after_user_as_system Emitted as a system turn after the resolved input.

Don't put {{user_message}} (or {{slot.<name>}} for whatever input resolves to) in the template — the resolved input always appears as its own separate turn already; referencing it again in the template duplicates it.

If you want the rendered text to fully replace what the user sees — the old in_place_of_user placement — compose it with a Transform node instead and have Generate consume it via input: see Query rewriting for RAG for the pattern.

docs.title: Step 1 — Simple RAG template
docs.text:
The most common pattern: inject all retrieved chunks before the user message:

PythonC++ 
from tryll_client.graph import (
    GraphDescription, RetrieveParams, GenerateParams, Placement,
)

RAG_TEMPLATE = (
    "{{#knowledge}}"
    "{{name}}:\n"
    "{{#chunks}}- {{text}}\n{{/chunks}}"
    "\n{{/knowledge}}"
)

graph = (
    GraphDescription()
    .add_node("retrieve", RetrieveParams(
        embedded_string_storage="my_kb.json",
        source="docs",
        found_exit="generate",
        not_found_exit="generate",
    ))
    .add_node("generate", GenerateParams(
        template=RAG_TEMPLATE,
        placement=Placement.BeforeUserAsSystem,
        system_prompt="Answer using the context above.",
        # default_exit is "" (END) by default.
    ))
    .set_start_node("retrieve")
    .set_default_model_name("Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)")
)

using namespace Tryll::Client;
using namespace Tryll::NodeParams;

constexpr std::string_view kRagTemplate =
    "{{#knowledge}}"
    "{{name}}:\n"
    "{{#chunks}}- {{text}}\n{{/chunks}}"
    "\n{{/knowledge}}";

RetrieveParamsT retrieveParams;
retrieveParams.embedded_string_storage = "my_kb.json";
retrieveParams.source                  = "docs";
retrieveParams.found_exit              = "generate";
retrieveParams.not_found_exit          = "generate";

GenerateParamsT genParams;
genParams.template_     = std::string{kRagTemplate};
genParams.placement     = ::Tryll::Placement_BeforeUserAsSystem;
genParams.system_prompt = "Answer using the context above.";
// genParams.default_exit is "" (END) by default.

GraphDescription graph;
graph.AddRetrieve("retrieve", std::move(retrieveParams))
     .AddGenerate("generate", std::move(genParams))
     .SetStartNode("retrieve")
     .SetDefaultModelName("Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)");

docs.title: Step 2 — Direct per-source lookup
docs.text:
When your graph has multiple Retrieve nodes with distinct source labels you can access each one directly and format them differently:

{{#knowledge_rules}}
Rule: {{text}}
{{/knowledge_rules}}
{{#knowledge_lore}}
Lore: {{text}}
{{/knowledge_lore}}

Each knowledge_<source> section is a list of chunk objects, so you iterate over it with {{#knowledge_rules}}…{{/knowledge_rules}}.

docs.title: Step 3 — Instructions from InstructionNode
docs.text:
Use an InstructionNode to inject a changeable instruction string into the prompt without touching the graph:

PythonC++ 
from tryll_client.graph import (
    GraphDescription, InstructionParams, GenerateParams, Placement,
)

INSTRUCTION_TEMPLATE = "{{#instructions}}{{text}}\n{{/instructions}}"

graph = (
    GraphDescription()
    .add_node("persona", InstructionParams(
        instruction="You are a friendly guide.",
        default_exit="generate",
    ))
    .add_node("generate", GenerateParams(
        template=INSTRUCTION_TEMPLATE,
        placement=Placement.BeforeUserAsSystem,
        # default_exit is "" (END) by default.
    ))
    .set_start_node("persona")
    .set_default_model_name("Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)")
)

# Later, change persona without recreating the agent:
agent.change_param("persona", "instruction", "You are a sarcastic pirate.")

using namespace Tryll::Client;
using namespace Tryll::NodeParams;

InstructionParamsT personaParams;
personaParams.instruction  = "You are a friendly guide.";
personaParams.default_exit = "generate";
InstructionParamsT personaBaseline = personaParams;   // for ChangeParams below

GenerateParamsT genParams;
genParams.template_ = "{{#instructions}}{{text}}\n{{/instructions}}";
genParams.placement = ::Tryll::Placement_BeforeUserAsSystem;
// genParams.default_exit is "" (END) by default.

GraphDescription graph;
graph.AddInstruction("persona",  std::move(personaParams))
     .AddGenerate("generate",    std::move(genParams))
     .SetStartNode("persona")
     .SetDefaultModelName("Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)");

// Later (clone-set-send via typed ChangeParams):
InstructionParamsT mut = personaBaseline;
mut.instruction = "You are a sarcastic pirate.";
agent.ChangeParams("persona", std::move(mut));

Use {{slot.<name>}} for a direct single-instruction lookup:

{{slot.persona}}

docs.title: Step 4 — Combine instructions and knowledge
docs.text:
Nothing prevents you from using both in one template:

{{#instructions}}{{text}}
{{/instructions}}
{{#knowledge}}{{name}}:
{{#chunks}}- {{text}}
{{/chunks}}
{{/knowledge}}

With placement: before_user_as_system the rendered block becomes a system turn immediately before the user message.

docs.title: Placement guidance
docs.text:
1. before_user_as_system is the default recommendation — most modern chat-tuned models treat system turns as highest-priority.
  2. If the model ignores the context, try before_user_as_user.
  3. The after_* variants are uncommon; they exist for models that prefer seeing the question before the context.
  4. Need to fully replace what the model sees instead of framing around it? Use a Transform node and input instead of template/placement — see Query rewriting for RAG.

docs.title: Verify it worked
docs.text: Create the agent with enable_diagnostics=True (Python) / enableDiagnostics=true (C++). The TurnComplete.debug_info JSON includes the full rendered prompt for each Generate node, so you can inspect exactly what the model received.

docs.title: Common pitfalls
docs.text:
• {{user_message}} (or the resolved-input slot) inside the template. The tag renders the real text, and the placement also emits the resolved input as its own turn, so the prompt contains it twice. The server only logs a warning. Remove it from the template.
  • Unknown sections. Mustache silently ignores unknown section names. If {{#knowledge_rag}} renders nothing, check that your Retrieve node has source: "rag".
  • Empty knowledge. When the template renders to an empty string (e.g. a {{#has_chunks}} block with no chunks), the server skips injecting the extra message entirely. The resolved input still goes through on its own, so the model is never left with an empty turn.

docs.title: Bias Voice Input with Hotwords
docs.text:
Open-vocabulary speech-to-text engines guess every word from acoustic evidence alone, which means they often mangle game-specific proper nouns — the NPC name "Aeltharion" becomes "Al Therion", the spell "frostbolt" becomes "frost bolt". Sherpa-ONNX exposes a hotwords list that nudges the decoder toward a designer-authored set of phrases without retraining the model.

This recipe shows how to ship a phrase list with your game and apply it to a VoiceInput.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A working VoiceInput session — see Use Voice Input for the full setup walkthrough.
  • An STT model that supports hotwords. Most transducer / CTC families do; encoder-decoder families (Whisper, SenseVoice, Moonshine, Canary) log a warning and ignore the list when the voice input is created. The matrix and the warning are in Which models support hotwords below.

docs.title: 1. Author a phrase list
docs.text:
Hotwords live in a StringStorage of kind List, shipped as a UTF-8 text file in your game's storage data folder — one phrase per line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored:

# data/voice-hotwords.txt
# fantasy NPC names
Aeltharion
Cor'than
Bjornthor

# spells / abilities
fireball
frostbolt
magic missile

The file path is relative to the process storage root (Project Settings Storage Data Folder, default TryllStorage/). The server loads it on demand the first time a VoiceInput references it — no CreateStringStorage call is needed.

docs.title: 2. Reference the file when creating VoiceInput
docs.text:
C++

#include <tryll/TryllClient.h>
#include <tryll/VoiceInput.h>

Tryll::Client::VoiceInputConfig viCfg;
viCfg.modelName            = "Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)";
viCfg.inputFormat          = micFormat;
viCfg.hotwordsStoragePath  = "data/voice-hotwords.txt";
viCfg.hotwordsScore        = 1.8f;   // bonus per matched phrase; default 1.5

auto vi = client.CreateVoiceInput(viCfg);

Python

voice = client.create_voice_input(
    model_name="Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)",
    sample_rate=16000, channels=1, bits_per_sample=16,
    hotwords_storage_path="data/voice-hotwords.txt",
    hotwords_score=1.8,
)

Unity (C#)

var cfg = new VoiceInputConfig
{
    ModelName            = "Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)",
    InputFormat          = AudioFormat.Default,
    VadThreshold         = 0.5f,
    VadMinSilenceMs      = 1000,
    VadSpeechPadMs       = 250,
    HotwordsStoragePath  = "data/voice-hotwords.txt",
    HotwordsScore        = 1.8f,
};
var (voice, err) = await client.CreateVoiceInputAsync(cfg);

On TryllVoiceInputComponent, set the same values in the inspector: Hotwords Storage Path (relative to Storage Data Folder; empty disables) and Hotwords Score (default 1.5).

Unreal (C++)

FTryllVoiceInputConfig Config;
Config.ModelName             = TEXT("Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)");
Config.InputFormat.SampleRate = 16000;
Config.HotwordsStoragePath   = TEXT("data/voice-hotwords.txt");
Config.HotwordsScore         = 1.8f;

Subsystem->CreateVoiceInput(Config,
    [](TSharedPtr<FTryllVoiceInput> Voice, FTryllError Err)
    {
        if (!Err.IsOk()) { /* handle error */ return; }
        // Voice is ready — call BeginUtterance to start capturing.
        // BeginUtterance options include auto_finish_on_silence and
        // max_utterance_ms.
    });

The referenced file must exist under the process storage root; a missing file fails CreateVoiceInput with StorageFileNotFound.

docs.title: Picking a score
docs.text:
The score is the bonus added to a matched phrase during beam search (default 1.5). No score value turns biasing off: an empty hotwordsStoragePath is what disables it.

Score Bias Use when… 1.0 light a smaller bonus than the default; still biases 1.5 gentle (default) the lexicon is broad and you do not want false positives 1.8 – 2.5 moderate proper nouns + spell names — typical game lexicon 3.0 – 4.0 aggressive the recognizer keeps picking a phonetically-similar real word and you accept some false positives

The score applies to every phrase in the list — unless a line sets its own. Append :<number> to a lexicon line to bias that phrase alone:

Kaelthorne :3.0
Veyra
frostbolt

Here Kaelthorne is biased at 3.0 and the rest at whatever the session's hotwordsScore is. Use it for the one name a recognizer keeps mangling, instead of raising the score for the whole list and paying for it everywhere.

docs.title: The score you set is one of two
docs.text:
The server applies hotword bias in two places, and only one of them is yours to set per session:

What it does Where it is set Candidate boost makes a hotword's tokens reachable by the recognizer at all the server's model catalog (stt_hotwords_score), per model Phrase weight weights matched phrases against one another hotwordsScore on the VoiceInput — the one in this guide

The catalog value is what lets the recognizer consider Kaelthorne in the first place; hotwordsScore then decides how strongly Kaelthorne competes with the other phrases in your lexicon. You normally only touch the second.

docs.title: Turning biasing on for a model
docs.text:
Biasing needs beam-search decoding, which the server chooses when it loads the model — so it is a per-model decision, not something a single voice input can switch on. The shipped catalog enables it for Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 and no other model.

To change that for your project, use the Hotword biasing control in the Model Manager (beside Memory placement) — it is available on STT models:

Default follow the server's setting for this model Off never bias. Supplying a lexicon then fails with HotwordBiasDisabled (4106) instead of quietly doing nothing On always bias. Beam-search decoding is then in force for every voice input on this model, costing a few percent of decode time and changing its transcripts — on but unused is not free

From code, the same choice is a per-model hint on the session: hotword_hints on create_session in Python; in C++, a TryllClient::ModelPlacementHint with hotwords set, passed in SessionConfig::placementHints:

using Tryll::Client::TryllClient;

TryllClient::SessionConfig cfg;
cfg.placementHints.push_back({
    .modelName = "Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)",
    .hotwords  = ::Tryll::HotwordBias_On,
});
client.CreateSession(cfg);

from tryll_client import HotwordBias

client.create_session(hotword_hints={"Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)": HotwordBias.On})

If hotwords seem to do nothing at all on a model — no value of hotwordsScore changes anything — that model is not enabled for biasing. Check the control above, and the server log, which says hotwords=unavailable on the model's load line.

Raising the score is not free, and past a point it is actively destructive. Bias nudges the beam toward your phrases everywhere, including in speech that contains none of them, and short utterances have the least context to resist it. Measured on Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 with a nine-phrase fantasy lexicon, at score 6.0:

Spoken Transcribed "Fireball" "Mord" "Hello, how are you?" "Mords soul. Mordrian souls souls soul" a four-sentence passage unaffected

So tune against two sets, not one: utterances that contain your terms, and utterances that do not. The second set is what tells you when to stop. Start at 1.5, raise until the terms land, then check the second set before keeping the value.

docs.title: Which models support hotwords
docs.text:
Two things have to be true: the decoder must have a beam for the bias to act on, and the model bundle must carry a sub-word vocabulary the server can encode your phrases with.

Family Hotwords Zipformer transducer / Parakeet TDT (Transducer, NemoTransducer) yes Streaming Zipformer (online transducer) yes Zipformer-CTC, NeMo CTC, Paraformer, Dolphin, WeNet CTC no — no beam to bias Whisper no SenseVoice no Moonshine, Canary, FireRedASR, CohereTranscribe no

When you pass a hotwords list to a model that cannot use it, the server logs a warning when the voice input is created and ignores the phrases, rather than accepting the list silently:

[Sherpa-ONNX] Hotword biasing unavailable for STT family 'whisper'
              (this decoder has no token-level bias hook); ignoring
              9 supplied phrase(s) on this session.

The model's load banner also states it up front:

[Sherpa-ONNX] STT model loaded: … | family=nemo_transducer | … |
              decoding=modified_beam_search | hotwords=available

The session is otherwise unaffected. Hotword-capable models load with beam-search decoding, which costs a few percent of decode time.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Write plain words. The server hands your phrases to the recognizer's own tokenizer, so Aeltharion is what you want in the file — not a pre-tokenized ▁Ael th ar ion. Lexicons written in the older ▁-piece form still work; the server folds them back to graphemes. There is no longer any reason to run text2token.py over a lexicon by hand.
  • A whole utterance biases better than a fragment. The recognizer decodes one speech segment at a time, and a phrase near a segment boundary has less context to be recognised from. If a term is being missed, check whether the pause structure of the speech is splitting the sentence before blaming the score.
  • The score is the default for the whole voice input. A lexicon line that ends with :<number> overrides it for that phrase only.
  • The lexicon is loaded from the process storage root. The server reads the file on demand and caches it. Ship the file with your game data and every session on that server can use it.
  • Out-of-vocabulary characters are dropped. If your lexicon contains characters the model's tokenizer cannot represent (e.g. CJK characters against a pure-English Zipformer), they are silently dropped from the bias.

docs.title: Use Voice Input
docs.text:
Voice Input is the Tryll subsystem that streams raw PCM audio to the server, runs it through a speech-to-text (STT) model, and delivers transcripts back to your application. This page covers the full lifecycle: creating a VoiceInput handle, starting and finishing utterances, streaming audio, and cleaning up. It ends with links to hotwords biasing and model selection.

For the mental model behind this — the utterance lifecycle, push-to-talk vs. hands-free, offline vs. streaming recognisers, and the transcript-update kinds — see Concept: STT and Voice Input.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A connected session. No STT engine setting is needed: the STT model's catalog entry names its engine (Sherpa-ONNX).
  • An STT model on disk — download one in the editor Model Manager, or from code (DownloadModel in C++, download_model in Python, RequestDownloadModel in Unity and Unreal).
  • With the Unity or Unreal voice input component: a microphone. The component checks for one itself and reports when there is none; see Handle a missing microphone.

Optionally, warm the STT engine up at session creation so the first utterance does not pay its start-up cost:

// C++ — `engines` is an optional warm-up hint, not a requirement.
client.CreateSession({
    .engines = {{::Tryll::ModelRole_Stt, ::Tryll::InferenceEngine_SherpaOnnx}},
});

# Python
client.create_session(engines=[(ModelRole.Stt, InferenceEngine.SherpaOnnx)])

The Unity and Unreal plugins build this hint from the Model Manager's manifest when they create the session, so there is nothing to add there.

docs.title: 1. Create a VoiceInput handle
docs.text:
A VoiceInput is a stateful server-side object that holds the loaded STT model and the current utterance state. Create one per microphone source; most games need only one.

C++

#include <tryll/VoiceInput.h>

Tryll::Client::VoiceInputConfig cfg;
cfg.modelName        = "Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)";
cfg.inputFormat      = { .sampleRate = 48000, .channels = 1, .bitsPerSample = 16 };
cfg.vadThreshold     = 0.5f;   // Silero VAD speech-probability threshold
cfg.vadMinSilenceMs  = 1000;   // silence that ends a segment (ms)
cfg.vadSpeechPadMs   = 250;    // padding around detected speech (ms)

auto vi = client.CreateVoiceInput(cfg);

Python

voice = client.create_voice_input(
    model_name="Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)",
    sample_rate=48000, channels=1, bits_per_sample=16,
)

Unity (C#)

var cfg = new VoiceInputConfig
{
    ModelName       = "Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)",
    InputFormat     = new AudioFormat { SampleRate = 48000, Channels = 1, BitsPerSample = 16 },
    VadThreshold    = 0.5f,
    VadMinSilenceMs = 1000,
    VadSpeechPadMs  = 250,
};
var (voice, err) = await client.CreateVoiceInputAsync(cfg);
if (!err.IsOk) { /* handle */ }

Unreal (C++)

FTryllVoiceInputConfig Config;
Config.ModelName              = TEXT("Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (int8)");
Config.InputFormat.SampleRate = 48000;

Subsystem->CreateVoiceInput(Config,
    [](TSharedPtr<FTryllVoiceInput> Voice, FTryllError Err)
    {
        if (!Err.IsOk()) { /* handle */ return; }
        // Store Voice — it is now ready for BeginUtterance.
    });

The server loads the model (or reuses a cached copy) and returns a voice_input_id. Every client wraps that id in a VoiceInput handle (VoiceInput in C++ and Python, TryllVoiceInput in Unity, FTryllVoiceInput in Unreal); you call the utterance methods on the handle.

docs.title: A note on vadSpeechPadMs
docs.text:
The voice-activity detector hands the recognizer only the part of the audio it judged to be speech, cropped tight. Recognizers are trained on recordings, which always begin with a little room tone, so a crop with no silence around it costs you the opening word — and for a very short utterance, everything. A one-word "Fireball" cropped to 0.9 seconds transcribes as nothing at all; with 100 ms of silence added to each end it transcribes correctly.

vadSpeechPadMs is that silence. The server adds it around each segment before decoding, so leave it at the default unless you have a reason not to. Raising it above 500 ms has no effect.

docs.title: 2. Set up transcript callbacks
docs.text:
Register a callback before starting utterances so you receive transcripts as they arrive. Tryll delivers four update kinds:

Kind When SpeechStart VAD detects rising edge; no text yet Partial In-progress hypothesis from online (streaming) STT SegmentFinal Engine committed a chunk; utterance still open UtteranceFinal Last update for this Begin/End cycle

C++

vi.SetOnTranscriptUpdate([](const Tryll::Client::TranscriptUpdate& u) {
    if (u.kind == ::Tryll::TranscriptUpdateKind_UtteranceFinal)
        ProcessFinalTranscript(u.text);
});

Python

from tryll_client.voice_input import TranscriptUpdateKind

def on_transcript(kind: int, text: str, audio_ms_consumed: int) -> None:
    if kind == TranscriptUpdateKind.UtteranceFinal:
        process_final_transcript(text)

voice.set_on_transcript_update(on_transcript)

Unity (C#)

voice.OnTranscriptUpdate += update =>
{
    if (update.Kind == TranscriptUpdateKind.UtteranceFinal)
        ProcessFinalTranscript(update.Text);
};

Unreal (C++)

Voice->OnTranscriptUpdate.AddLambda([](const FTryllTranscriptUpdate& U)
{
    if (U.Kind == ETryllTranscriptUpdateKind::UtteranceFinal)
        ProcessFinalTranscript(U.Text);
});

docs.title: 3. Begin an utterance
docs.text:
BeginUtterance opens a recording window and arms the VAD.

C++

Tryll::Client::UtteranceOptions opts;
opts.autoFinishOnSilence = true;
opts.maxUtteranceMs      = 30000;
vi.BeginUtterance(opts);

Python — VoiceInput.begin_utterance(auto_finish_on_silence=..., max_utterance_ms=...). The transcript callback runs on the reader thread: start a turn from it with send_message_async. The blocking send_message deadlocks on that thread.

Unity (C#)

var opts = new UtteranceOptions
{
    AutoFinishOnSilence = true,
    MaxUtteranceMs      = 30000,
};
voice.BeginUtterance(opts);

Unreal (C++)

FTryllUtteranceOptions Opts;
Opts.bAutoFinishOnSilence = true;
Opts.MaxUtteranceMs       = 30000;
Voice->BeginUtterance(Opts);

The server only transcribes. On a non-empty UtteranceFinal, start the turn yourself: SendText (C++), send_message_async (Python, from the transcript callback), or SendMessage on the agent component (Unity / Unreal). The engine voice components do that when a target agent is set, and drop the final with a warning if that agent already has a turn in flight. Leave the target unset when you want to filter or rewrite the text before sending.

docs.title: 4. Stream audio
docs.text:
Send PCM chunks as fast as they arrive. The buffer is fire-and-forget: no acknowledgement, no backpressure from the server.

C++

// Called from your audio capture code at ~20 ms intervals.
// pcmChunk is a std::vector<std::int16_t> of mono samples.
vi.SendAudioBuffer(pcmChunk);   // binds to std::span<const std::int16_t>

Python

voice.send_audio_buffer(pcm_bytes)   # int16 little-endian PCM bytes

Unity (C#)

// Called on the main thread, e.g. from a coroutine that polls
// Microphone.GetPosition and reads new samples with AudioClip.GetData.
// SendAudioBuffer takes mono 16-bit samples (ReadOnlySpan<short>).
var pcm = new short[floatSamples.Length];
for (int i = 0; i < pcm.Length; i++)
    pcm[i] = (short)(Mathf.Clamp(floatSamples[i], -1f, 1f) * short.MaxValue);
voice.SendAudioBuffer(pcm);

Unreal (C++)

// Called from the audio capture thread.
Voice->SendAudioBuffer(PcmChunk);

Audio must be raw signed-16-bit PCM at the sample rate declared in inputFormat. The server resamples to the model's expected rate as needed. No encoding (opus, mp3, etc.) is supported on the voice path.

docs.title: 5. End or cancel an utterance
docs.text:
If autoFinishOnSilence is true the server closes the segment automatically. You can also close it explicitly:

vi.EndUtterance();    // C++ — commit; produces UtteranceFinal
vi.CancelUtterance(); // C++ — discard; no UtteranceFinal fired

voice.end_utterance()     # Python
voice.cancel_utterance()  # Python

voice.EndUtterance();    // Unity (C#)
voice.CancelUtterance(); // Unity (C#)

Voice->EndUtterance();    // Unreal (C++)
Voice->CancelUtterance(); // Unreal (C++)

docs.title: Push-to-talk
docs.text: Call BeginUtterance when the player presses a button and EndUtterance when they release it. Disable autoFinishOnSilence so VAD does not cut short a deliberate pause mid-sentence.

docs.title: Hands-free (VAD-driven)
docs.text: Keep autoFinishOnSilence = true. The server commits each phrase on silence and fires UtteranceFinal. A non-empty final is the text you send (see §3). The engine voice components drop that final when the target agent already has a turn in flight. Empty finals close the utterance and do not start a turn; during silence the server emits empty SegmentFinal heartbeats you can surface as a "listening…" hint. Open a fresh BeginUtterance for the next turn — typically after the agent's reply and any TTS playback finish, which keeps the mic from transcribing its own output.

docs.title: 7. Destroy the handle
docs.text:
Always destroy the VoiceInput when you are done with it. This frees the model slot on the server.

In C++ the handle is move-only and has no Destroy() method: its destructor cancels any active utterance and destroys the server-side object. Let it go out of scope (or reset the object that owns it); move it to keep it alive longer.

voice.destroy()  # Python — or use `with client.create_voice_input(...) as voice:`

voice.Dispose();  // Unity (C#)

Subsystem->RequestDestroyVoiceInput(Voice);  // Unreal (C++)

docs.title: Handle a missing microphone
docs.text:
The Unity TryllVoiceInputComponent and Unreal UTryllVoiceInputComponent check for a microphone before creating the voice input and before every BeginUtterance. When there is none they do not create the voice input (no STT model is loaded), log one [Tryll] warning naming the component, and report MicrophoneUnavailable (4108) from each call. Text chat is unaffected. Automatic creation (on enable / BeginPlay) only sets the status and logs, because it can run before your listeners are bound: read the status at start-up.

  • Unity: OnError receives the TryllError; MicrophoneStatus / IsMicrophoneUnavailable say why (NoDevice, DeviceNotFound for a micDeviceName that is not connected, or CaptureFailed).
  • Unreal: bind OnErrorDetailed to get the FTryllError with its code (OnError still fires with the message alone); GetMicrophoneStatus / IsMicrophoneUnavailable say why (NoDevice or CaptureFailed).

Show "type to chat" while the microphone is unavailable. To recover, call BeginUtterance again on a user action or a timer: once a microphone is present it creates the voice input and reports VoiceInputStarting (4109) for that one call. In Unreal, if the default device's sample rate changes under a live voice input, BeginUtterance recreates the voice input with the new rate and also reports 4109; the microphone status stays Available. Treat 4109 as "try again in a moment", not as an error to show.

docs.title: Use Your Own Local Model
docs.text:
Register a GGUF file already on disk so Tryll can load it without a Hugging Face download.

Prerequisites

  • A .gguf file inside the server's process storage root, e.g. <Project>/TryllStorage/LocalModels/my-model-q4_k_m.gguf. Unity and Unreal default the root to <Project>/TryllStorage/; a server you run yourself uses --storage-root, storage_root, or the folder of tryll_server.exe. See Server Configuration → Storage root.
  • A JSON file inside your game project, if you use the Unity or Unreal plugin. Any file name. Do not edit the shipped data/models.json — updates overwrite it.
  • No engine setup. The catalog entry's engine decides which engine runs the model.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Put the catalog JSON somewhere inside the project. Any file name, any folder. Same schema as models.json. The key fields are name plus one variants entry with engine = "llama-cpp", a local_path directory, and the files inside it:

    {
  "models": [
    {
      "name": "My Local Model",
      "variants": [
        {
          "engine": "llama-cpp",
          "local_path": "LocalModels",
          "files": ["my-model-q4_k_m.gguf"],
          "kv_cache_type": "q8_0",
          "tool_call_support": "unsupported"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

    A relative local_path resolves against the process storage root, so "LocalModels" above means <storage root>/LocalModels/. An absolute path also works when it points inside that root. A path outside the root (for example C:/models) is ignored with a warning, and the model never resolves. A Client Prod server ignores local_path entirely.

    Leave the shipped models.json unchanged. A relative chat_template_file is resolved against the directory that contains your catalog file, so keep those template files inside the project. The catalog is optional — leave the setting empty if you are not adding models.

    Unity: Project Settings → Tryll Client → Custom Models → Catalog, or Browse.

    Auto-launch runs at BeforeSceneLoad, before any scene Awake. Subscribe before that so the first process sees the file:

    [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.AfterAssembliesLoaded)]
static void PointAtCatalog()
{
    TryllRuntimeSettings.BeforeAutoLaunch += () =>
    {
        var settings = TryllRuntimeSettings.Load();
        if (!settings.TrySetUserModelsCatalogPath("Assets/Tryll/my-models.json", out string error))
            Debug.LogError(error);
    };
}

    Calling TrySetUserModelsCatalogPath after the server is already running restarts it. The open client session is dropped.

    A player build copies the catalog saved in Project Settings to Server/data/user-catalog/ next to the game, including relative chat templates. To pick a different file at runtime in a build, put it under Assets/StreamingAssets/ and set that project-relative path from code.

    Unreal: Project Settings → Plugins → Tryll Client → Models → Catalog, or Browse. From code or Blueprint, Set User Models Catalog Path.

    The first auto-launch runs in the Tryll subsystem's Initialize, before BeginPlay. Set the path from your GameInstance Init (or from Project Settings) so the first process sees it. Calling the setter while a server is already running restarts it when Auto Launch Server is on, and the open session is dropped.

    A packaged build copies the catalog saved in Project Settings to Server/data/user-catalog/ next to the game, including relative chat templates. A different file selected from code in a packaged game is used only when that file is already a loose file inside the project directory.

    The stored path is relative to the project and must stay inside it. If you launch tryll_server yourself, pass the same file as --user-models-path. There is no shipped user catalog. An omitted path still names a sibling user_models.json, and a missing file is silent. An optional models.d directory is loaded when it exists; the install does not create it.

  2. Validate (optional). From the server directory, point at the file you linked:

    tryll_server --check-catalogs --user-models-path "C:/YourProject/Assets/Tryll/my-models.json"

  3. Restart the server (or let the editor relaunch it). Your model appears in ListModels / the Model Manager alongside the shipped catalog.

  4. If something goes wrong: a malformed user file is skipped and the server still starts on the shipped catalog. The startup log names the file and the fix. Duplicate names against a shipped model are ignored for that entry only (rename yours).

docs.title: Unity / Unreal
docs.text: The Catalog field above is the place to link the file. Auto-launch passes it as --user-models-path. In a packaged game that path is the staged copy under Server/data/user-catalog/. A folder named <ProjectRoot>/Tryll/models.d is still passed as --user-models-dir when it exists, for extra drop-in files.

docs.title: Verify Required Models Before Play
docs.text:
Both editor plugins register models per-project as Production or Experimental in the Model Manager, then download them there. If a teammate pulls a repo change that adds or replaces a registered model, that download step is easy to miss — the next time you press Play (or open the Tryll Chat window) with a stale local model cache, CreateAgent used to fail with a GraphCompilationFailed error that gave no hint a download was the fix.

The editor guard closes that gap. It runs automatically at every point an agent is about to be created in the editor. The automatic Play / PIE check is on by default and can be turned off per project if you prefer to manage model provisioning yourself — see Turning off the Play/PIE check.

docs.title: What it checks
docs.text: On each guarded entry point, the guard loads your project's model manifest (the same Production/Experimental registrations you set in the Model Manager), compares every registered model of every kind (language, embedding, STT, TTS, VAD) against the live ListModels status, and treats anything Absent as needing attention.

docs.title: Where it runs
docs.text:
Entry point Behaviour Play (Unity) / PIE (Unreal) Blocks automatically: downloads every missing registered model behind a cancelable progress dialog, then continues into Play/PIE once ready. Cancelling, or a model that fails to download, keeps you in the editor instead. Tryll Chat window/panel Same automatic, blocking treatment as Play — the guard runs right after the session is created and before the chat agent is built. Model Manager window/panel Lighter-touch: after the model list loads, if anything registered is missing you get a Yes/No prompt instead of an automatic download — this is also where you'd go to fix it manually.

Unity: what a cancelled Play looks like

Unity has no way to pause entering Play mid-transition, so the guard cancels the transition, runs the check with a progress dialog, and — once every model is confirmed downloaded — automatically re-enters Play for you. You don't need to press Play twice.

docs.title: Turning off the Play/PIE check
docs.text:
The automatic Play (Unity) / PIE (Unreal) check is on by default but can be disabled per project:

  • Unreal: Project Settings → Plugins → Tryll Client → Editor → Enable Play Mode Model Guard (the bEnablePlayModeModelGuard field on UTryllRuntimeSettings, saved to DefaultGame.ini). Uncheck it to enter PIE immediately with no pre-flight model check.
  • Unity: Project Settings → Tryll Client → Play Mode (Editor) → Enable Play Mode Model Guard (the EnablePlayModeModelGuard field on TryllRuntimeSettings). Uncheck it to enter Play immediately with no pre-flight model check.

The toggle affects only the automatic Play/PIE check — the Tryll Chat window/panel still verifies models before creating its agent, and the Model Manager still prompts for missing ones. With the check off, a required model that isn't on disk surfaces as a CreateAgent failure at runtime instead of being caught (and offered for download) before Play.

docs.title: A model that can't be downloaded
docs.text: Some registered models are supplied as a local file path rather than a HuggingFace repo (see Use Your Own Local Model). If one of those is registered but missing on disk, the guard cannot fetch it — it surfaces a clear error naming the model instead of attempting a download. Provide the file or remove the registration in the Model Manager.

docs.title: Relationship to auto model downloading
docs.text:
Earlier releases had a server-side allow_auto_model_downloading session flag that made the server silently fetch a model mid-CreateAgent. That flag has been removed — model registration is now the only way to acquire models deliberately. This guard is the editor-side replacement: it catches the same "model referenced but never downloaded" case, earlier, and with a clear prompt instead of a silent multi-gigabyte download hidden inside a normal request.

Editor-only in both engines — packaged/Standalone builds never run this code, since they bundle Production models at build time and never download at runtime.

docs.title: Model Benchmarks
docs.text:
Provisional · immersion guard, speed and memory

How catalog models do on the jobs Tryll gives them, measured by the Tryll team on our own test sets. Measured so far: the immersion guard, General guard (attempts to pull the NPC out of the game) and World guard (lines that do not belong in the setting), and speed and memory: how fast a model reads its prompt and writes its answer, and how much graphics memory it needs. NPC roleplay, tool calling and summarization will follow.

The numbers are provisional: 13 models. The guard is measured once per model (it reads probabilities and does not sample), at a 5 in 100 false-block budget, with World guard on one game setting. Speed and memory are measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti with Vulkan; other hardware gives other numbers.

docs.title: Bonsai 8B (Q1_0 1-bit)
docs.text:
Model card

As an immersion guard, blocks 32 in 100 general attacks and 60 in 100 world attacks at a 5% false-block budget. Writes 238 tokens per second and needs 1.9 GB of VRAM at 8K context.

Bonsai · 8B · Q1_0 1-bit · 1.2 GB file · prism-ml/Bonsai-8B-gguf

Measured 2026-10-07 · Tryll 0.8.0-DEV · llama.cpp b10839 · NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti · vulkan · one deterministic pass (classifiers do not sample) · speed: median of 10 runs · ranked against 13 models

docs.title: Plain words
docs.text:
What the measured numbers mean for a game. Intervals and ranks are under In the field.

32 in 100 · Classification · General guard. Blocks 32 in 100 attempts to pull the NPC out of the game: asking whether it is an AI, jailbreaks, prompt leaks, coding requests and format tricks. Normal player lines wrongly blocked: 5 in 100 on held-out lines (the budget is 5 in 100, set on a separate tuning set).

60 in 100 · Classification · World guard. Blocks 60 in 100 lines that do not belong in the setting, such as paying by phone in a medieval town or asking how long chicken keeps in the fridge. Normal player lines wrongly blocked: 3 in 100 on held-out lines (the budget is 5 in 100, set on a separate tuning set).

World guard is measured on one setting, a medieval merchant. A different world needs its own check.

4,805 tokens/s · Performance · Prefill. Reads a 3,959-token prompt in 0.82 s. The first token reaches the player after 0.85 s. A 1,146-token prompt: first token after 0.26 s.

238 tokens/s · Performance · Generation. Writes 238 tokens per second after a 1K-token prompt, and 217 after a 4K-token prompt. 200 tokens take 0.8 s.

1.9 GB VRAM · Performance · Memory. Weights 1.15 GB, KV cache 0.64 GB for 8,192 tokens (q8_0), compute buffers 0.10 GB. Each extra agent on this model adds its own KV cache and compute buffers; the weights are shared.

Speed and memory were measured on one GPU, named in the header. Other hardware gives other numbers.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Complete, declarative documentation of every Tryll surface. Use this section when you need an authoritative answer about what a field is, what values it accepts, or what a specific error code means. For conceptual background, see the Concepts section; for task-driven walkthroughs, see How-to.

It splits in two: Client API is what your game code calls, Workflows and data is what you declare for the server to execute.

docs.title: Client API
docs.text: The surface your game code touches — one page per platform, plus the request fields, diagnostics, and errors shared by all of them.

docs.title: Per platform
docs.text:
• Unity — the com.tryll.client package: TryllClient, TryllAgentComponent, TryllWorkflowAsset, TryllRuntimeSettings, TryllSpeaker, TryllVoiceInputComponent.
  • Unreal C++ — TryllClient plugin headers: UTryllSubsystem, FTryllAgent, and friends.
  • Unreal Blueprint — every Blueprint-exposed UFUNCTION.
  • C++ — Tryll::Client::*.
  • Python — tryll_client.

docs.title: Shared across platforms
docs.text:
• Agent Parameters — every field on CreateAgentRequest: graph, default model name, diagnostics, dialogue-history retention, variables, KV-cache initialization, workload. Tool schemas live on the Tool Call node, not on the request.
  • Turn Inspector — the shared per-turn diagnostics panel: every block, when each appears, and what to do when one is missing. Hosted by the Chat Window, Agent Log, and Dialog Lab.
  • Turn Diagnostics JSON — every field of the debug_info payload behind that panel, and behind TurnComplete on the wire: the envelope, the per-node sections, and why a key is absent.
  • Error Codes — numeric catalog, ranges, per-code recovery guidance.

docs.title: Workflows and data
docs.text: What you declare, and what the server does with it.

docs.title: Workflow nodes
docs.text:
Node catalog — the table of every node type, its exits, and whether it needs a model. Start there when choosing a node.

Node What it does Generate Run a language model on the projected dialogue and emit its answer. Generate and Speak Generate and synthesize speech in one fused streaming step. Speak TTS-only — voice text another node already produced. Instruction Inject a static instruction via the {{#instructions}} block. Transform Model-free Mustache rendering into a slot; emits nothing on the wire. Branch Model-free conditional routing on a slot or agent variable. Pause Suspend the turn between nodes and hand control back to the client. Retrieve Search an embedded string storage and attach the hits as knowledge. Write to Memory Experimental: upsert a record into a named mutable knowledge base. Summarize Fold ageing turns into a rolling summary so long conversations stay coherent. Classify Intent Label the input by top-1 embedding similarity; exits found / not_found. Classify Intent (LLM) Label the input by first-token logprob on a small model. Intent to Instruction Map an intent label to an instruction through a Map-kind storage. Tool Call Advertise tools, let the model call them, control notify/pause/results. Canned Response Emit a fixed reply from a string storage — no model involved. Regex Guardrail Match input against patterns and route away before spending a model call.

Filter grammar is not a node: it is the JSON predicate language that Retrieve and Classify Intent accept in their filter param for metadata-filtered search.

Voice Profile is not a node either: it is the agent's one voice, which every Speak and Generate and Speak node of the agent uses. It holds the TTS model, the voice identity, and the named delivery modes.

docs.title: Knowledge and strings
docs.text:
• String Storage — session-owned name-to-strings containers (List / Map / Multimap) used by canned-response, guardrail, and intent nodes.
  • Embedded String Storage — vector-indexed knowledge bases used by retrieve and intent nodes.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
• Model Management — models.json schema, variants, download and load lifecycle, model status.
  • TTS Models — shipped voices (Sherpa-ONNX and llama.cpp SNAC), which families Tryll supports, and why the rest cannot load.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
• Server Configuration — every field of server-config.json.
  • Telemetry — what usage telemetry collects, and how to turn it off.
  • Wire Protocol — TCP framing, FlatBuffers schema, session flow, ErrorResponse shape. The contract a third-party client must implement.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: • Glossary — canonical definitions for every term used across the documentation. Check here before guessing what a word means.

docs.title: Agent Log format
docs.text:
Export in the Agent Log writes one JSON document. The format identifier is tryll.agent_log and format_version is 1. Readers should ignore keys they do not know. There is no importer.

The file can contain player input, prompts, lore, tool arguments, and diagnostics. It is a bug report from this editor's connection, not a redacted transcript.

docs.title: Document
docs.text:
Key order is fixed: format, format_version, exported_at, exporter, protocol, server, capture, agents, events, turns.

Key Contents exporter unity or unreal, the editor version, the plugin version, the project name, and the OS. protocol Wire version and the codegen fingerprint that rendered the payloads. server Version, run id, build config, and mode, when the connection hello carried them. capture capturing, paused, discarded, or idle; retention limits; how many turns and observations were evicted; the oldest retained timestamp. agents One row per agent that appeared, with its label, whether diagnostics were on, and created_seq / destroyed_seq. A null created_seq means the agent already existed when capture started. events The journal, after export coalescing. turns An index. duration_ms and ttft_ms come from turn diagnostics when that JSON is present. Otherwise they are measured on the client and the row has "timing_source": "client". A turn still in progress has complete: false and no status.

A field that does not apply is left out. Ids are never written as 0.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Field Meaning seq Journal order. Unique in the file. A coalesced run keeps the first event's seq. t_ms Milliseconds since the oldest retained event. t_end_ms, chunks Only on a merged run. dir out or in. Omitted for local events. kind request, reply, push, error, connection, local_error, or marker. type The message or local-event name. turn epoch:agent:request. payload The message body rendered from the schema. Bulk fields such as PCM are {"omitted": true, "count": N, "bytes": B} and the bytes are not in the file.

arguments_json stays a string. The tool-call panel in the window is what pretty-prints it.

Runs merge only when the schema marks the message for coalescing, and only across events of the same type, the same turn (or the same request or voice stream), and the same node name. A node-name change ends the run. A non-delta answer replaces the text instead of appending.

docs.title: Checking a file
docs.text:
From the repo:

python tools/agent_log_check.py path/to/TryllAgentLog.json

The command checks the envelope and prints agents, turns, errors, and capture gaps. python tools/agent_log_check.py --compare a.json b.json compares two exports after dropping timestamps, the exporter block, and renumbering ids.

docs.title: Agent Parameters
docs.text:
Every agent in Tryll is created by a single wire frame: CreateAgentRequest. This page documents every field on that request, grouped by what it controls:

  1. The graph the agent will run.
  2. The fallback model every language-model node uses by default.
  3. Diagnostics.
  4. The agent's variables declaration.
  5. KV-cache initialization.
  6. The agent's workload class.
  7. The agent's voice.

The authoritative source for every shape below is the wire protocol.

Changing parameters after creation

Many node parameters can be updated after the agent is created and while it is idle. See Change Agent Parameters at Runtime for the full list and API examples.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Field Type Required Default Description request_id uint64 Yes — Client-assigned correlation id. Echoed on CreateAgentResponse and on any ErrorResponse replacing it. graph GraphDescription Yes — The workflow graph. See Graph. default_model_name string No "" Fallback model name for language-model nodes (Generate, GenerateAndSpeak, ToolCall, ClassifyIntentLLM, Summarize) that do not set their own model_name param. Empty = no default; every such node must supply its own. See Default model. enable_diagnostics bool No false When true, the server serialises per-node execution data into TurnComplete.debug_info. maintain_dialogue_history bool No true When true (default) the agent keeps its full dialogue history across turns. When false the history is cleared after each turn completes — a stateless agent whose turns start with only the system prompt and the new message. Useful for technical agents (classification, routing, tool-picking) that gain nothing from prior turns and should not pay to store or project them. variables [AgentVariable] No [] The agent's complete variable declaration — every variable it will ever have, with its initial value. The value's type fixes that variable's type for the agent's lifetime; post-create writes to an undeclared name are rejected. See Variables. kv_cache_initialization AgentKvCacheInitialization No AllocateOnly How the agent's language-model KV caches are prepared at creation: AllocateOnly (default), Prefill, or DeferAllocation. See KV-cache initialization. workload AgentWorkload No Interactive Scheduling hint, fixed for the agent's lifetime: Interactive (default) or Background for agents nobody waits on, which the inference scheduler paces or defers first under load. See Inference throttle and agent workload. voice VoiceProfile When a node speaks absent The agent's one voice: TTS model, identity, emit_visemes and delivery modes. Required when the graph has a Speak or GenerateAndSpeak node. See Voice.

A CreateAgentRequest is rejected with error 3003 GraphCompilationFailed if any graph validation rule below fails. Voice errors have their own codes; see Voice.

docs.title: Graph
docs.text:
GraphDescription carries the full topology of the agent's workflow.

Field Type Description nodes [NodeDescription] List of every node in the graph. At least one. start_node string Name of the node where execution begins. Must match a node in nodes.

Wiring between nodes is encoded in each node's typed params object, not in a separate list. Each declared exit has a corresponding <exit_name>_exit field (e.g. default_exit, triggered_exit). An empty string routes the turn to END. A non-empty string must name another node in nodes — the server rejects graphs where an exit field names a missing node with error 3003 GraphCompilationFailed.

docs.title: NodeDescription
docs.text: Field Type Description name string Node instance name. Unique within the graph. Also the default source label on Retrieve. params_type union tag Selects the typed params table variant (GenerateParams, RegexGuardrailParams, etc.). params typed table The typed params table for this node type. Contains configuration fields (model name, prompts, …) and exit fields (default_exit, triggered_exit, …). Each node's reference page lists all available params and exit fields.

docs.title: ToolDefinition
docs.text:
Tool schemas are not a NodeDescription field. They live on the Tool Call node's own params, in ToolCallParams.tools: [ToolDefinition].

Field Type Description name string Tool name exposed to the model. description string Short description shown to the model as part of the tool prompt. parameters [ToolParamDefinition] Parameter schema for the tool.

docs.title: ToolParamDefinition
docs.text:
Field Type Description name string Parameter name. type string Type hint as a string (e.g. "string", "integer"). Model-facing only; the server does not validate arguments. description string Short description of the parameter.

See Tool Call node and the tool-calling concept page for how the server uses these definitions.

docs.title: Default model
docs.text:
default_model_name is a fallback used by language-model nodes that omit their own model_name param: Generate, GenerateAndSpeak, ToolCall, ClassifyIntentLLM, and Summarize. Speak, and the speech half of GenerateAndSpeak, take their TTS model from the agent's voice (voice.tts_model_name) and never use this field. Leaving it empty is legal — every such node must then supply model_name itself; any node missing both results in a compilation failure.

Naming resolves against the model catalog (models.json). The server loads the model on demand if it is not already resident; see model management.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
When enable_diagnostics = true, every TurnComplete carries a JSON string in debug_info describing what the turn did: the nodes it ran and the exit route each took, the prompt every model received, what each node produced, and engine counters. Turn Diagnostics JSON documents every field, including why a given key may be absent.

enable_diagnostics is structural: it is fixed for the agent's lifetime and cannot be turned on for an agent that already exists. Two server-side flags in server-config.json trim the payload further — include_engine_diagnostics removes the engine sections, and include_interaction_in_diagnostics removes the end-of-turn interaction snapshot.

The default is false — no diagnostics, zero overhead. Flip it on for debug sessions only; payloads grow linearly with graph size and knowledge component count.

The editor tooling manages this for you: the Chat Window enables it on the agent it creates, and the Agent Log holds a lease so agents created while it is open request diagnostics too. See How to define and handle tool calls for a worked example that turns diagnostics on to inspect the tool-call detection path.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
variables declares the agent's typed per-agent key→value store, complete at creation. Each AgentVariable carries a name and an initial value whose active type (int64 / double / string / bool / set<string>) fixes that variable's type for the agent's lifetime.

  • Consumed by Mustache templates as {{var.<name>}}, by the Retrieve / ClassifyIntent filter grammar as a {"var": "<name>"} operand, and — when a Generate / GenerateAndSpeak node sets substitute_agent_variables — by __NAME__ marker substitution in streamed output.
  • Mutated over the wire with UpdateAgentVariablesRequest; writes to an undeclared name are rejected locally without a round-trip. An invalid declaration fails creation with 3015 InvalidVariableValue; runtime write errors are 3013 UnknownVariable and 3014 VariableTypeMismatch.

See Concept: Agent Variables and the how-tos Drive prompts and retrieval from game state and Substitute agent variables in LLM output.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text:
voice is the agent's voice profile: the TTS model (tts_model_name, required), the base identity (speaker_id, reference_voice or voice_description), speed, lang, emit_visemes, and named delivery modes. Every speaking node of the agent uses it; the nodes hold no voice settings.

  • Required when the graph speaks. If any node is a Speak or GenerateAndSpeak and voice is absent, creation fails with 3025 AgentVoiceRequired. There is no default voice.
  • Optional otherwise. An agent whose graph never speaks loads no TTS model, even with a voice. It cannot be given a voice later, so pass one at creation if you will need SetAgentVoice or SetAgentDeliveryMode.
  • Validated when set. A field the model cannot use, a missing clip, or an unknown model fails creation with 3023 InvalidVoiceProfile; a session language the model does not declare fails with 3017 ModelLanguageUnsupported.
  • Not a node parameter. ChangeAgentParam cannot change it. Replace it with SetAgentVoiceRequest (idle only) and switch its delivery mode with SetAgentDeliveryModeRequest (any time).

See Voice Profile for every field and rule.

docs.title: KV-cache initialization
docs.text:
kv_cache_initialization chooses how the agent's eligible language-model contexts (LLM nodes only — embeddings and all STT/TTS models, including the llama.cpp voices Orpheus and Maya1, are unaffected) are prepared when the agent is created:

Value Behavior AllocateOnly (default) Allocate each context's KV cache but do not decode anything yet. Prefill Allocate and decode each context's reusable prefix up front, so the first turn skips that cost. Prefill failure surfaces as 4004 KvCacheOperationFailed. DeferAllocation Defer even allocation until the first send.

Idle agents also support the aggregate PrefillAgentKvCache, EvictAgentKvCache, and GetAgentKvCacheStatus operations; eligible contexts are restored automatically before every send. See Manage an agent's KV cache.

docs.title: Embedded String Storage
docs.text:
An embedded string storage is a session-owned, named, vector-indexed container of text chunks. It is the backing store for every Retrieve node in a graph — the building block of RAG in Tryll.

Under the hood, each storage holds:

  1. A list of records — { id, text } pairs, optionally with metadata.
  2. A precomputed embedding per record.
  3. An HNSW index over those embeddings, tuned for cosine distance.
  4. An in-process Okapi BM25 index over record text (persisted as a .bm25 sidecar on Path A), used by Retrieve in Lexical / Hybrid modes. Tokenization is Unicode-aware (casefold + letter/number split via utf8proc); sidecar format version 2 — older ASCII-casefold sidecars are rebuilt on next load.

Dense retrieval uses embedding similarity. Lexical / Hybrid modes add BM25 (and RRF fusion for Hybrid). For plain substring / regex / exact-match over non-embedded lists, see string storage.

docs.title: Node param: relative file path (preferred)
docs.text:
Set the node's embedded_string_storage parameter to a relative path under the process storage root:

embedded_string_storage = "rag/adventure_quests.json"

The path is resolved at CreateAgentRequest time against the process storage root, set at server startup (see Server Configuration → Storage root). There is no per-session root; a path that resolves outside it is rejected with 3009 StorageOutsideRoot. The server loads the KB config file, builds or reuses a cached HNSW index, and Pins the entry so it survives eviction for the lifetime of the agent.

docs.title: Creation paths (explicit Pin)
docs.text:
CreateEmbeddedStringStorageRequest supports two construction paths. Exactly one is used per request.

Path Trigger What the server does A (file-backed) config_path set Relative path resolved against the process storage root. Loads the KB config JSON, resolves records_file and optional index_file / bm25_file relative to the config's directory, builds or loads the HNSW + BM25 indexes, and Pins the entry. B (inline) strings non-empty Embeds every string with embedding_model and builds an in-memory HNSW index. Registered as a virtual entry under name.

embedding_model is required for Path B (inline strings). For Path A (file-backed), the model is taken from the KB config file; the wire embedding_model field is ignored.

docs.title: Path A — config_path
docs.text:
The config is a UTF-8 JSON file with this shape:

{
    "version": 1,
    "embedding_model": "All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)",
    "records_file": "adventure_quests.kb.json",
    "index_file": "adventure_quests.kb.usearch",
    "bm25_file": "adventure_quests.kb.bm25",
    "bm25_tokenizer": "basic",
    "fields": [
        { "name": "min_level",         "type": "int",         "default": 0      },
        { "name": "character_class",   "type": "string",      "optional": true  },
        { "name": "character_classes", "type": "set<string>", "optional": true  }
    ]
}
Field Type Required Description version int No Schema version. Currently 1. embedding_model string Yes Catalog name of the embedding model. Must exist in models.json with "model_type": "embedding". records_file string Yes Relative path (from the config file's directory) to the records JSON. index_file string No Relative path to a pre-built *.usearch HNSW index. If absent, the server builds the index at load time from the records and their embeddings. bm25_file string No Relative path to a persisted BM25 sidecar. If omitted and index_file is set, defaults to the same stem with a .bm25 extension (e.g. adventure_quests.kb.usearch → adventure_quests.kb.bm25). First load builds and writes the sidecar; later loads reuse it until the records file is newer, or format / tokenizer / doc-count mismatch forces a rebuild. bm25_tokenizer string No "basic" (default) or "enhanced". Both modes Unicode-casefold via utf8proc, then split on non-letter/non-number. "enhanced" additionally drops a small English stopword set and applies a trivial suffix strip. Stored in the sidecar header; changing it forces a rebuild. Format version 2 (utf8proc) rebuilds any version-1 ASCII sidecar automatically. fields array No Typed metadata schema — field declarations for filterable record metadata. When present, each record's metadata object is validated against it at load time. See Metadata schema.

The records file (*.kb.json by convention) is a JSON array of objects:

[
    {
        "id":   "ai_storytellers_1",
        "text": "The AI storyteller is the main mechanism used to ...",
        "metadata": { "source": "…", "link": "…" }
    },
    {
        "id":   "ai_storytellers_2",
        "text": "…"
    }
]

Per record:

Field Type Required Description id string Yes Stable identifier; returned on retrieval so clients can map back to the source. text string Yes The chunk text, already segmented to a size that fits within the embedding model's context window. metadata object No Optional typed metadata object. When the config declares a fields schema, each record's metadata is validated and stored in typed slots used by the Retrieve node's filter predicate. Fields not listed in the schema are ignored.

If an index_file is present, its dimension must match embedding_model's output dimension; a mismatch is rejected with error 8003 InvalidEmbeddedStringStorageData.

docs.title: Metadata schema
docs.text: When a config includes a fields array, the server validates every record's metadata object against it at load time and stores the values in typed per-field slots. Those slots are what the Retrieve node's filter predicate compares against during vector search — the filter compiler resolves field names to slot indices once at compile time, so no string lookups happen on the hot path.

docs.title: Field declarations
docs.text:
Each entry in fields declares one filterable field:

Key Required Description name Yes Field identifier used in records and in filter references ({"knowledge": "<name>"}). type Yes One of int, float, string, bool, set<string>. default Exclusive with optional Value applied when a record omits this field. Must be coercible to type. optional Exclusive with default true — missing field is allowed; filters referencing it on a record where it is absent evaluate to false. filterable No (default true) If false, the field is loaded but cannot be referenced in filters. Useful for display-only fields such as page_title.

Exactly one of default or optional: true must be present — a field that is neither is a load-time error.

docs.title: Supported types
docs.text: Type JSON value in records Notes int number (integer) Stored as int64. float number Stored as double. int↔float promotion is allowed in comparisons. string string bool true / false set<string> array of strings Stored sorted and deduplicated. Used as the haystack of an in op.

docs.title: Missing-field semantics
docs.text: When a field is declared optional: true and a record omits it, every comparison or in operation that references that field on that record evaluates to false. The field is not treated as "no restriction" — filter authors who want an unrestricted fallback should encode it explicitly with or and a separate boolean gating field.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
    "version": 1,
    "embedding_model": "All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)",
    "records_file": "adventure_quests.kb.json",
    "index_file":   "adventure_quests.kb.usearch",
    "fields": [
        { "name": "topic",             "type": "string",      "default": ""       },
        { "name": "min_level",         "type": "int",         "default": 0        },
        { "name": "tier",              "type": "string",      "default": "common" },
        { "name": "character_class",   "type": "string",      "optional": true    },
        { "name": "character_classes", "type": "set<string>", "optional": true    },
        { "name": "quest_reached",     "type": "string",      "optional": true    }
    ]
}

A record that uses this schema might look like:

{
    "id":   "warrior_combat_intro",
    "text": "The sword-and-shield style favoured by Aldhaven warriors …",
    "metadata": {
        "topic":             "Combat",
        "min_level":         1,
        "character_classes": ["warrior", "paladin"]
    }
}

topic, min_level, and tier use defaults when absent. character_class, character_classes, and quest_reached are optional and will evaluate to false in any filter that references them on a record that omits them.

See Retrieve filter grammar for the full JSON predicate syntax that queries these fields.

docs.title: Path B — inline strings
docs.text:
For programmatic small-scale use, the client sends strings directly:

Field Type Required Description name string Yes Unique name within the session. strings [string] Yes The chunks. The server assigns sequential ids ("0", "1", …). embedding_model string Yes Catalog name of the embedding model.

The server embeds every string at creation time and builds the index in memory. Nothing is written to disk; the storage is gone once the session ends.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
The preferred approach is a relative file path on the node param — no explicit Create / Destroy is needed. The server caches the loaded index and Pins it when the agent is created; the cache entry reverts to OnDemand (eligible for eviction) when the agent is destroyed.

Use explicit CreateEmbeddedStringStorageRequest / DestroyEmbeddedStringStorageRequest only when you need to share the same index across multiple agents or supply inline strings (Path B).

Step Frame Notes Lazy load (none) Set embedded_string_storage = "relative/kb.json" on the node param. The server resolves, loads, and Pins the index at CreateAgentRequest time. Explicit Pin CreateEmbeddedStringStorageRequest Pins the storage so it persists beyond a single agent creation. Server responds with CreateEmbeddedStringStorageResponse carrying record_count and embedding_dim. Use (referenced by Retrieve node embedded_string_storage param) Scoped to the session. For a Path A storage the param value is the relative config_path; for a Path B storage it is the name used at creation. Explicit Unpin DestroyEmbeddedStringStorageRequest For file-backed (Path A) entries: demotes from Pinned to OnDemand, eligible for eviction once no agent holds it. For virtual (Path B) entries: removes the named entry. Server responds with Ack.

See Lifetime and Ownership → EmbeddedStringStorage for the full ownership model and the separation between the on-disk index cache and the in-memory index object.

docs.title: Consumption by Retrieve
docs.text:
A Retrieve node names the storage via its embedded_string_storage param. Per turn, the node:

  1. Embeds the user's message with the embedding model recorded in the KB config file referenced by embedded_string_storage.
  2. Queries the storage's HNSW index for the top_k closest records by cosine distance. If a filter is set on the node, each candidate record's metadata is evaluated against the compiled predicate during the search; records that do not match are excluded before top_k is applied.
  3. Drops results whose distance exceeds threshold.
  4. Emits one knowledge component per surviving record onto the current interaction.

How those components appear in the prompt is controlled by the downstream Generate node's template (Mustache) and placement params — see Use Mustache Templates.

docs.title: Validation and errors
docs.text:
The server validates at creation time:

  • Exactly one of config_path / strings must be set.
  • Path B: the wire embedding_model must be in the catalog with "model_type": "embedding".
  • Path A: the KB config's embedding_model must be in the catalog with "model_type": "embedding".
  • Path A: records_file must exist, parse, and be non-empty.
  • Path A with index_file: the index must load and its dimension must match the embedding model.
  • Path B: strings must be non-empty.
Code Cause 8001 Name empty, malformed, or reserved. 8002 A storage with this name already exists in the session. 8003 Content rejected: missing / corrupt config or records, empty inline array, unknown embedding model, or index-dimension mismatch.
