docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text:
Every Tryll server response that is not a normal success reply carries an ErrorResponse frame with a numeric code and a human-readable message. Codes are grouped by the layer that produces them, and each range has a characteristic recovery strategy.

This page lists every code defined in ErrorCodes.h. A few are reserved or raised only by the client; their rows say so. If a client ever receives a code not listed here, treat it as a protocol violation (server/client version mismatch) and log both the code and the message verbatim.

docs.title: Error-code ranges
docs.text:
Range Layer Typical recovery 1xxx Connection Reconnect after backoff; session state is gone. 2xxx Session Re-send CreateSessionRequest; stop issuing requests if the server is shutting down. 3xxx Agent Depends on the code. For a bad agent id, a graph that does not compile, or a storage path problem (3001–3003, 3008–3011), fix the graph or id and recreate the agent. Most other 3xxx codes leave the agent usable; see the per-code recovery. 4xxx Inference / workflow / voice input Local to the turn or request that failed; other turns and other agents are unaffected. 5xxx Protocol / framing Client bug or version mismatch; stop and investigate. 6xxx Model download User-actionable (disk, network, catalog); retry once resolved. 7xxx String storage Fix the input and re-create the storage. 8xxx Embedded string storage / mutable KB Fix the config, schema, or snapshot and retry.

The authoritative source of every code is tryll/common/include/tryll/ErrorCodes.h. Client libraries expose the same values: Tryll::Client::ErrorCode (C++), tryll_client.ErrorCode (Python), ETryllErrorCode (Unreal).

docs.title: 1xxx — Connection
docs.text:
These errors surface client-side only: the client failed to reach the server, lost the TCP connection, or timed out waiting for a reply. The server never emits 1xxx codes itself.

Code Name Meaning 1001 ConnectionFailed TCP connect to the configured host/port failed outright. The server process is not running or the port is blocked. 1002 ConnectionDropped The established connection was closed mid-session (peer close, socket error, network partition). Session state on the server is gone. 1003 Timeout The client gave up waiting for a response frame. The socket itself may still be healthy; typically the server is overloaded or a node hung.

Recovery: reconnect after exponential backoff; re-configure the session; recreate agents.

docs.title: 2xxx — Session
docs.text:
The server rejected a request because the session is not in the right state to accept it, or because the server is shutting down.

Code Name Meaning 2001 ServerShuttingDown The server is in graceful shutdown and no longer accepts new requests on this session. In-flight turns continue until they complete or time out. 2002 SessionNotReady The client issued a request (agent, model, storage, or voice) before sending CreateSessionRequest. CreateSession is mandatory and must come first. 2003 SessionAlreadyExists The client sent a second CreateSessionRequest on a connection that already has a session. CreateSession is one-shot. 2004 InvalidLocale CreateSessionRequest.locale is not a well-formed BCP-47 tag. Expected language[-script][-region] — e.g. de, pt-BR, zh-Hans-CN. The error message names what was wrong. 2005 InvalidEngineSet CreateSessionRequest.model_config carries an enum value outside its range (a role, engine, memory placement, or hotword-bias ordinal), or placement_hints names the same model twice. These are the only ways model_config fails: the engine list is advisory, so an empty, incomplete, or wrong list is not an error.

Recovery:

  • ServerShuttingDown — stop sending; close the socket; back off before attempting to reconnect.
  • SessionNotReady — send CreateSessionRequest first, then retry the original request.
  • SessionAlreadyExists — the session is already created; do not call CreateSession again. Reconnect if you need a fresh session with different model_config settings.
  • InvalidLocale — send a well-formed BCP-47 tag, or an empty one to clear the locale.
  • InvalidEngineSet — fix the out-of-range or duplicated model_config entry named in message and re-send CreateSessionRequest.

docs.title: 3xxx — Agent
docs.text:
The request targeted an agent that does not exist, the agent cannot be created because its graph is invalid, or the agent cannot accept the request in its current state. Dialog snapshot, locale-model and voice profile errors are also in this range.

Code Name Meaning 3001 InvalidAgentId The agent_id in the request does not match any agent the server knows about, including an agent that was already destroyed. Typically a client-side bookkeeping bug. 3002 AgentAlreadyDestroyed Defined but not currently returned. A request for a destroyed agent gets 3001. 3003 GraphCompilationFailed CreateAgentRequest carried a graph the server could not compile into an executable plan. The message field names the first validation failure (invalid start node, duplicate node names, missing model name, a malformed grammar on a Generate / GenerateAndSpeak node, etc.). Voice problems are not reported here: see 3023–3025. 3004 AgentBusy SendMessageRequest arrived while the agent's previous turn was still open — either running or paused. A paused turn stays open until it is resumed, cancelled, or times out. Also returned by ChangeAgentParam when a turn is running, by SetAgentVoice when a turn is running or paused, and by KV-cache operations that conflict with a running/paused turn or another cache operation. 3005 UnknownNode ChangeAgentParam named a node that does not exist in the agent's compiled graph. 3006 ParamNotMutable ChangeAgentParam targeted a parameter that cannot be changed at runtime (e.g., structural exit fields are fixed at agent creation). 3007 InvalidParamValue ChangeAgentParam supplied a value that failed the parameter's own validation (e.g., out-of-range sampling temperature, or a malformed GBNF grammar). The message field describes the constraint. 3008 InvalidExitTarget Defined for an exit field that names a node not in the graph, but not currently returned: the server reports that case as 3003 GraphCompilationFailed, with a message naming the source node, the exit, and the missing target. An empty exit field routes to END and is valid. 3009 StorageOutsideRoot A node's string_storage or embedded_string_storage parameter is an absolute path, or a relative path that escapes the process storage root (--storage-root / storage_root / mode default) via .. traversal. Returned by CreateAgentRequest, and by CreateEmbeddedStringStorageRequest for a config_path that escapes the root. 3010 StorageFileNotFound A node's storage path resolves inside the storage root but the file does not exist on disk at agent-creation time. Returned by CreateAgentRequest. CreateStringStorageRequest with a file_path and CreateVoiceInputRequest with a hotwords_storage_path return 3010 for any load failure, including a path outside the root. 3011 StorageKindMismatch A node that requires Map-kind storage (e.g. IntentToInstruction) was given a .txt (List) or Multimap file. Returned by CreateAgentRequest. 3012 AgentNotPaused ResumeAgentRequest arrived while the agent was idle or actively running (not paused). See Pause and resume a turn. 3013 UnknownVariable An UpdateAgentVariablesRequest write targeted a variable name not declared in CreateAgentRequest.variables. (An undeclared name in a template/filter fails earlier as 3003 GraphCompilationFailed.) 3014 VariableTypeMismatch An UpdateAgentVariablesRequest Assign/AddToSet/RemoveFromSet value's type did not match the variable's declared type. 3015 InvalidVariableValue An invalid variable declaration (CreateAgentRequest.variables: bad name grammar, duplicate name, or an over-limit name/string/set), an unknown variable op, a missing or over-limit update value, or a set that would exceed its 4096-element cap. 3016 InvalidToolResults ResumeAgentRequest.tool_results is not a complete, unique batch for the agent's currently paused AwaitResult tool calls: an unknown or already-completed call_id, a batch sent on a non-AwaitResult pause, or a batch exceeding the size limits (64 entries; 128 bytes/call_id; 256 KiB/result; 512 KiB aggregate). The turn stays paused for retry. 3017 ModelLanguageUnsupported Raised when a speaking agent's voice is set (CreateAgent, SetAgentVoice) and its profile has no lang of its own, and at CreateVoiceInput for the STT model, when the model does not support the session language. Fix by picking a model that covers the language, setting the voice profile's own lang, or changing the session locale. Not raised when the model declares no languages at all, or when no node of the agent speaks. 3018 DialogSnapshotInvalid Export/import snapshot is malformed, missing required fields, or has inconsistent tool call/result data. Import leaves the existing dialog unchanged. 3019 DialogFormatUnsupported Snapshot format_version is newer than this server, or the file identifier is not TDLG. 3020 DialogGraphMismatch Import Strict: graph_signature does not match the agent's create-time graph. 3021 DialogSnapshotTooLarge Encoded snapshot would overflow the 1 MiB frame cap. Unity and Unreal also return this locally when the snapshot cannot be framed; the connection stays up. Tryll never truncates. 3022 DialogUnsupportedComponent Unknown component type on export, or unknown union arm on import. 3023 InvalidVoiceProfile The voice profile in CreateAgentRequest or SetAgentVoiceRequest failed validation: an empty or unknown tts_model_name, a model that failed to load, an out-of-range value, a missing clip file, a bad or duplicate delivery-mode name, or a field the model cannot use (for example reference_voice on Supertonic 3, or a non-empty lang on a fixed-language model). The message names the field and, for a delivery mode, the mode. 3024 UnknownDeliveryMode SetAgentDeliveryModeRequest named a mode the agent's voice does not define. neutral is always accepted. The active mode is unchanged. 3025 AgentVoiceRequired CreateAgentRequest has a Speak or GenerateAndSpeak node but no voice. Also returned by SetAgentVoice and SetAgentDeliveryMode for an agent created without a voice.

Recovery:

  • 3001 — recreate the agent with CreateAgentRequest; do not retry the original request against the bad id.
  • 3003 — fix the graph and re-create. The message field points at the first node-level failure.
  • 3004 — the rejected send is an ErrorResponse only; no TurnComplete follows it. If the turn is still running, wait for its TurnComplete before sending again. If the turn is paused, waiting does not help: send ResumeAgentRequest to continue it or CancelRequest to abandon it (a pause with a pause_timeout_ms also ends when the timeout expires). The message says which case applies. The Tryll client libraries re-queue that line and flush it when the busy window closes.
  • 3005 — check the node name spelling; it must match a name declared in the original GraphDescription.
  • 3006 — remove the attempt to set that parameter; structural fields (exit routes, node type) cannot change after agent creation.
  • 3007 — correct the value against the constraints described in message and re-send the ChangeAgentParam request.
  • 3008 — not currently returned. A missing exit target arrives as 3003: fix the exit field on the offending node's params so it names an existing node (or leave it empty for END), then re-create the agent.
  • 3009 — use a relative path that stays within the process storage root; never pass an absolute path or .. components.
  • 3010 — verify the file exists at the path specified, under the process storage root (--storage-root / storage_root / mode default).
  • 3011 — use the correct file type for the node: IntentToInstruction requires a .json Map file, not a .txt list.
  • 3023 — fix the field named in message and re-create the agent, or re-send SetAgentVoice. A failed SetAgentVoice leaves the old voice in place. See Voice Profile.
  • 3024 — use a mode the profile defines, or neutral. The agent keeps speaking in its current mode.
  • 3025 — pass a voice profile when you create the agent. An agent created without one cannot be given a voice later; destroy and re-create it.
  • 3016 — resend ResumeAgentRequest.tool_results with exactly one result per pending call_id (from the tool_call event), within the size limits; the turn is still paused, so retry is safe. See Pause and resume a turn.

docs.title: 4xxx — Inference / workflow
docs.text:
Errors raised while a turn runs, by dedicated KV-cache operations, and by voice-input requests. A turn that fails is reported as 4001 InferenceFailed followed by a TurnComplete with TurnStatus::Error; the agent remains usable and can accept the next turn. The voice-input codes (4100–4107) are ErrorResponses to the voice-input request itself: they do not end a turn and do not affect the agent. 4108 and 4109 are raised by the client's voice input component before any request is sent.

Code Name Meaning 4001 InferenceFailed A Generate or other inference node raised a non-recoverable runtime error (tokenizer failure, backend crash, model unloaded unexpectedly), or TTS synthesis failed (message = "TTS synthesis failed"; the turn still completes). 4002 InferenceTimeout Defined but not currently returned. Nodes have no per-node time budget. 4003 MaxStepsExceeded Defined but not currently returned. When the workflow exceeds the maximum number of node transitions for one turn, the server sends 4001 with the message "Max steps per turn (…) exceeded", then TurnComplete with TurnStatus::Error. Usually indicates an unterminated loop in the graph. 4004 KvCacheOperationFailed Explicit KV-cache prefill, or agent creation with kv_cache_initialization = Prefill, failed while allocating, formatting, or decoding a reusable prefix. 4005 KvCacheManagementUnsupported The selected inference backend does not support the requested KV-cache lifecycle operation. 4100 SttModelLoadFailed A CreateVoiceInputRequest referenced an STT (or VAD) model that could not be loaded — not on disk, or the STT engine failed to initialise it. 4101 AudioFormatUnsupported Audio pushed to an open utterance is not in a format the STT engine accepts (sample rate / channel / encoding). 4102 VoiceInputNotFound A voice-input request targeted a handle that does not exist (never created, or already destroyed). 4103 UtteranceInProgress BeginUtterance was called while an utterance is already open on that handle. 4104 NoActiveUtterance EndUtterance / CancelUtterance / audio push arrived with no utterance open. 4105 UtteranceTimeout Defined but not currently returned. When an open utterance exceeds max_utterance_ms, the server flushes and closes it as if EndUtterance had been sent, without sending an error. 4106 HotwordBiasDisabled The voice input supplied a hotwords lexicon for a model this session turned hotword biasing off on. Refused rather than ignored, so a lexicon never silently does nothing. Either drop the lexicon or set that model's hotword bias to on. 4107 InvalidHotwordsScore hotwords_score was not a finite, non-negative number. It reaches the recognizer's beam search as a per-token bonus, where a NaN or an infinity produces garbled output with nothing in the log — so it is refused rather than clamped. 4108 MicrophoneUnavailable Client-side only; the server never sends it. The voice input component found no usable microphone: none present, the configured device is not connected, or its capture stream would not open. message names the cause; the component's microphone status says the same. 4109 VoiceInputStarting Client-side only; the server never sends it. BeginUtterance did not start because the component is (re)creating its voice input: a microphone appeared after creation was skipped, or (Unreal) the default device's sample rate changed under a live voice input. Not a failure; try again shortly.

Recovery: for 4001 during a turn, the turn ends with the TurnComplete that follows; surface the error to the user or retry the user's message. For 4004 / 4005, the failed request is a dedicated KV-cache operation rather than a turn: keep the agent, inspect the message, and retry only after resolving the underlying resource or backend issue. For 4100–4107, only the voice-input request failed: fix the model, audio format, handle, or hotword settings named in message and retry that request. For 4108, keep text input working and offer voice again later: the next BeginUtterance re-checks the microphone and recreates the voice input once one is present. For 4109, just call BeginUtterance again a moment later.

docs.title: 5xxx — Protocol / framing
docs.text:
Most 5xxx codes mean the server could not make sense of a frame the client sent — a client bug or a version mismatch, with no automated recovery. 5003 FrameTooLarge is also synthesized locally on Unity and Unreal when an outbound payload cannot be framed: that one request fails and the connection stays up, so the caller can retry with a smaller payload. 5004 ProtocolVersionMismatch is raised only by the client.

Code Name Meaning 5001 MalformedMessage The frame could not be decoded against the FlatBuffers schema. 5002 UnknownMessageType The frame's message-type tag is not in the server's known set. 5003 FrameTooLarge A frame would exceed the fixed 1 MiB (1 048 576-byte) payload cap. The server returns it when a response it built cannot be framed. An inbound frame with an out-of-range length is not answered with 5003: the server closes the connection. Unity and Unreal fail an oversized outbound request with this code and keep the connection; only a socket I/O error drops the session. 5004 ProtocolVersionMismatch Client-side only; the server never sends it. The client compared ConnectionReady.protocol_version with its own version, found they differ, and failed the connection. Upgrade the client or server so both speak the same version. 5005 DebugCommandsUnavailable A DebugCommandRequest arrived but the debug-command channel is not compiled into this build (Production) or is disabled in config. 5006 UnknownDebugCommand A DebugCommandRequest.command is not a recognised verb.

Recovery: for a local outbound 5003, shrink the request and retry; the session is still usable. For the other 5xxx codes — log, escalate, and investigate. See the wire protocol reference for the framing contract.

docs.title: 6xxx — Model download
docs.text:
The server was unable to download a model. All 6xxx codes are user-actionable: fix the underlying condition (network, disk, catalog) and retry.

Code Name Meaning 6001 DownloadFailed The download transport failed (HTTP error, interrupted transfer, checksum mismatch). 6002 DownloadNotAvailable The named model has no HuggingFace repo/files configured, so there is nothing to download (e.g. a local_path-only entry). 6003 InsufficientDiskSpace The target download directory lacks free space for the model. 6004 DownloadAlreadyActive A download for this model is already in progress on the server. 6005 ModelResolutionFailed The named model is not in the catalog, or the engine it needs is not registered. Also returned by LoadModel/CreateAgent when a referenced model cannot be resolved (e.g. LoadModel for a VAD-only catalog entry). 6007 ModelPlacementUnavailable Reserved; not currently returned. Placement requests are hints and do not fail: the server downgrades a placement it cannot satisfy and reports the resolved placement instead. 6008 EngineNotAvailable A referenced model needs an engine that is not registered in this server build. 6009 ModelManagementDisabled This deployment mode does not download or delete models (Client Prod / Standalone). Ship every model with the game.

Note

6006 (ModelAutoDownloadFailed) is retired along with the removed auto-model-downloading feature and will not be reused. A missing model referenced by CreateAgent / CreateEmbeddedStringStorage / CreateVoiceInput now surfaces as GraphCompilationFailed (3003), ModelResolutionFailed (6005), or SttModelLoadFailed (4100) instead. A missing TTS model named by the agent's voice surfaces as InvalidVoiceProfile (3023).

Recovery:

  • 6001 — retry after checking connectivity.
  • 6002 — ask the server admin to add a matching variant to the catalog (see Use Your Own Local Model), or request a different model.
  • 6003 — free disk space or reconfigure models_root.
  • 6004 — wait for the in-flight download's completion frame instead of re-issuing.
  • 6009 — do not call DownloadModel / DeleteModel in Client Prod; stage Production models at build time.

docs.title: 7xxx — String storage
docs.text:
Errors raised by CreateStringStorageRequest and by the session storage manager at registration time. The session is unchanged on failure; the storage is not created.

Code Name Meaning 7001 InvalidStringStorageName The storage name is empty, malformed, or reserved. 7002 StringStorageAlreadyExists A storage with this name is already registered for the session. 7003 InvalidStringStorageData The content was rejected: unreadable file, bad format, empty array. 7004 StorageNameInUse The virtual name passed to an inline (strings-based) CreateStringStorageRequest or CreateEmbeddedStringStorageRequest resolves to an existing real file under the storage root. The name is rejected to prevent the virtual entry from silently shadowing the file. Use a name that does not match any filename under the process storage root.

Recovery: fix the name or content and re-send the request. For 7004, choose a virtual name that does not correspond to any file under the process storage root. See the string storage reference.

docs.title: 8xxx — Embedded string storage
docs.text:
Errors raised by CreateEmbeddedStringStorageRequest. The session is unchanged on failure; the storage is not created.

Code Name Meaning 8001 InvalidEmbeddedStorageName The storage name is empty, malformed, or reserved. 8002 EmbeddedStorageAlreadyExists A storage with this name is already registered for the session. 8003 EmbeddedStorageBuildFailed The index could not be built: missing *.kb.json, missing or corrupt *.usearch, empty inline array, or an embedding model that is not in the catalog / not on disk. 8101 StorageBusy Export/import/save/load refused because an agent is not strictly idle (running, paused, or in a KV-cache operation). 8102 SchemaMismatch The named store already exists under a different schema. 8103 MaxRecordsExceeded An insert was rejected because the schema max_records cap is reached. 8104 UnknownSchema The schema name is not in schemas.json, or the schema file failed to load. 8105 MutableKbSnapshotInvalid The TMKB buffer failed verification, is missing required fields, or has an unsupported format_version. 8106 StorageSnapshotTooLarge The encoded snapshot exceeds MaxMutableKbSnapshotBytes (wire) or MaxGameMemorySnapshotBytes (file). 8107 InvalidEmbedTiming LoadGameMemory used Unspecified; callers must pass Now or Lazy. 8108 UnknownMutableKb The named store does not exist (read/write/export without EnsureMutableKb). 8109 SavesDisabled SaveGameMemory / SaveDialog refused because saves.enabled is false (config or --disable-saves). Load* still work.

Recovery: fix the config, schema, or snapshot and re-send the request. See the embedded string storage reference and Save and load agent state.

docs.title: Client-side handling
docs.text:
Every Tryll client library delivers these codes through its error channel:

  • C++ — Tryll::Client::ErrorCode plus an std::string message on the on_error callback.
  • Python — raised as tryll_client.TryllError with .code and .message attributes, or delivered to the async callback.
  • Unity — TryllError value struct with Code (int) and Message (string) fields; IsOk is true when Code == 0. All …Async methods return Task<(T result, TryllError error)>; callers must check error.IsOk before using the result.
  • Unreal — FTryllError USTRUCT with Code and Message properties; the ETryllErrorCode UENUM matches this table.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Canonical definitions for every term used across the Tryll documentation. Every page links the first mention of a term below to its anchor on this page. Subsequent mentions render as plain text.

Terms are grouped by topic so related concepts sit next to each other.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text: A server-side object that owns one conversation: its dialog, its compiled workflow, its retained knowledge, and a handle to the models it needs. Each agent belongs to exactly one session and is referenced by a numeric agent_id. Created via CreateAgentRequest, retired via DestroyAgentRequest.

docs.title: Session
docs.text: A single configured connection between a client and the Tryll server. The client opens a TCP socket, sends a CreateSessionRequest, and receives a session_id. All subsequent requests from that socket are scoped to the session; closing the socket ends the session and destroys every agent it owns.

docs.title: Turn
docs.text: One request–response cycle initiated by a user message. A turn begins when the client sends SendMessageRequest and ends when the server emits TurnComplete. Between those two frames the client may receive zero or more AnswerText chunks (see streaming). Only one turn is in flight per agent at a time.

docs.title: Dialog
docs.text: The ordered list of interactions belonging to an agent — the conversation as the server sees it. Each turn appends exactly one interaction. Used by the projection stage to build the next prompt.

docs.title: Interaction
docs.text: A single user-and-assistant exchange within a dialog. Holds the user message, the assistant response, any retrieved knowledge components, and (when diagnostics are on) per-node debug information.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: The overall per-turn behaviour of an agent — what happens between receiving the user message and emitting TurnComplete. A workflow is defined by a graph of nodes and is compiled from a GraphDescription when the agent is created.

docs.title: Graph
docs.text: A declarative description of a workflow: a list of nodes, where each node's typed params carry both its configuration and its exit wiring, plus a start node name. Built client-side with the graph builder APIs, validated server-side at agent creation. Compilation failures surface as error 3003 (see error codes).

docs.title: Node
docs.text: A single unit of computation within a graph. Each node has a typed parameter struct containing both its configuration and one or more named exit fields, and well-defined side effects on the dialog. See Workflow Nodes for the full, current catalog of built-in node types.

docs.title: Exit route
docs.text: A named output of a node. Each exit is encoded as a typed string field on the node's params object using the naming convention <exit_name>_exit (e.g. triggered_exit, not_triggered_exit). An empty string routes the turn to end-of-turn; any non-empty value names the next node to execute. For example, RegexGuardrailNode has triggered and not_triggered exits; ToolCallNode has tool_called and no_tool_called.

docs.title: Projection
docs.text: The stage that turns the dialog plus retained state into a prompt for a language model. For Generate nodes, projection also renders the node's Mustache template against the current turn's instruction slots and knowledge components, then splices the result into the prompt at the configured placement. A token budget with hysteresis ensures the prompt fits inside the model's context window. When a rolling summary is present, history replay starts after the newest fold. See the projection concept page.

docs.title: Rolling summary
docs.text: The compressed record of interactions a Summarize node has folded. Projection appends the newest summary to the system message and replays the dialog only after covered_through. Older summaries stay in the dialog as history and are not rendered. The summary is part of an exported dialog snapshot.

docs.title: Fold
docs.text: One summarizer pass. It rewrites the rolling summary from the previous summary plus the interactions that have aged out of the hot window (keep_recent_turns). A fold that does not fit the summarizer's own context covers the largest chronological prefix that does, and leaves the rest for a later fold.

docs.title: Mustache template
docs.text: A Mustache source string attached to a Generate node via the template param. Before each model call, projection renders it against a context that includes {{user_message}}, the {{#instructions}} list from instruction slots, and the {{#knowledge}} list from knowledge components. The rendered text is spliced into the prompt at the position specified by the placement param. See the Use Mustache Templates how-to.

docs.title: Classify Intent node
docs.text: A node type that maps a user message to a discrete intent label by top-1 vector similarity search over a small, labelled embedded string storage. On a match it attaches an intention component to the current interaction for a downstream Intent to Instruction node to consume; it generates no text and renders nothing into the prompt. See the Classify Intent reference.

docs.title: Intent to Instruction node
docs.text: A node type that looks up the intent label written by a preceding Classify Intent node in a Map-kind string storage and attaches the matching value as an instruction slot to the current interaction. The downstream Generate node then renders it via its Mustache template. It always takes the default exit. See the Intent to Instruction reference.

docs.title: RAG
docs.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation. An approach that injects topically relevant text snippets into the prompt so the language model can ground its answer on content the model itself does not "know". In Tryll, RAG is implemented by a Retrieve node in front of a Generate node.

docs.title: Retrieval
docs.text: The act of selecting the snippets from a knowledge source that best match the current query. Dense retrieval (the default) ranks by cosine distance to the query embedding; lexical retrieval ranks by BM25 keyword score; hybrid runs both and fuses the rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Produces knowledge components that the workflow may or may not present to the model.

docs.title: Retrieve node
docs.text: A node type that searches an embedded string storage (dense, lexical, or hybrid retrieval) and attaches the top-k matches to the current interaction as knowledge components. See the Retrieve reference.

docs.title: Knowledge base
docs.text: Synonym for "vector index used by a Retrieve node". In Tryll, a knowledge base is realised as an embedded string storage.

docs.title: Instruction slot
docs.text: A named instruction string attached to the current interaction as a kind=Instruction slot by an Instruction node (or Intent to Instruction). Projection exposes instruction slots to the downstream Generate node's Mustache template as: {{slot.<name>}} (direct lookup) and entries in the {{#instructions}} list (each with {{name}} and {{text}}).

docs.title: Knowledge component
docs.text: A single piece of retrieved or attached text plus metadata (source, score, chunk id). Multiple components may attach to one interaction. Projection exposes them to the Generate node's Mustache template as the {{#knowledge}} list and {{#knowledge_<source>}} direct-lookup sections.

docs.title: Chunk
docs.text: A bounded slice of source text that has been offline-embedded and stored in an embedded string storage. Chunking happens at index build time, not at query time; each retrieval result is one chunk.

docs.title: Embedding
docs.text: A dense floating-point vector that represents the semantic content of a piece of text. Produced by an embedding model; compared via cosine distance inside an HNSW index.

docs.title: Embedding model
docs.text: A model whose output is an embedding rather than generated text. Declared in the model catalog with "model_type": "embedding". Referenced by name from RetrieveNode parameters or from an embedded string storage config file.

docs.title: HNSW
docs.text: Hierarchical Navigable Small World — the approximate-nearest-neighbour index structure used by Tryll's embedded string storage. Optimised for fast cosine-distance search over large vector sets.

docs.title: String storage
docs.text: A named, session-owned container of plain strings. Created via CreateStringStorageRequest (inline array or file path). Consumed by canned-response and regex-guardrail nodes, which pick or match one string per invocation. Not embedded, not indexed. See the string storage reference.

docs.title: Embedded string storage
docs.text: A session-owned vector index built from strings plus a precomputed HNSW file. Two construction paths: a directory containing a *.kb.json config plus a *.usearch file (Path A), or an inline array of strings that the server embeds on demand (Path B). Consumed by Retrieve nodes. See the embedded string storage reference.

docs.title: Canned response
docs.text: A fixed reply selected from a string storage. The canned-response node emits one string from its backing storage (RoundRobin by default, or Random or First) and terminates the turn without invoking a language model. Useful for scripted answers and fallback paths.

docs.title: Guardrail
docs.text: A pattern-matching check that gates workflow flow. The regex-guardrail node runs an input slot (default user_message) against a string storage of patterns and routes the turn to triggered or not_triggered accordingly. Common use: short-circuit unsafe or off-topic inputs to a canned response.

docs.title: Language model
docs.text: A model that takes a text prompt and emits generated text token-by-token. In the Tryll catalog, language models omit the model_type field entirely — language is the implicit default. See the models concept page.

docs.title: SLM
docs.text: Small Language Model — a language model small enough to run on consumer hardware (CPU, integrated GPU, or a single consumer GPU). Tryll is designed around SLMs: on-device inference, no cloud round-trip, and aggressive KV-cache management.

docs.title: Inference engine
docs.text: The backend runtime that executes a model. Each model catalog entry names its engine, and every variant of that entry shares it. The session does not choose an engine: CreateSessionRequest.model_config may carry optional (role, engine) hints, which only let the server initialise those engines early. The default build runs llama.cpp (LlamaCpp), Sherpa-ONNX (SherpaOnnx, for STT and TTS), and ONNX Runtime (OnnxRuntime). OnnxGenAI, WindowsML, OpenVino, and TensorRtLlm are InferenceEngine enum slots reserved for future engines.

docs.title: GGUF
docs.text: The binary file format used by llama.cpp for quantised language models. Tryll downloads GGUF files from HuggingFace for catalog entries whose inference engine is llama.cpp.

docs.title: LoRA adapter
docs.text: A small GGUF file, fine-tuned for one base language model, that changes how that model behaves for a narrow job. An LLM node runs its model with up to 8 adapters, each with a scale (1 = as trained, 0 = off), listed in the node's adaptation table. Fixed when the agent is created. See Use a LoRA Adapter.

docs.title: Model catalog
docs.text: The server's models.json file — the authoritative list of models Tryll can download, load, and run. Each catalog entry declares a name, a purpose (model_type: language — the default when the field is omitted — embedding, stt, tts, or vad), default sampling parameters, and one or more variants. See the model management reference.

docs.title: Model variant
docs.text: One concrete packaging of a catalogued model, such as one GGUF quantisation. All variants of one catalog entry share a single inference engine, and loading the model uses that engine. LoadModelRequest takes a model name and an optional memory placement hint; it does not select an engine or a variant.

docs.title: Variant
docs.text: Short form of model variant.

docs.title: Pinned retention
docs.text: A model-loading policy that keeps a language / embedding / STT / TTS model resident in memory until an explicit UnloadModelRequest (and no live users remain). Suitable for the hot model(s) on a given machine. Opposite of OnDemand retention. VAD catalog entries are not pin/unloadable.

docs.title: OnDemand retention
docs.text: A model-loading policy that loads a language / embedding / STT / TTS model when an agent (or voice input / TTS / embedding use) needs it and unloads it when unused — after DestroyAgent, or when the next validated model load sweeps idle OnDemand entries across all four caches. Trades memory for latency. Opposite of Pinned retention.

docs.title: Context (KV)
docs.text: The KV cache — the per-model tensor of cached attention keys and values for every token the model has processed this turn. Tryll reuses as much KV state as possible across turns when the prompt prefix is stable; this is what makes conversational inference fast.

docs.title: TTS
docs.text: Text-to-speech — turning text into spoken audio. The Generate and Speak node voices generated tokens sentence by sentence as they stream; the Speak node voices a slot's text. Both speak with the agent's voice profile; neither node has voice settings of its own.

docs.title: Voice profile
docs.text: An agent's one voice (VoiceProfile): the TTS model from the model catalog (tts_model_name, required), the base identity (speaker_id, a reference clip, or a voice description), speed, language, emit_visemes, and named delivery modes. Passed at CreateAgent and replaced with SetAgentVoice. Every speaking node of the agent uses it, so one workflow can serve many characters. See Voice Profile.

docs.title: Delivery mode
docs.text: A named way of speaking that a voice profile defines, such as angry or whisper. Game code switches it with SetAgentDeliveryMode, which applies from the next sentence. neutral is built in and means the plain voice. What a mode can change depends on the TTS model: a different reference clip, a Maya1 delivery clause, the Chatterbox exaggeration, or only speed. See Voice Profile and Add Emotions to a Voice.

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text: The concatenated input passed to the language model at generation time: system preamble, projected dialog, attached knowledge, tool descriptions, and the current user message. Produced by projection.

docs.title: Token
docs.text: The atomic unit the language model reads and emits. Each model has its own tokenizer; token counts for the same text differ between models. Token budgets in projection are measured in tokens of the active model.

docs.title: Token budget
docs.text: The number of tokens a language-model node's projected prompt may use: that node's context size minus the headroom reserved for the generated response. Each node trims its own prompt; there is no per-agent setting. Exceeding the budget triggers dialog truncation with hysteresis.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text: The mode in which the server emits generated text in chunks rather than waiting for the full response. Each chunk arrives as an AnswerText frame carrying only the new text (is_delta = true). The last chunk from each node carries is_final = true; for streamed output it is an empty terminator. TurnComplete follows once the turn ends. See how to stream answers to a UI.

docs.title: Tool call
docs.text: A structured instruction emitted by a language model indicating it wants to invoke a named external function. In Tryll, tool calls are detected only — the server parses them from model output and returns them to the client, which is responsible for execution. See the tool calling concept page.

docs.title: Tool-call format
docs.text: The specific textual convention the language model uses to express a tool call. Tryll follows the model's own chat template for both prompting and parsing, so there is nothing to choose. The tool_call_format field on the tool-call node is deprecated and ignored by the server.

docs.title: Constrained decoding
docs.text: Forcing a language model's output to match a formal grammar at every decode step: tokens that could not legally continue the output are masked out before sampling, so malformed output is impossible (not merely discouraged). Also called grammar-constrained generation. In Tryll it is exposed via the grammar param on Generate and Generate and Speak nodes. It guarantees the output's shape, never its meaning — a constrained model can still emit a valid-but-wrong answer. See the constrained output concept page.

docs.title: GBNF
docs.text: GGML BNF — the grammar notation used by llama.cpp (and therefore by Tryll's grammar param) to describe constrained output. A grammar is a set of name ::= … rules over string literals, alternation (|), and sequences; it must define a rule named root and must not be left-recursive. See the upstream GBNF guide for the full syntax.

docs.title: Wire protocol
docs.text: The byte-level contract between the Tryll client and server: TCP transport, 4-byte little-endian length prefix, FlatBuffers payload, 1 MiB max frame. See the wire protocol reference.

docs.title: Chat Window
docs.text: An editor-only window (Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Chat in Unity, Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Tryll Chat in Unreal) that creates its own agent from a scene component and lets you converse with it without entering Play mode. Hosts the turn inspector in a side pane. See Test an agent in the editor.

docs.title: Dialog Lab
docs.text: An editor-only window that runs one scripted dialog across parameter variants and seeds, then shows every result side by side so the spread is visible. Makes no quality claim — it shows raw output, deterministic checks, and timings. Ships in both editors. See Compare dialog variants.

docs.title: Agent Log
docs.text: An editor-only window that records what this editor process sent to and received from each agent — turns, voice transcripts the client sent, deferred variable flushes, and lifecycle events — as a per-agent narrative rather than an event dump. Scoped to one client connection, not the whole server. See Use the Agent Log.

docs.title: Turn inspector
docs.text: The shared panel that explains a single turn: which nodes ran and via which exit routes, per-node timing, the node parameters used, the rendered prompt and output, retrieval hits, and tool calls. One implementation, hosted by the Chat Window, Agent Log, and Dialog Lab. See the turn inspector reference.

docs.title: Turn diagnostics
docs.text: The per-turn debug_info payload the server attaches when an agent was created with enable_diagnostics. It is the data the turn inspector renders. The flag is structural — it cannot be enabled on an agent that already exists.

docs.title: Server monitor
docs.text:
A contributor-facing browser UI served by a dev-time HTTP/SSE sidecar in the server process. Sees every session on the server, which is its advantage over the Agent Log; it cannot see what a client sent, which is the Agent Log's. Compiled out of Production builds.

See also:

  • Concept map — narrative explanations of the terms above.
  • Error codes — numeric error catalog used across all responses.

docs.title: Model Management
docs.text:
The Tryll server treats models as first-class, named resources. Every model it can load is declared in a single catalog file, models.json, that the server reads at startup. Clients discover, download, load, and unload models over the wire protocol; the server handles all disk I/O, HuggingFace downloads, and backend-specific loading.

This page is the reference for:

  • The models.json schema that tells the server what exists and how to find it.
  • The model lifecycle wire-protocol flow: ListModels → DownloadModel → LoadModel / UnloadModel.
  • The status enum reported per-model.
  • The retention modes that control memory occupancy.

Server-wide model settings (download directory, catalog path) live in server-config.json.

Models must be acquired explicitly

CreateAgent, CreateEmbeddedStringStorage, and CreateVoiceInput fail fast if a referenced model is not already on disk — the server does not download it for you. Run ListModels → DownloadModel yourself, or acquire the model from the editor Model Manager, before referencing it.

docs.title: models.json and user catalogs
docs.text:
Default base catalog: data/models.json, configurable via models_catalog_path in server-config.json. This file is shipped by Tryll — do not edit it; package updates overwrite it. A missing, unreadable, or invalid base catalog is fatal: the process does not listen.

Plugin projects point at their own catalog from Project Settings (Unity: Tryll Client → Custom Models; Unreal: Plugins → Tryll Client → Models). Any file name, any path inside the project. Empty means no extra file. The plugin passes that file as --user-models-path. Set it before the server's first launch, or call the setter while a server is running to restart it (the open session is dropped). A packaged game copies the saved file to Server/data/user-catalog/ and copies relative chat_template_file values beside that copy. The editor uses the project file, so those relative paths resolve in place.

Running the server yourself, pass --user-models-path or set user_models_catalog_path. The default path is a sibling user_models.json of the base catalog. That file is not shipped; a missing file is silent. A broken user file is skipped and the server still starts; duplicate model names or shared-asset ids against the shipped catalog skip only that entry (the shipped entry wins). Extra models.d/*.json files are loaded the same way when that directory exists. The install does not create it. Validate with tryll_server --check-catalogs.

docs.title: Top-level structure
docs.text:
{
    "shared_model_assets": [
        { ... }
    ],
    "models": [
        { ... },
        { ... }
    ]
}

shared_model_assets is optional. Each asset is a file set several models share, such as the SNAC decoder: id, huggingface_repo, and files, each with path, size_bytes and a 64-hex-digit sha256. A model names an asset from its dependencies; every such id must resolve.

docs.title: Model descriptor fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes Human-readable model name. This is the identifier used everywhere on the wire: CreateAgentRequest.default_model_name, DownloadModelRequest.model_name, LoadModelRequest.model_name. Must be unique within the catalog. model_type string No "embedding", "stt", "tts", or "vad". Omit for language models — language is the implicit default. audience string No Informational visibility hint surfaced to editor clients via ListModels ("public", "experimental", "internal"). Not consumed by the server. hidden bool No When true, the entry is omitted from ListModels. default_sampling object No Default sampling params for this model. Sampling params set on a node take precedence. Absent fields fall back to built-in defaults listed below. Ignored for non-language models. variants array Yes One entry per file set. Every variant of one model must use the same inference engine — the catalog is rejected otherwise.

docs.title: default_sampling fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description temperature float 0.7 Sampling temperature; higher = more random. top_p float 1.0 Nucleus sampling threshold. 1.0 disables. top_k int 0 Top-K sampling cut-off. 0 disables. min_p float 0.05 Min-P filter. 0.0 disables. repeat_penalty float 1.0 Penalty for repeating tokens. 1.0 disables. presence_penalty float 0.0 OpenAI-style presence penalty. 0.0 disables. frequency_penalty float 0.0 OpenAI-style frequency penalty. 0.0 disables. max_tokens int 758 Maximum generated tokens per turn. seed uint32 0 RNG seed. 0 selects a random seed per turn.

docs.title: variants entry fields
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description engine string Yes Which inference engine runs this model. Implemented engines: "llama-cpp" (language, embedding, and SNAC TTS), "sherpa-onnx" (STT / TTS / VAD) and "onnx-runtime" (Chatterbox TTS, internal). The server takes a model's engine from here, never from the session. local_path string No Path to a directory containing the model file(s). Combined with files[0]. Takes priority over path and downloads.json. Dev only: must resolve inside the process storage root. Outside paths are ignored with a warning. path string No Legacy relative path under models_root. Fallback when neither local_path nor a downloads.json entry resolves. huggingface_repo string No HuggingFace repository slug ("owner/repo"). Required for downloads. Empty means the model cannot be downloaded over the wire — it must already be on disk via local_path. files array of string No Filenames for this variant. For HuggingFace, these are downloaded from huggingface_repo; for local, resolved relative to local_path. Empty disables both download and resolution. context_size int No Override the engine's default context window (in tokens). 0 or absent uses the engine default — currently 8192 for llama.cpp. kv_cache_type string No llama.cpp KV-cache dtype: "f16", "q8_0", or "q4_0". Default "q8_0" (≈half the KV VRAM vs F16). Ignored by other engines. chat_template_file string No llama.cpp only. Path to a Jinja chat-template file that replaces the GGUF's own embedded template. Relative paths resolve against the directory of the catalog file that declares them. A packaged Unity or Unreal build copies those relative files next to the staged user catalog. Use this when a model's own GGUF conversion ships a template that doesn't render tool definitions — see Tool Calling — even though the model itself may support tool calling. tool_call_support string Yes (language models) Advisory capability declaration: "supported" or "unsupported". Required on every language-model variant (the server rejects the catalog otherwise) and not allowed on other model types. Shown in the Unity/Unreal Model Manager detail pane and returned by ListModels, so you can pick a tool-capable model before downloading it. Advisory only: whether a ToolCall node accepts the model is still decided at agent creation from the model's own chat template. disable_thinking bool No llama.cpp only. Suppresses chain-of-thought by toggling the template's enable_thinking. use_jinja bool No llama.cpp only. false reverts to the legacy C-API chat-template path instead of the Jinja engine. reasoning_budget int No llama.cpp only. Hard cap on thinking tokens.

STT / TTS variant fields:

Field Type Required Description stt_family string STT STT model family (e.g. "whisper"). stt_recognizer string No Recognizer sub-type when a family has more than one. tts_family string TTS TTS family. Sherpa-ONNX: "supertonic" or "pocket" — every other Sherpa family (VITS/Piper, Kokoro, Kitten, Matcha, ZipVoice) fails to load. llama.cpp SNAC: "orpheus" or "maya1". ONNX Runtime: "chatterbox". See TTS Models. tts_files object TTS Named file map for the TTS bundle (e.g. duration_predictor, text_encoder, vocoder, voice_style, or gguf for SNAC) rather than the flat files array. tts_lang string No Default synthesis language for a multilingual TTS model (e.g. "en"). dependencies object No Role → shared-asset id. SNAC entries declare "snac_decoder": "snac-24khz-decoder". tts_capabilities object No Advertised controls: booleans voice_description, delivery_instruction, reference_voice, speed, language_per_call, expressiveness (Chatterbox exaggeration); num_speakers (int, 0 = not advertised); plus voice_presets and inline_tags (each tag's verification is verified or declared). TTS models only. Editors use it to show only the voice profile fields a model accepts, and the server uses it to check the voice of an agent that never speaks (no model loaded). For a speaking agent the loaded engine is authoritative. Every shipped TTS entry declares it. languages array of string No Language codes the model supports: lowercase, 2–3 letters, no duplicates. Not allowed on language models. Drives the session-locale check (3017) and ModelInfo.languages. num_threads int No Thread count for the sherpa-onnx, SNAC or Chatterbox session.

Memory placement is not a catalog field (an unknown key such as memory_placement is ignored). Set it per session with CreateSession's placement_hints, per load with LoadModelRequest.placement, or with the Model Manager's Placement control.

Per-agent voice settings (speaker_id, speed, lang, reference_voice, voice_description, delivery modes) are fields of the agent's voice profile, and the chunking knobs (min_sentence_chars, first_chunk_max_chars) are node params. Neither is a catalog field — see Add Voice Output to an Agent.

docs.title: Minimal example — user-provided model
docs.text:
{
    "models": [
        {
            "name": "My Local Model",
            "variants": [
                {
                    "engine":            "llama-cpp",
                    "local_path":        "models/my-local-gguf",
                    "files":             ["my-model.gguf"],
                    "tool_call_support": "unsupported"
                }
            ]
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: Downloadable example — HuggingFace + tuned sampling
docs.text:
{
    "models": [
        {
            "name": "Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)",
            "default_sampling": {
                "temperature":    0.6,
                "top_p":          0.9,
                "top_k":          50,
                "min_p":          0.05,
                "repeat_penalty": 1.2
            },
            "variants": [
                {
                    "engine":            "llama-cpp",
                    "huggingface_repo":  "bartowski/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF",
                    "files":             ["Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf"],
                    "tool_call_support": "supported"
                }
            ]
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: Embedding models
docs.text: Models with "model_type": "embedding" are declared the same way and referenced by name from embedded string storages and from Retrieve node params. Their sampling fields are ignored; only the file resolution and engine fields matter.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
The wire-protocol flow for putting a model under a running agent:

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: ListModelsRequest
    S-->>C: ListModelsResponse([ModelInfo])
    alt status == Absent
        C->>S: DownloadModelRequest(name)
        S-->>C: DownloadProgress × N
        S-->>C: DownloadComplete(success=true)
    end
    C->>S: LoadModelRequest(name)
    S-->>C: LoadModelResponse
    C->>S: CreateAgentRequest(default_model_name=name, ...)
    S-->>C: CreateAgentResponse(agent_id)
    note over C,S: Agent runs turns...
    C->>S: UnloadModelRequest(name)
    S-->>C: Ack

Key rules:

  • You do not have to call LoadModelRequest explicitly. An agent whose graph references a not-yet-loaded language / embedding / STT / TTS model triggers on-demand load at CreateAgent (or voice-input / storage creation) time.
  • LoadModelRequest pins the model for any of the four managed kinds. The server keeps it resident until UnloadModelRequest, regardless of agent count. Pinning is process-global.
  • UnloadModelRequest on a shared model is polite. If any agent still uses the model, it stays resident; it is freed when the last user goes away.
  • VAD is not pin/unloadable. Catalog vad entries are download / config metadata; offline STT loads them as a dependency. Sending LoadModelRequest for a VAD model returns ModelResolutionFailed.
  • Unused OnDemand models are swept before the next load. When the server is about to load a new model into any of the four caches, it first frees idle OnDemand entries across all caches (pinned models and models still held by agents are left alone).
  • DeleteModelRequest removes the downloaded files from disk. It reverses a download (back to Absent); it does not touch user-supplied local_path models.

See How to pin and unpin models for the end-to-end walkthrough.

docs.title: ModelInfo fields
docs.text:
ListModelsResponse carries one ModelInfo per catalog entry, enriched with the metadata editors and clients need:

Field Description name Catalog name — the identifier used everywhere on the wire. status Where the model is now (see Model status). huggingface_repo Download source slug, or empty if not downloadable. size_bytes On-disk size when present. model_type "language" | "embedding" | "stt" | "tts" | "vad". engine "llama-cpp" | "sherpa-onnx" | "onnx-runtime". audience "public" | "experimental" | "internal" | "" — server-side visibility hint. tool_call_support Advisory tool-calling capability from the catalog: "supported" | "unsupported"; empty for non-language models. context_size Context window in tokens; 0 = engine default. files Resolved variant filenames. local_path On-disk directory, or empty when not on disk. default_sampling The catalog's recommended sampling params, if any. languages Catalog-declared language codes; empty means undeclared, not "none". dependencies Shared assets the model needs: id, role, status, size_bytes, folder, local_path, failure_reason. tts_capabilities TTS models only: the catalog's advertised controls, voice presets and inline tags.

docs.title: Model status
docs.text:
The ModelInfo.status field in ListModelsResponse reports where a model is right now:

Value Int Meaning Absent 0 Known in catalog but not on disk and not downloading. Local 1 User-provided path resolved (local_path); on disk; can be loaded. Downloading 2 Transfer in progress. DownloadProgress frames are flowing. Loaded 3 Currently resident in memory for its model kind (language, STT, TTS, or embedding). Downloaded 4 On disk from a HuggingFace download; can be loaded. Incomplete 5 Catalog parent is present but a shared-asset dependency is missing or still downloading.

Ordinals match the ModelStatus enum on the wire protocol and ETryllModelStatus in the Unreal client.

Loaded is per model kind

Loaded means the model is resident in the server's in-memory cache for its specific kind. A language model and an STT model are tracked independently — a voice-input session that pins an STT model will show it as Loaded whatever other models are loaded. ListModels reports every catalog model with its own engine and status, whatever engines the session hinted at.

docs.title: Retention modes
docs.text:
Tryll decides what to keep in memory based on a simple rule. The same two modes apply to language, embedding, STT, and TTS (each kind has its own cache; sweeps are cross-cache):

Retention How it is triggered When the model is freed Pinned LoadModelRequest On UnloadModelRequest (delayed until no agent uses it). OnDemand Implicit: an agent's graph (or voice input / TTS / embedding use) references the model, no prior LoadModelRequest When the last user is destroyed or when the next validated model load sweeps unused OnDemand entries.

Use Pinned for the hot model(s) on the machine — the latency cost of the first load is paid once at startup. Use OnDemand for secondary models where memory matters more than first-turn latency.

These labels match the client-facing names used in the glossary (pinned retention, on-demand retention).

See Lifetime and Ownership → Models for the reference-counting story that connects Pinned / OnDemand to what nodes inside an agent actually hold.

docs.title: Editor window
docs.text: Both plugins ship an editor-only Model Manager that drives the lifecycle above through a GUI — browse the catalog, download / load / unload / delete, and tag models for your build. Open it from Window → Tryll → Model Manager (Unity) or Window → Tryll → Tryll Model Manager (Unreal). The task walkthrough is Manage Models in the Editor; this section is the reference for the two pieces of editor state it adds.

docs.title: Build registration
docs.text:
Each model can be tagged with a registration tier that decides whether it ships in a packaged build:

Tier Int Meaning None / Not registered 0 Not part of the build. Experimental 1 Available in the editor; stripped from packaged builds. Production 2 Shipped in the packaged build.

The registration is project-side, not server-side:

  • Unity: a TryllModelManifest ScriptableObject at Assets/Resources/TryllModelManifest.asset (it must sit directly in a Resources folder so player builds can load it).
  • Unreal: the Tryll Model Manifest developer settings, persisted to DefaultGame.ini.

docs.title: Registered-model pickers — (tryll_model)
docs.text:
Model-name fields on nodes and components render as a dropdown of registered models of the matching kind rather than a free-text box. This is driven by the (tryll_model: "...") schema attribute on the field; the editor resolves it against the manifest above:

Field Kind Generate / ToolCall / ClassifyIntentLLM / GenerateAndSpeak model_name language Voice profile tts_model_name tts Voice Input component STT model stt

Unity emits a [TryllModelType("...")] drawer; Unreal swaps the field to FTryllModelName with meta=(TryllModelType="..."). A value that is set but unregistered still displays (never silently dropped), but only Production-tagged models ship in a build. The wire still carries the model name as a plain string — the picker is editor sugar.

docs.title: Download record — downloads.json
docs.text:
The server maintains a downloads.json file inside models_root — its download ledger — to track completed HuggingFace downloads. This file is server-managed; do not edit it by hand. Its contents feed ModelInfo.status == Downloaded at startup so that a previously downloaded model can be loaded without re-downloading. Shared model assets (for example the SNAC decoder) live in a sibling assets array with their own records. The server stores a per-file SHA-256 on each asset (file_sha256) when the download finishes. Listing compares that digest to the catalog pin; the file is re-hashed when a model actually loads the asset. Deleting a parent model does not delete a shared asset. A parent whose asset is still missing, the wrong size, or pinned to a different digest reports Incomplete. Release staging copies each reachable asset once.

Structure (for reference only):

{
    "entries": [
        {
            "name":        "Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)",
            "engine":      "llama-cpp",
            "folder":      "bartowski--Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GGUF",
            "files":       ["Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf"],
            "total_bytes": 2019377152
        }
    ]
}

engine is stored as the same engine name the catalog uses ("llama-cpp", "sherpa-onnx", "onnx-runtime"), not as the InferenceEngine ordinal the wire protocol carries.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Code Cause 6001 Download failed (HTTP, interrupted, checksum). 6002 DownloadNotAvailable — the model has no huggingface_repo/files configured, so there is nothing to download (e.g. a local_path-only entry). 6003 Disk full in the download directory. 6004 A download for this model is already active. 6005 ModelResolutionFailed — the model is not in the catalog, or it failed to load. Also returned by LoadModel for a VAD-only entry. 6008 EngineNotAvailable — the model's catalog engine is not included in this server build.
