docs.text:
Package: com.tryll.client Namespace: Tryll.Client Target: Unity 6 (6000.x), .NET Standard 2.1, Windows Standalone + Editor

The Unity client is a hand-authored C# port of the Unreal plugin. The public surface is documented on this page and the entity pages linked below. Internal types under Tryll.Client.Internal are not part of the public API.

docs.title: Inspector entities
docs.text:
These types appear in the Inspector and have dedicated reference pages.

Type Kind Description TryllClient MonoBehaviour Singleton session manager. Created automatically — do not add it to a scene. TryllAgentComponent MonoBehaviour Drop-in component that owns and drives one agent on a GameObject. TryllSpeaker MonoBehaviour Plays streaming TTS audio from an agent through an AudioSource. Assign to a TryllAgentComponent's Speaker slot. TryllLipSync MonoBehaviour Plays an agent's viseme track on ARKit face blendshapes, in step with a TryllSpeaker. TryllVoiceInputComponent MonoBehaviour Microphone capture component that streams audio to the STT pipeline. TryllWorkflowAsset ScriptableObject Project asset that stores a TryllGraphDescription. TryllVoiceProfile ScriptableObject An agent's voice: TTS model, identity, visemes and delivery modes. Assign to a TryllAgentComponent's Voice slot. docs.title: TryllAgent
docs.text:
IDisposable handle for a server-side agent. Obtained from TryllClient.RequestCreateAgentAsync or from TryllAgentComponent.Agent.

public ulong AgentId { get; }
public bool  IsValid { get; }

// Actions
public void SendMessage(string text);
public void Cancel(TryllCancelMode mode = TryllCancelMode.StopAndKeep);
public void ChangeParams(string nodeName, TryllNodeParamsBase @params,
                         Action<TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void Resume(string resumeNode = "", Action<TryllError> onComplete = null);
public TryllNodeParamsBase GetNodeParamsBaseline(string nodeName);
public void AppendInteractions(
    IReadOnlyList<TryllDialogInteraction> interactions,
    Action<uint, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void RemoveInteractionsFromEnd(
    int count,
    Action<uint, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void ExportDialog(
    Action<TryllDialogSnapshot, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void ImportDialog(
    TryllDialogSnapshot snapshot,
    TryllDialogCompatibility compatibility = TryllDialogCompatibility.Strict,
    Action<TryllDialogImportResult, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void SaveDialog(string path, string saveId,
                       Action<TryllDialogFileSaveResult, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void LoadDialog(string path,
                       TryllDialogCompatibility compatibility = TryllDialogCompatibility.Strict,
                       Action<TryllDialogFileLoadResult, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void RegisterTool(string toolName, Func<TryllToolCall, string> handler);
public void RegisterTool(string toolName, Func<TryllToolCall, Task<string>> handler);
public TryllAgentVariables Variables { get; }

// Voice (protocol v27)
public Task<TryllError> SetVoiceAsync(TryllVoiceProfileData voice);
public Task<TryllError> SetVoiceAsync(Tryll.VoiceProfileT voice);
public Task<TryllError> SetDeliveryModeAsync(string mode, float intensity = 1f);

// Delivery callbacks (last-writer-wins; pass null to clear).
// All fire on the Unity main thread. Register before SendMessage.
public void SetOnAnswerText(Action<string, string, bool, bool> callback);
public void SetOnTurnComplete(Action<TryllTurnStatus, string, int> callback);
public void SetOnError(Action<TryllError> callback);
public void SetOnTtsAudioFormat(Action<string, int, int, int> callback);
public void SetOnTtsAudio(Action<string, ArraySegment<short>> callback);
// Lip-sync track (voice profile with EmitVisemes). Additive multicast (+=);
// the array is valid only during the callback — copy it to keep it.
public event Action<string, TryllVisemeEvent[]> OnTtsVisemes;
public event Action<TryllError> ToolHandlerError;

// Lifetime
public void Dispose();

A code-created agent (RequestCreateAgentAsync without a component) must register SetOnAnswerText / SetOnTurnComplete before SendMessage or the reply is discarded. Pass null to clear. These replace any previously set callback (not multicast). ToolHandlerError is a separate multicast event for RegisterTool handler / resume failures.

ChangeParams / onComplete and Resume / onComplete deliver a TryllError value — check error.IsOk (it is a struct; success is not null). GetNodeParamsBaseline returns a deep copy (or null if unknown). ChangeParams is allowed while idle or paused.

SetVoiceAsync replaces the agent's voice; it is admitted while idle or paused (AgentBusy otherwise) and keeps the old voice when the new one is rejected (InvalidVoiceProfile). SetDeliveryModeAsync switches the delivery mode at any time, from the next sentence (UnknownDeliveryMode, or AgentVoiceRequired when the agent has no voice). Both return the server's verdict as a TryllError.

Variables is the agent's typed Agent Variables mirror — see TryllAgentVariables below.

For Inspector-friendly wrappers with OnParamChanged / OnResumed UnityEvents, prefer TryllAgentComponent.

AppendInteractions / RemoveInteractionsFromEnd use TryllDialogInteraction pairs — strict idle-only; see Seed and edit dialog history.

ExportDialog / ImportDialog return a TryllDialogSnapshot (full-fidelity replace). ToFlatBufferBytes / FromFlatBufferBytes are the canonical TDLG helpers — the game owns the save file. See Save and Load Agent State for multi-agent coordination, variable restoration, and save-slot handling.

Ownership

If you obtain a TryllAgent directly from TryllClient.RequestCreateAgentAsync (not via TryllAgentComponent), you own it and must call Dispose().

docs.text:
Typed per-agent Variables mirror, reachable via the TryllAgent.Variables property (e.g. agentComp.Agent.Variables).

public TryllError SetInt(string name, long value);
public TryllError SetFloat(string name, double value);
public TryllError SetString(string name, string value);
public TryllError SetBool(string name, bool value);

Setters validate locally — an unknown name or type mismatch returns a non-Ok TryllError immediately, with no wire round-trip. Writes update the local mirror synchronously; the actual UpdateAgentVariablesRequest is batched and flushed automatically immediately before the agent's next SendMessage/Resume/ChangeParams call.

var vars = agentComp.Agent.Variables;
var err = vars.SetInt("level", 13);
if (!err.IsOk) Debug.LogError($"{err.Code}: {err.Message}");
vars.AddToSet("quests_reached", "lost_amulet");

Declare variables on TryllWorkflowAsset.Variables; a component's VariableOverrides may override an asset's declared initial value per-instance (Material-Instance pattern — the Inspector shows one optional row per declaration). Play Mode override edits update the live mirror; flush remains deferred (or use Flush Now in the Inspector).

docs.title: TryllErrorCode
docs.text:
Named error code constants, generated from the server ErrorCodes.h into Runtime/Generated/TryllErrorCode.gen.cs. See Error Codes for the full table.

public enum TryllErrorCode
{
    Ok = 0,
    // Connection: 1001–1003
    // Session: 2001–2005 (2004 InvalidLocale, 2005 InvalidEngineSet)
    // Agent: 3001–3022 (3012 AgentNotPaused, 3013–3015 Variables,
    //        3016 InvalidToolResults, 3018–3022 Dialog snapshots)
    // Inference: 4001–4005 (4004–4005 KV cache)
    // VoiceInput / STT: 4100–4109 (4108–4109 are raised client-side)
    // Protocol: 5001–5006 (5004 ProtocolVersionMismatch is raised client-side)
    // Download / models: 6001–6005, 6007–6009
    // StringStorage: 7001–7004
    // EmbeddedStringStorage: 8001–8003
    // Mutable KB: 8101–8109
}

docs.title: TryllGraphDescription and related types
docs.text:
[Serializable]
public class TryllGraphDescription
{
    public List<TryllNodeDescription> Nodes = new List<TryllNodeDescription>();
    public string                     StartNode;
    public string                     DefaultModelName;

    public TryllGraphDescription Clone();                  // deep copy, params included
    public T FindParams<T>(string nodeName) where T : TryllNodeParamsBase;
    public bool HasNode(string nodeName);
}

[Serializable]
public class TryllNodeDescription
{
    public string               Name;
    public TryllNodeParamsBase  Params;  // typed subclass; exit fields live here
}

Wiring between nodes is set as exit fields directly on the typed Params object — e.g. TryllGenerateParams.DefaultExit, TryllRegexGuardrailParams.TriggeredExit. An empty string routes to END (the default). See each node type's params class for the full list of exit fields and configuration params.

Tools are not on the node description. A ToolCall node carries them on TryllToolCallParams.Tools (TryllToolDefinition[], each with TryllToolParamDefinition parameters).

Both types are classes, so one graph instance handed to several agents shares its params objects. Call Clone() before customising a copy per agent.

docs.title: TryllGraphBuilder
docs.text:
Fluent builder for TryllGraphDescription. Typed AddXxx() methods accept a typed params object; exit fields are set on that object before calling AddXxx().

var graph = new TryllGraphBuilder()
    .AddGenerate("gen", new TryllGenerateParams
    {
        ModelName   = "mymodel",
        // DefaultExit defaults to "" (END)
    })
    .SetStartNode("gen")
    .SetDefaultModelName("mymodel")
    .Build();

docs.title: TryllModelInfo
docs.text:
[Serializable]
public struct TryllModelInfo
{
    public string                 Name;
    public TryllModelStatus       Status;
    public string                 HuggingFaceRepo;
    public long                   SizeBytes;
    public string                 ModelType;        // "language" | "embedding" | "stt" | "tts" | "vad"
    public string                 Engine;           // catalog engine, e.g. "llama-cpp", "sherpa-onnx"
    public string                 Audience;         // "public" | "experimental" | "internal" | ""
    public string[]               Languages;        // BCP-47 primary subtags; empty = undeclared
    public string                 ToolCallFormat;   // "chatml" | "llama3" | "mistral" | "generic" | ""
    public string                 ToolCallSupport;  // "supported" | "unsupported" | ""
    public int                    ContextSize;      // 0 = engine default
    public string[]               Files;
    public string                 LocalPath;        // empty when not on disk
    public bool                   HasDefaultSampling;
    public TryllSamplingParams    DefaultSampling;  // valid only when HasDefaultSampling
    public TryllModelDependency[] Dependencies;     // shared assets; empty when none
    public bool                   HasTtsCapabilities;
    public TryllTtsCapabilities   TtsCapabilities;  // valid only when HasTtsCapabilities
}

[Serializable]
public struct TryllTtsCapabilities
{
    public bool                  VoiceDescription;     // voice profile VoiceDescription
    public bool                  DeliveryInstruction;  // delivery mode Instruction
    public bool                  ReferenceVoice;       // profile and mode ReferenceVoice
    public bool                  Speed;                // Speed / SpeedScale other than 1.0
    public bool                  LanguagePerCall;      // non-empty Lang
    public bool                  Expressiveness;       // Chatterbox exaggeration
    public int                   NumSpeakers;          // SpeakerId is 0..NumSpeakers-1; 0 = undeclared
    public TryllTtsVoicePreset[] VoicePresets;         // named speakers (Orpheus, Maya1)
    public TryllTtsInlineTag[]   InlineTags;
}

Engine is read-only catalog data. A model's variants share one engine, and no client call selects it.

docs.title: Enumerations
docs.text:
public enum TryllInferenceEngine : byte { Mock, LlamaCpp, OnnxGenAI, WindowsML, OpenVino, TensorRtLlm, SherpaOnnx, OnnxRuntime }
public enum TryllNodeType        : byte { Generate, RegexGuardrail, CannedResponse, ToolCall, Retrieve, Instruction, ClassifyIntent, IntentToInstruction, ClassifyIntentLLM, GenerateAndSpeak, Speak, Pause, Transform, Branch, WriteToMemory, Summarize }
public enum TryllTurnStatus      : byte { Success, Error, Cancelled, PauseTimedOut }
public enum TryllCancelMode      : byte { StopAndKeep, StopAndDiscard }
public enum TryllModelStatus     : byte { Absent, Local, Downloading, Loaded, Downloaded, Incomplete }
public enum TryllPlacement       : byte { BeforeUserAsUser, BeforeUserAsSystem, AfterUserAsUser, AfterUserAsSystem }
public enum TryllSendAnswer      : byte { None, Whole, Streamed }
public enum TryllHistoryRole     : byte { None, Assistant }

// Namespace Tryll (not Tryll.Client) — add `using Tryll;`.
public enum WireViseme : byte { sil, PP, FF, TH, DD, kk, CH, SS, nn, RR, aa, E, ih, oh, ou }

TryllNodeType is 0-based, while the wire NodeParams union tag is 1-based. Use the named value, never a raw number. The per-node option enums (TryllToolCallMode, TryllToolCallDisposition, TryllRetrievalMode, TryllBranchTest, and the rest) live in TryllGraphDescription.cs next to these.

docs.title: Threading and error handling summary
docs.text:
• All events and Task<T> completions fire on the Unity main thread.
  • Always check error.IsOk before using any Task<T> result.
  • Call TryllAgentComponent.SendMessage / CreateAgent from the main thread only.
  • Use await only from async void methods rooted on the main thread (e.g., async void Start()).

docs.title: TryllAgentComponent
docs.text:
Type: MonoBehaviour Namespace: Tryll.Client Source: Runtime/TryllAgentComponent.cs

Manages one TryllAgent lifetime on a GameObject. Drop it on any GameObject to get an agent that connects, creates itself, and fires UnityEvents as tokens arrive — no code required.

docs.title: Inspector fields
docs.text: The component with a workflow assigned. Under Variable Overrides, the workflow's Advanced variable is overridden (left checkbox ticked) to true. Field Type Default Description WorkflowAsset TryllWorkflowAsset — Required. Workflow graph asset to use. CreateAgent fails if this is unset. Author the graph as a TryllWorkflowAsset (Create ▸ Tryll ▸ Workflow Asset). To build a graph in code without a component, use TryllGraphBuilder and TryllClient.RequestCreateAgentAsync. EnableDiagnostics bool false When true, the server includes LLM diagnostic info in TurnComplete payloads. MaintainDialogueHistory bool true When true (default) the agent keeps its full dialogue history across turns. Set false for a stateless agent whose history is discarded after each turn — for classification/routing agents that should not store or project prior turns. KvCacheInitialization TryllKvCacheInitialization AllocateOnly Choose AllocateOnly, Prefill, or DeferAllocation for eligible language-model contexts at creation. AutoCreateOnConnect bool true Automatically calls CreateAgent() when the session is ready (or when this component is enabled while already session-ready). Speaker TryllSpeaker — Optional. Plays streaming TTS audio for this agent. When it is null and the graph speaks, CreateAgent uses the TryllSpeaker already on this GameObject, else adds one. Read at CreateAgent; a later change applies on the next CreateAgent. Leave null (and have no TTS nodes) to ignore TTS audio. Voice TryllVoiceProfile — The agent's voice: TTS model, speaker or reference clip, speed, language, visemes and delivery modes. Required when the workflow has a Speak or GenerateAndSpeak node: without it CreateAgent fails with AgentVoiceRequired (3025), and the Inspector shows the same error. Ignored (and no TTS model is loaded) when the workflow does not speak. Read at CreateAgent; set it from code before creation when spawning characters at runtime. Change a live agent's voice with SetVoiceAsync. OverrideVoiceDelivery / VoiceDelivery bool / string false / neutral Per-agent override of the Voice profile's default delivery. The Inspector presents Voice Delivery as a checkbox and dropdown (neutral plus the assigned profile's modes). It is copied into CreateAgent without modifying the shared profile; changing it while an agent is live applies immediately. VariableOverrides List<TryllVariableOverride> empty Per-instance initial-value overrides for variables declared on the workflow (Material-Instance pattern). The custom Inspector shows one optional row per declared variable — checkbox, read-only name, typed value — rather than a free-form list. Stale serialized entries (renamed/removed declarations) appear in a warning foldout and are skipped at CreateAgent with a Debug.LogWarning.

docs.title: Variable Overrides Inspector
docs.text:
For each variable declared on the WorkflowAsset, the Inspector draws:

  1. Override checkbox — when checked, this component's value replaces the declaration's initial value at CreateAgent (and, in Play Mode, updates the live agent mirror — see below).
  2. Name — read-only, taken from the declaration.
  3. Value — the type-appropriate editor (int / float / string / bool / string-set). Disabled until the override is checked; enabling seeds the field from the workflow default.

Only enabled overrides are stored as active sparse entries. Disabling an override keeps the authored value on the component (so re-enabling restores it) but clears the override flag.

Live agent (Play Mode or Tryll Chat): editing an override row updates Agent.Variables immediately (local mirror) whenever HasAgent is true. The wire flush stays deferred — the update is sent before the next SendMessage / Resume / ChangeParams. Unchecking an override assigns the workflow declaration default (not Reset(), which would restore the CreateAgent-time merged initial). A Flush Now button under Live Agent — Variables calls FlushIfDirty for debugging (useful before the next chat turn).

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
// Runtime state
public TryllAgent Agent   { get; }
public bool       HasAgent { get; }
public TryllSpeaker Speaker { get; set; }
public TryllVoiceProfile Voice { get; set; }
public bool OverrideVoiceDelivery { get; set; }
public string VoiceDelivery { get; set; }

// Actions
public async void CreateAgent();
public void       DestroyAgent();
public new void   SendMessage(string text);
public void       Cancel(TryllCancelMode mode = TryllCancelMode.StopAndKeep);
public void       ChangeParams(string nodeName, TryllNodeParamsBase @params,
                               Action<TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void       Resume(string resumeNode = "", Action<TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void       PrefillKvCache();
public void       EvictKvCache();
public void       GetKvCacheStatus();
public void       AppendInteractions(IReadOnlyList<TryllDialogInteraction> interactions);
public void       RemoveInteractionsFromEnd(int count);
public void       ExportDialog();
public void       ImportDialog(
    TryllDialogSnapshot snapshot,
    TryllDialogCompatibility compatibility = TryllDialogCompatibility.Strict);
public void       SaveDialog(string path, string saveId);
public void       LoadDialog(string path,
    TryllDialogCompatibility compatibility = TryllDialogCompatibility.Strict);
public void       RegisterTool(string toolName, Func<TryllToolCall, string> handler);
public void       RegisterTool(string toolName, Func<TryllToolCall, Task<string>> handler);
public TryllNodeParamsBase GetNodeParamsBaseline(string nodeName);

// Voice (protocol v27)
public Task<TryllError> SetVoiceAsync(TryllVoiceProfile profile);
public Task<TryllError> SetDeliveryModeAsync(string mode, float intensity = 1f);

Per-agent Variables are reached through the agent handle: agentComponent.Agent.Variables (a TryllAgentVariables mirror). Agent is null until OnAgentCreated has fired.

CreateAgent is ignored when HasAgent is already true. On success it populates Agent and fires OnAgentCreated. On failure it fires OnError and logs to the console.

SendMessage fires OnError and logs a warning if no agent is ready.

Cancel cooperatively stops the in-flight turn (OnTurnComplete with TryllTurnStatus.Cancelled). No-op if no agent/turn is active.

ChangeParams / Resume complete via their result UnityEvents (OnParamChanged / OnResumed) and the optional per-call callback — exactly once per call. When no agent is ready they report InvalidAgentId (3001) through both channels immediately. ChangeParams is allowed while idle or paused (rejected with AgentBusy only while a turn is actively running between pauses).

GetNodeParamsBaseline returns a deep copy of the last authored params for the named node, or null if no agent is ready / the name is unknown. The returned object is already a clone — mutate it in place, then send via ChangeParams.

KV-cache operations are idle-only. Their result is aggregate status; sending after eviction restores eligible contexts automatically. This component exposes no status UI — use the result events below in your own UI if needed.

AppendInteractions / RemoveInteractionsFromEnd mutate scripted dialog history without running the graph. Strict idle-only — rejected with AgentBusy while a turn is running, paused, or during a KV-cache operation. See Seed and edit dialog history.

ExportDialog captures the complete dialog into a TryllDialogSnapshot; ImportDialog replaces the complete dialog. Both are strict idle-only. The component reports completion through OnDialogExported / OnDialogImported. Tryll does not write a save file.

SaveDialog / LoadDialog persist the same snapshot to a path resolved against the server's process storage root and carry a caller save_id (the server stamps saved_at_ms). Completion is OnDialogSaved / OnDialogLoaded. See Save and Load Agent State.

SetVoiceAsync replaces the live agent's voice and, on success, makes the profile this component's Voice, so a re-created agent keeps it. It is admitted while the agent is idle or paused; a running turn rejects it with AgentBusy (3004), and a profile the model cannot use with InvalidVoiceProfile (3023), keeping the old voice. With no agent yet it only stores the profile for the next CreateAgent and returns Ok; while a create is in flight it returns AgentBusy.

SetDeliveryModeAsync switches the delivery mode (a mode name from the voice profile, or the built-in "neutral"). It is accepted at any time, including mid-turn, and applies from the next sentence. intensity (0–1) scales the mode where the model can use it. Errors: UnknownDeliveryMode (3024), AgentVoiceRequired (3025) when the agent has no voice, InvalidAgentId when no agent is ready.

RegisterTool has a synchronous and an async (Task<string>) overload. A complete paused batch auto-resumes only after every handler finishes on the main thread.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The UnityEvent rows wire up in the Inspector or with AddListener. The NodeEvent rows (ToolCallNotification through NodeEvent) are C# events: subscribe in code. They have no agent id — this component is the agent. TryllClient keeps the all-agents versions. TryllAgent exposes the same seven events for an agent you created without a component. A typed subscriber on this component suppresses this component's NodeEvent for that event, and does not suppress TryllClient.NodeEvent.

Event Signature Description OnAnswerText (string nodeName, string text, bool isDelta, bool isFinal) Fired for each token chunk. nodeName attributes the producing workflow node; isDelta=true when the chunk is a streaming delta; isFinal=true on the last chunk of the turn. OnTurnComplete (TryllTurnStatus status, string debugInfo, int tokensGenerated) Fired once per turn after the last OnAnswerText. debugInfo is non-empty only when EnableDiagnostics is true. OnError (TryllError error) Fired on any agent-level error. OnAgentCreated UnityEvent Fired when CreateAgent() completes successfully. OnAgentDestroyed UnityEvent Fired when the agent is destroyed (by this component, by the server, or on disconnect). OnParamChanged (TryllError error) Fired when a ChangeParams request completes. Check error.IsOk — TryllError is a value type (success is not null). OnResumed (TryllError error) Fired when a Resume request completes. Check error.IsOk. Failures include AgentNotPaused (3012) and UnknownNode (3005). OnKvCachePrefilled (TryllKvCachePrefillResult result, TryllError error) Fired after a prefill request. TryllKvCachePrefillResult extends TryllKvCacheStatus with ContextsCreated, TokensDecoded, and TokensReused. Listeners must take this exact type. OnKvCacheEvicted (TryllKvCacheEvictResult result, TryllError error) Fired after an eviction request. TryllKvCacheEvictResult extends TryllKvCacheStatus with ContextsEvicted. Listeners must take this exact type. OnKvCacheStatus (TryllKvCacheStatus result, TryllError error) Fired after an aggregate status request. OnInteractionsAppended (uint count, TryllError error) Fired when AppendInteractions completes. count is appended_count from the server. OnInteractionsRemoved (uint count, TryllError error) Fired when RemoveInteractionsFromEnd completes. count is removed_count. OnDialogExported (TryllDialogSnapshot snapshot, TryllError error) Fired when ExportDialog completes. Encode a successful snapshot with ToFlatBufferBytes. OnDialogImported (TryllDialogImportResult result, TryllError error) Fired when ImportDialog completes. The result contains the restored interaction count and any compatibility warnings. OnDialogSaved (TryllDialogFileSaveResult result, TryllError error) Fired when SaveDialog completes. OnDialogLoaded (TryllDialogFileLoadResult result, TryllError error) Fired when LoadDialog completes. ToolCallNotification event Action<string, string> (toolName, argumentsJson) for this agent. ToolCallNotificationWithId event Action<string, string, string> (callId, toolName, argumentsJson). Use the id when resuming with a result. ToolCallDetailed event Action<TryllToolCall> Node name and disposition included. A subscriber suppresses NodeEvent for that call. IntentClassified event Action<TryllIntentClassification> Embedding ClassifyIntent result. The payload has no agent id. IntentLlmClassified event Action<TryllIntentLlmClassification> ClassifyIntentLLM result. The payload has no agent id. Paused event Action<string, string> (nodeName, pendingExit). This agent's turn paused. NodeEvent event Action<string, string, IReadOnlyList<KeyValuePair<string, string>>> (nodeName, eventType, kvPairs). Generic fallback when no typed listener is bound here.

docs.title: Lifetime and ownership
docs.text:
• The component owns its agent. It calls Agent.Dispose() in OnDisable and OnDestroy.
  • Do not retain the Agent reference beyond the component's lifetime.
  • If you need an agent that outlives the component, create it directly via TryllClient.RequestCreateAgentAsync and manage its lifetime yourself.
  • On disconnect the component clears its local state without sending a DestroyAgent wire message (the TCP connection is gone).

docs.title: TryllClient
docs.text:
Type: MonoBehaviour (singleton) Namespace: Tryll.Client Source: Runtime/TryllClient.cs

Singleton MonoBehaviour that manages the TCP session to the Tryll server. Created automatically at game start by TryllClientModule via [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(BeforeSceneLoad)] — you do not add it to a scene yourself.

In Play mode it lives on a DontDestroyOnLoad GameObject. In the Editor outside Play mode the static helper EnsureEditorInstance() creates a hidden HideAndDontSave instance.

docs.title: Connection settings
docs.text:
These are read from TryllRuntimeSettings on Awake.

Field Type Default ServerHost string "127.0.0.1" ServerPort int 9100

RequestGetMemoryConsumptionAsync is session-scoped (needs CreateSession) but the snapshot is server-wide — every session on that process. It never fails with AgentBusy. See Inspect Server Memory.

docs.title: GPU throttling and background agents
docs.text:
SetInferenceThrottle tells the server how hard to yield the GPU back to your game — 0f = full speed (the default for a session that never calls it), 1f = maximum yielding. It is fire-and-forget: no request id, no response, nothing to await, so calling it from Update() is fine. It never changes what is generated, only how fast.

void Update()
{
    // Example policy: yield harder as your own frame time worsens.
    float pressure = Mathf.InverseLerp(11f, 20f, Time.smoothDeltaTime * 1000f);
    TryllClient.Instance.SetInferenceThrottle(pressure);
}

Agents nobody is waiting on should say so, so their inference is the first to give way:

var (agent, error) = await TryllClient.Instance.RequestCreateAgentAsync(
    graph, workload: Tryll.AgentWorkload.Background);

Everything else the server classifies from the graph itself, per turn — streamed Generate text is protected, spoken and buffered work absorbs the slack. See Wire Protocol and Server configuration.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
All events fire on the Unity main thread.

Event Signature Description ConnectionChanged Action<bool> Connection state changed. Parameter: isConnected. Error Action<TryllError> Session-level or unroutable error. CreateSessionComplete Action<TryllError> Server acknowledged CreateSession. DownloadProgress Action<string, ulong, ulong, float> (modelName, bytesDownloaded, totalBytes, percent 0–100) — streaming progress. totalBytes may be 0 when unknown. DownloadComplete Action<string, bool, string> (modelName, success, error) — download finished or failed. error is empty on success. LoadModelComplete Action<string, bool> (modelName, success) UnloadModelComplete Action<string, bool> (modelName, success) AgentDestroyed Action<ulong> (agentId) — server confirmed agent teardown. ToolCallNotification Action<ulong, string, string> All agents. (agentId, toolName, argumentsJson). Prefer TryllAgentComponent.ToolCallNotification for one NPC. ToolCallNotificationWithId Action<ulong, string, string, string> All agents. (agentId, callId, toolName, argumentsJson). ToolCallDetailed Action<ulong, TryllToolCall> All agents. Fired in addition to the other tool-call events; a subscriber does not swallow NodeEvent. IntentClassified Action<ulong, TryllIntentClassification> All agents. (agentId, classification). The payload has no agent id. A subscriber swallows this client's generic NodeEvent. IntentLlmClassified Action<ulong, TryllIntentLlmClassification> All agents. (agentId, classification). The payload has no agent id. A subscriber swallows this client's generic NodeEvent. Paused Action<ulong, string, string> All agents. (agentId, nodeName, pendingExit) — the executor paused a turn between nodes (Pause node, or a ToolCall with a pausing disposition). See How to pause and resume a turn. NodeEvent Action<ulong, string, string, IReadOnlyList<KeyValuePair<string,string>>> All-agents generic fallback for unknown or unsubscribed typed events. (agentId, nodeName, eventType, kvPairs). An agent-scope listener does not suppress this, and the reverse. StringStorageChanged Action<string, bool> (name, isCreate) EmbeddedStringStorageChanged Action<string, int, bool> (name, recordCount, isCreate)

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. TryllClientModule creates the singleton at BeforeSceneLoad.
  2. Awake reads TryllRuntimeSettings and applies ServerHost / ServerPort.
  3. Call Connect() to open the TCP session (or enable Auto Launch Server in settings).
  4. Call CreateSession(...) to open the session. It may pass an optional engine warm-up hint; it does not choose an engine. Each model's engine comes from its catalog entry.
  5. Use RequestCreateAgentAsync or attach a TryllAgentComponent.
  6. Call Disconnect() when done, or let OnDestroy clean up on exit.

docs.title: TryllLipSync
docs.text:
Type: MonoBehaviour (sealed) Namespace: Tryll.Client Source: Runtime/TryllLipSync.cs Menu: Add Component → Tryll → Tryll Lip Sync

Plays an agent's viseme track on a face with ARKit blendshapes, in step with the audio played by a TryllSpeaker. The agent's voice profile must have Emit Visemes on — see Add Lip Sync to a Character.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• [RequireComponent(typeof(TryllSpeaker))] — the speaker on the same GameObject is the playback clock. Assign it to the TryllAgentComponent's Speaker field so the agent's audio plays through it.
  • A TryllAgentComponent — the source of the viseme track. A warning is logged in Awake if none is assigned or found on the GameObject.
  • A TryllVoiceProfile on that component with Emit Visemes on. Without it no viseme track arrives: the Inspector shows a warning, and one is logged when the agent is bound.
  • Face meshes whose blendshapes use ARKit names.

docs.title: Source
docs.text: Field Type Default Description _agent TryllAgentComponent same GameObject Agent whose viseme track is played. Re-binds automatically when the agent is re-created. _speaker TryllSpeaker same GameObject Speaker whose playback position the face follows.

docs.title: Face
docs.text:
Field Type Default Description _renderers List<SkinnedMeshRenderer> empty Meshes to drive. Bound at Start when set. _faceRoot Transform none Parent of the face meshes. When Renderers is empty, every SkinnedMeshRenderer under it is bound at Start.

Set one of the two, or call BindFace at runtime; with neither, no mesh is driven.

Only blendshapes named by the Map are bound and written; every other blendshape on those meshes is left untouched for other animation to drive. MappedShapes counts the bound ones.

docs.title: Clock
docs.text: Field Type Default Description _smoothPlaybackClock bool true Smooths the speaker's playback position into a steady clock. _clockWindowSeconds float 1.5 Window of the clock smoother. _outputLeadTrimMs float 342 How far the streaming clip's buffer runs ahead of what is audible. Device-dependent; adjust when a large sync offset is needed. _compensateOutputLatency bool true Subtracts Unity's DSP buffer latency. _syncOffsetMs float 0 Manual sync correction. Positive moves the face earlier.

docs.title: Envelope
docs.text: Field Type Default Description _attackDecayMs float 50 Cross-fade between consecutive shapes. _intensity float (0–1.5) 0.4 Scale on every pose. 0 = no movement, 1 = the full pose table. _smoothingPerSecond float (0–120) 16 Rate at which the face moves toward each shape. 0 disables smoothing. _closureSmoothingPerSecond float (0–200) 60 Rate used while a lip closure (PP, FF) is active. _maxHoldMs float 400 Returns to rest when the last shape of a turn has been held this long (cancelled turns). 0 disables. _compensateSmoothingLag bool true Samples the track ahead by the delay the smoothing adds (1000 / smoothing + attack / 2 ms), so tuning smoothing does not shift sync.

docs.title: Mapping
docs.text: Field Type Default Description _map List<TryllVisemePose> built-in table Pose per viseme, as ARKit channel weights. Left empty, it is filled with the built-in table at Awake.

docs.title: Diagnostics and apply
docs.text: Field Type Default Description _logFrameArrival bool false Logs how far ahead of playback each viseme frame arrived. _applyToMesh bool true When off, the pose is evaluated but not written to the meshes.

AttackDecayMs float (get/set) Same as the Attack Decay Ms field. ApplyToMesh bool (get/set) Same as the Apply To Mesh field. MappedShapes int Number of bound blendshapes. ActiveViseme WireViseme Viseme being shown this frame. docs.title: Related types
docs.text: Type Description TryllVisemeEvent readonly struct: SampleOffset (uint, samples from the start of the turn's audio — its format announcement — across every speaking node of the turn), Viseme (WireViseme), Weight (float, 0–1). TryllAgent.OnTtsVisemes event Action<string, TryllVisemeEvent[]> — fired on the main thread for each viseme frame (one per synthesized sentence). The array belongs to the invocation; copy it to keep it. WireViseme enum : byte in namespace Tryll (add using Tryll;): sil, PP, FF, TH, DD, kk, CH, SS, nn, RR, aa, E, ih, oh, ou. TryllVisemePose Serializable: Viseme + Channels (TryllVisemeChannelWeight[]). TryllVisemeChannelWeight Serializable: Channel (ARKit blendshape name) + Weight.

docs.title: Lifecycle and threading
docs.text:
• Awake fills the default map and builds the pose table; Start binds the meshes; OnEnable subscribes to the agent's viseme events.
  • Each LateUpdate evaluates the pose at the current playback position and writes it to the meshes. Everything runs on the main thread.
  • Each audio format announcement (one per agent turn) clears the previous track.
  • OnDisable unsubscribes and resets the clock and smoothing.

docs.title: TryllRuntimeSettings
docs.text:
Type: ScriptableObject Namespace: Tryll.Client Source: Runtime/TryllRuntimeSettings.cs

Project-level settings for the Tryll Client package. Persisted to Assets/Resources/TryllRuntimeSettings.asset (created automatically on first access).

Edit via Project Settings → Tryll Client (registered by TryllRuntimeSettingsProvider). Selecting the asset itself shows the same fields in the Inspector:

The settings asset with the bundled server auto-launched on the Vulkan backend at 127.0.0.1:9100.

docs.title: Loading at runtime
docs.text:
var settings = TryllRuntimeSettings.Load();

Load() returns a cached singleton. If the asset does not exist in Resources, it falls back to default values.

docs.title: Server process
docs.text:
Field Type Default Description AutoLaunchServer bool true When true, TryllClient spawns the bundled tryll_server.exe automatically on startup (Windows only). Set to false when you manage the server yourself. LlamaCppBackend TryllLlamaCppBackend Vulkan llama.cpp GPU plugin for an auto-launched server (Vulkan or Auto). Passed as --llama-backend. Auto prefers CUDA on NVIDIA when those DLLs were staged and a player build copies them; Vulkan skips them. Ignored when AutoLaunchServer is false. ServerBuildVariant ServerBuild Default Which bundled server payload to launch/stage: Default or Release.

The server exe is always resolved from the package payload — bundled in the package in the Editor, or the Server/ folder copied next to the player exe at build time — so there is no path to configure.

docs.title: Connection defaults
docs.text: Field Type Default Description ServerHost string "127.0.0.1" Host name or IP address of the Tryll server. ServerPort int 9100 TCP port the Tryll server listens on.

docs.title: Session engines
docs.text: There are no engine dropdowns. Each model's engine comes from its catalog entry. BuildEngineDeclarations() derives an optional warm-up hint from the models registered in the Model Manager, and CreateSession sends it so the server starts those engines early. The hint never gates a load. See Choose where models run.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Field Type Default Description StorageDataFolder string "TryllStorage" Project-relative root outside Assets/. The editor launches the server with --storage-root pointing here. Default <Project>/TryllStorage/. A path under Assets/ is rejected. Protocol v24 no longer sends this on CreateSession.

docs.title: Editor / Play Mode
docs.text: Field Type Default Description EnablePlayModeModelGuard bool true When true, entering Play Mode (or the Chat window) verifies every registered model is downloaded first, blocking behind a cancelable dialog if not.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text: Field Type Default Description GameName string "" Integration identifier sent on every session for telemetry grouping. Use a short, stable, lowercase slug (e.g. "my-game"). Leave empty to omit.

docs.title: TryllSpeaker
docs.text:
Type: MonoBehaviour (sealed) Menu: Add Component → Tryll → Tryll Speaker Namespace: Tryll.Client Source: Runtime/TryllSpeaker.cs

Plays streaming TTS audio from a TryllAgent through an AudioSource. Wire it up by assigning this component to the Speaker slot on a TryllAgentComponent, let TryllAgentComponent find or add it when the graph contains a GenerateAndSpeak / Speak node (it uses a TryllSpeaker already on the GameObject, else adds one, at CreateAgent), or attach it to a code-created agent:

var speaker = GetComponent<TryllSpeaker>(); // or AddComponent
agent.SetOnTtsAudioFormat(speaker.HandleFormat);
agent.SetOnTtsAudio(speaker.HandleAudio);

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: [RequireComponent(typeof(AudioSource))] — Unity provisions an AudioSource automatically when TryllSpeaker is added to a GameObject.

docs.title: Inspector fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description _src AudioSource auto The AudioSource used for playback. Populated automatically in Awake; override only when using a pre-existing AudioSource on the same GameObject.

docs.title: Runtime state
docs.text:
Member Type Description HasPendingAudio bool True while decoded audio is still waiting in the chunk queue (or the front chunk is only partially played). After the turn's TurnComplete — when no further audio arrives — a false value means playback has drained down to the small (~100 ms) streaming clip buffer. Useful for hands-free flows that must not re-open the microphone while the character is still audibly speaking. Main thread. ConsumedSamples long Playback clock: samples handed to the audio device since the stream started, at the current sample rate. Underrun silence is not counted; audio dropped unplayed (cancel, format change, disable) counts as played, so the clock never falls behind the stream. Restarts at 0 when the sample rate changes. Any thread. QueuedSamples long Samples still waiting in the queue, including the unplayed tail of the front chunk. ConsumedSamples + QueuedSamples at a format announcement is where that turn's audio starts. Main thread. StopPlayback() void Cancels the current playback: drops all queued audio and ignores further audio frames until the next format announcement, which arrives once per agent turn — so the rest of the turn stays silent, across every speaking node. Does not cancel the turn; call Cancel on the agent for that. Safe to call repeatedly and when nothing is playing. Main thread.

AudioSource.isPlaying is not a playback signal here: the streaming clip loops and keeps "playing" silence between turns.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Both fire on the Unity main thread and are additive multicast (+=). TryllLipSync uses them; subscribe yourself to drive your own track.

Event Signature When OnTtsFormat Action<string nodeName, int sampleRate, int channels, int bitsPerSample> Each format announcement (one per agent turn, from its first speaking node), after the mono-int16 check and after a sample-rate change has reset the clock. OnTtsPcm Action<string nodeName, ArraySegment<short> pcm> Each PCM chunk, before the format and StopPlayback checks. The segment is valid only during the callback.

docs.title: Lifecycle and threading
docs.text:
Method Thread Description HandleFormat(nodeName, sampleRate, channels, bitsPerSample) Main thread Public. Called when the server announces the audio format (via TryllAgent.SetOnTtsAudioFormat or TryllAgentComponent). Creates the streaming AudioClip on the first call and reuses it while the sample rate stays the same; a new rate rebuilds it, discards queued audio and restarts ConsumedSamples at 0. Lifts StopPlayback and raises OnTtsFormat. Outside Play mode (for example the Tryll Chat window) it logs an error and plays nothing. nodeName is accepted for signature compatibility and unused — this speaker mixes all producers into one AudioSource. Only mono int16 PCM is supported; other formats are logged as warnings and ignored. HandleAudio(nodeName, ArraySegment<short>) Main thread Public. Raises OnTtsPcm, then converts int16 → float32 and enqueues the chunk. Ignored before the first format, and after StopPlayback until the next format. nodeName is unused (same as HandleFormat). Drops the newest chunk with a logged warning when the queue is full (kMaxQueuedChunks = 1024). PcmReader(float[]) Audio thread Drains the chunk queue into Unity's audio buffer. Zero-fills the tail on underrun.

HandleFormat and HandleAudio fire on the Unity main thread (drained by TryllClient.Update). PcmReader runs on the Unity audio thread. The two share a chunk queue protected by a brief lock.

docs.title: End-of-stream
docs.text: TtsAudioFrame carries no is_final flag — the turn ends with TurnComplete. The queue drains naturally; there is no explicit flush. When the AudioSource reaches the tail of the queue it will play silence until the next turn starts a new stream.

docs.title: Overflow behaviour
docs.text: TTS synthesis runs well above realtime for typical responses. When many chunks arrive faster than they are played the queue fills. On overflow the newest incoming chunk is dropped (not the oldest), producing a minor glitch rather than a truncated sentence. A single warning is logged per turn's stream (the counter resets at each format announcement).

docs.title: Lifetime and ownership
docs.text:
• TryllSpeaker does not own its TryllAgent. TryllAgentComponent owns both when you use the component path; a code-created agent owns the wiring via SetOnTtsAudioFormat / SetOnTtsAudio.
  • OnDisable stops playback and clears the chunk queue.
  • OnDestroy destroys the AudioClip.
  • Safe to disable between turns (playback stops immediately, queue clears). Re-enabling before the next HandleFormat call is fine.

docs.title: TryllVoiceInputComponent
docs.text:
Type: MonoBehaviour Namespace: Tryll.Client Source: Runtime/TryllVoiceInputComponent.cs

Manages one TryllVoiceInput handle and drives it from the Unity Microphone API. It captures PCM audio in a coroutine and streams it to the Tryll server for speech-to-text transcription. Transcripts can be forwarded automatically to a TryllAgentComponent.

docs.title: Inspector fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description modelName string "Whisper Tiny EN (int8)" STT model catalog name. targetAgent TryllAgentComponent — Agent that receives the final transcript. Leave empty for transcribe-only mode. autoFinishOnSilence bool true Let the server VAD close the utterance on silence (stop-on-silence mode). maxUtteranceMs uint 60000 Hard timeout per utterance in milliseconds. vadThreshold float 0.5 Silero VAD speech-probability threshold (0–1). vadMinSilenceMs uint 1000 Silence duration in ms that closes a speech segment. A shorter value splits one spoken sentence at ordinary pauses, and each fragment is then recognized without the context of the rest. vadSpeechPadMs uint 250 Padding in ms added around detected speech. hotwordsStoragePath string "" Relative path (resolved against Storage Data Folder) to a UTF-8 phrase list. Empty disables hotword biasing. Inspector browse uses the same file picker as knowledge-base and canned-response paths. hotwordsScore float 1.5 How strongly matched phrases are weighted against one another during beam search. Ignored when hotwordsStoragePath is empty. micDeviceName string "" Microphone device name. Empty = system default. pumpIntervalMs float 50 PCM pump cadence in milliseconds. ringBufferSeconds int 2 Microphone ring-buffer length in seconds. createOnEnable bool true Create the VoiceInput handle automatically once the TryllClient session is ready.

docs.title: Runtime state
docs.text:
public TryllVoiceInput Voice       { get; }
public bool HasVoiceInput          { get; }
public bool IsUtteranceActive      { get; }

// Microphone check (see "No microphone" below)
public TryllMicrophoneStatus MicrophoneStatus { get; }  // Unknown, Available, NoDevice, DeviceNotFound, CaptureFailed
public string MicrophoneStatusMessage         { get; }  // why it is unavailable; empty otherwise
public bool IsMicrophoneUnavailable           { get; }  // NoDevice, DeviceNotFound or CaptureFailed

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
// Handle lifecycle
public async void CreateVoiceInput();
public void       DestroyVoiceInput();

// Utterance control
public void BeginUtterance(TryllAgentComponent agentOverride = null);
public void EndUtterance();
public void CancelUtterance();

BeginUtterance starts the microphone and opens a server-side utterance. When agentOverride is given the final transcript is sent to that agent; otherwise targetAgent is used. When both are null the component operates in transcribe-only mode.

EndUtterance commits the current utterance (push-to-talk release) and stops capture.

CancelUtterance discards the current utterance without producing a transcript.

CreateVoiceInput and BeginUtterance both check the microphone first. Without one they raise OnError with MicrophoneUnavailable (4108) and send nothing to the server.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Event Signature Description OnTranscriptUpdate UnityEvent<TranscriptUpdate> Fired for each transcript update (partial and final). Check update.Kind for UtteranceFinal. OnError UnityEvent<TryllError> Fired on protocol-level errors, and with MicrophoneUnavailable (4108) when there is no usable microphone. OnVoiceInputCreated UnityEvent Fired when the VoiceInput handle is created.

docs.title: Capture model
docs.text:
• Microphone starts on BeginUtterance and stops when the UtteranceFinal arrives (or on EndUtterance / CancelUtterance). Each turn closes on a non-empty speech final; begin a new utterance for the next turn.
  • A coroutine pumps small PCM chunks at pumpIntervalMs cadence into the server's audio pipeline.
  • The device-native sample rate is declared to the server; the server resamples to the STT model's expected rate.

docs.title: No microphone
docs.text:
Before creating the voice input and before every utterance, the component checks Microphone.devices:

MicrophoneStatus Cause NoDevice The system reports no recording device. DeviceNotFound micDeviceName names a device that is not connected. The message lists the devices that are. CaptureFailed The device is listed but Microphone.Start could not open it (in use by another app, or blocked by Windows microphone privacy settings).

In each case the voice input is not created, so no STT model is loaded; one [Tryll] warning is logged per distinct problem; and every CreateVoiceInput / BeginUtterance raises OnError with MicrophoneUnavailable (4108) and the same message. Text chat on the agent is unaffected.

The automatic create (createOnEnable) is the exception: it can run inside OnEnable, before other scripts subscribe to OnError, so it only sets the status and logs. Read MicrophoneStatus at start-up rather than waiting for an error.

Read IsMicrophoneUnavailable to show "type to chat" instead of a listening prompt. Calling BeginUtterance again is how to recover: it re-reads the device list and, once a microphone is present, creates the voice input and reports VoiceInputStarting (4109) for that one call: not a failure, just begin again a moment later. Re-check on a user action or a timer, not every frame.

docs.title: Lifetime and ownership
docs.text:
• The component owns its TryllVoiceInput handle and disposes it in OnDisable and OnDestroy.
  • On disconnect the component drops its local state without sending DestroyVoiceInput (the TCP connection is gone).

docs.title: TryllVoiceProfile
docs.text:
Type: ScriptableObject (sealed) Namespace: Tryll.Client Source: Runtime/TryllVoiceProfile.cs, Runtime/TryllVoiceProfileData.cs Menu: Create → Tryll → Voice Profile

A character's voice as an asset: which TTS model speaks, the base identity (speaker, reference clip or description), speed and language, whether a viseme track is emitted, and named delivery modes (moods such as angry or calm) that game code switches at runtime.

Assign the profile to a TryllAgentComponent's Voice field. Every speaking node of that agent (Speak, GenerateAndSpeak) uses it; the nodes hold no voice settings. Because the voice lives on the agent and not in the workflow, one workflow asset can drive many characters, each with its own profile.

A workflow with a speaking node cannot create an agent without a voice: the server rejects it with AgentVoiceRequired (3025). There is no default voice and no default model. A workflow that does not speak ignores the profile and loads no TTS model.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
The asset holds one TryllVoiceProfileData in its Data field.

Field Type Default Description TtsModelName string — Required. TTS model catalog name, picked from the registered TTS models. SpeakerId int 0 Speaker / style index for multi-speaker models (Supertonic 3: 0–9; Orpheus, Maya1: preset index). Must be below the model's speaker count. ReferenceVoice string empty Reference clip (.wav) for clone models (Pocket TTS, Chatterbox, Qwen3-TTS Base), relative to the storage root. Locale-aware: voices/loc/<locale>/ is tried first. Empty = the model's default voice. VoiceDescription string empty Maya1: natural-language identity of the voice. Overrides SpeakerId. Speed float 1.0 Speech-rate multiplier, 0.1–3.0. Must stay 1.0 on models without speed control. Lang string empty Language for multilingual models that pick it per call. Empty = session locale, then the model default. Rejected on models with a fixed language. Expressiveness float 0.5 Chatterbox exaggeration, 0.0–2.0, used by neutral and by modes that do not set their own. Ignored by other models. Prepare TryllVoicePreparation Eager When reference clips are prepared: Eager (all clips when the voice is set, so the first sentence in a new mode has no extra latency) or Lazy (on first use). EmitVisemes bool false Emit a viseme track for every sentence the agent speaks. Turn on for characters with TryllLipSync. DeliveryModes List<TryllDeliveryMode> empty Named deliveries (below). DefaultDeliveryMode string empty Mode active after the voice is set. Empty = neutral.

docs.title: TryllDeliveryMode
docs.text:
Field Type Default Description Name string — Mode name: 1–32 characters of a-z, 0-9, _, unique in the profile. neutral is built in and cannot be defined. ReferenceVoice string empty Clone models: a clip of this character in this mood. Replaces the profile clip while the mode is active. Instruction string empty Maya1: sustained delivery clause. A known keyword (angry, sad, whisper, …) becomes its tuned clause. A ticked Text ID in this field is not resolved; the text resolver only walks graph node params. Expressiveness float -1 Chatterbox exaggeration for this mode, 0.0–2.0. Negative = the profile value. SpeedScale float 1.0 Multiplies the profile speed while the mode is active, 0.5–2.0. Must stay 1.0 on models without speed control.

A mode with no fields set behaves like neutral. This lets every profile define the same mode names, so game code that asks for angry works on any voice, including models with no emotion channel.

A field the model cannot use (a reference clip on Supertonic, an instruction on Qwen3-TTS) is an error: the server rejects the profile with InvalidVoiceProfile (3023) when the voice is set.

docs.title: Inspector
docs.text:
A cloning-model profile with one reference clip per emotion. Qwen3-TTS has no speaker presets, so no Speaker field is shown.

The custom Inspector shows only what the chosen model can use, read from the catalog's TTS capabilities:

  • Speaker is a preset dropdown for models with named presets (Orpheus, Maya1), a slider for multi-speaker models (Supertonic 3), and hidden for single-speaker models.
  • Reference Voice, Voice Description, Speed, Lang and Expressiveness appear only for models that support them. A field that holds a value the model cannot use stays visible so you can clear it.
  • Delivery Modes is a reorderable list whose rows apply the same rules.
  • Default Delivery Mode is a dropdown of the defined modes.
  • Validation findings (missing model, bad mode names, unsupported fields, missing clip files) are shown at the bottom.

When the catalog cannot be read, every field is shown.

Assets ▸ Tryll ▸ Validate Workflow also validates selected voice profiles. A Windows Standalone build fails when a profile names a model that is not marked Production in the Model Manager.

docs.title: Using a profile from code
docs.text:
// Spawning a character: set the voice before the agent is created.
var agent = go.AddComponent<TryllAgentComponent>();
agent.AutoCreateOnConnect = false;
agent.WorkflowAsset = merchantWorkflow;
agent.Voice = merchantVoice;          // TryllVoiceProfile asset
agent.CreateAgent();

// Mood: any time, including mid-turn; applies from the next sentence.
var err = await agent.SetDeliveryModeAsync("angry", intensity: 0.8f);

// Identity: idle (or paused) only.
err = await agent.SetVoiceAsync(disguisedVoice);

Without a component, build a TryllVoiceProfileData and pass it to TryllClient.RequestCreateAgentAsync (voice:), then use TryllAgent.SetVoiceAsync / SetDeliveryModeAsync.

public sealed class TryllVoiceProfileData
{
    public const string NeutralMode = "neutral";
    public TryllVoiceProfileData Clone();
    public Tryll.VoiceProfileT ToWire();
    public static TryllVoiceProfileData FromWire(Tryll.VoiceProfileT wire);
    public static bool IsValidModeName(string name);
}
Error When InvalidVoiceProfile (3023) A field fails validation or the model cannot use it. The message names the field and, for modes, the mode. UnknownDeliveryMode (3024) SetDeliveryModeAsync names a mode the profile does not define. AgentVoiceRequired (3025) A speaking workflow was created without a voice, or SetDeliveryModeAsync on an agent with no voice. AgentBusy (3004) SetVoiceAsync while a turn is running.

docs.title: TryllWorkflowAsset
docs.text:
Type: ScriptableObject Namespace: Tryll.Client Source: Runtime/TryllWorkflowAsset.cs

ScriptableObject that stores a TryllGraphDescription as a project asset. Assign it to a TryllAgentComponent to define which workflow graph the agent runs. Because it is a regular Unity asset, it is serialized, version-controlled, and reusable across multiple GameObjects.

docs.title: Creating an asset
docs.text:
In the Project window: right-click → Create → Tryll → Workflow Asset.

The asset opens in the Inspector where you can configure Graph nodes and their exit fields, or populate them programmatically via TryllGraphBuilder.

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
public sealed class TryllWorkflowAsset : ScriptableObject
{
    public TryllGraphDescription Graph;
    public List<TryllVariableDecl> Variables;
}

Graph is the complete workflow graph description. It is serialized by Unity's standard serialization and editable in the Inspector.

Variables declares the agent's Agent Variables store — name, type, and initial value, passed to CreateAgent. A TryllAgentComponent.VariableOverrides entry may override a declared variable's initial value per-instance without changing this asset (Material-Instance pattern).

docs.title: Programmatic alternative
docs.text:
If you do not need a persistent asset, build a TryllGraphDescription in C# and create the agent directly from it — no component required:

var graph = new TryllGraphBuilder()
    .AddGenerate("gen", new TryllGenerateParams
    {
        // DefaultExit is "" (END) by default
    })
    .SetStartNode("gen")
    .SetDefaultModelName("my-model")
    .Build();

var (agent, error) = await TryllClient.Instance.RequestCreateAgentAsync(graph);

When you drive an agent through TryllAgentComponent, assign this asset to the component's Workflow Asset field. A component cannot create an agent without one.
