docs.title: Blueprint Catalog
docs.text:
The Blueprint-visible nodes exposed by the Tryll Unreal plugin, grouped by category. Use this page to find which Blueprint function or event to place; use the Unreal C++ API Reference and the feature reference pages for parameter-level detail.

Most nodes live under two UObjects; the speaker, lip-sync and voice-input components add their own (below):

  • UTryllSubsystem — a UGameInstanceSubsystem. Access from any Blueprint with the Get Tryll Subsystem node (GameplayStatics → GetGameInstance → GetSubsystem<TryllSubsystem>).
  • UTryllAgentComponent — an UActorComponent. Add one to any actor; when bAutoCreateOnConnect is true (the default), it auto-creates its agent once the session is ready (connected and the session created), queuing if it spawns earlier. (The property name predates the session-ready semantics.)

Static helper libraries (Tryll|Languages, Tryll|Intent), the UTryllKvResidencyPolicy component (Tryll|KV Cache), and the generated node-params factory are not listed here; see their class pages.

Categories use the pipe convention (Tryll|Connection, Tryll|Models, …) so everything appears grouped under a single Tryll folder in the Blueprint context menu.

docs.title: Connection — Tryll|Connection
docs.text:
On UTryllSubsystem.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Connect Callable — — Starts the background connect. Fires OnConnectionChanged(true) when ready. Uses the host/port from project settings; see Run the Tryll Server. Disconnect Callable — — Closes the socket. Fires OnConnectionChanged(false) once torn down. Is Connected Pure — bool True while the background state is Connected. Get Session Id Pure — int64 Server-assigned session id; 0 when disconnected.

docs.title: Session — Tryll|Session
docs.text:
On UTryllSubsystem.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Create Session Callable Game Name (FString, default empty), Locale (FString, BCP-47, default empty), Use Project Locale When Empty (bool, default true) — Sends CreateSessionRequest. Fires OnCreateSessionComplete(bSuccess). Mandatory and one-shot: only valid once, immediately after OnConnectionChanged(true). Storage root comes from Project Settings Storage Data Folder via the launcher (--storage-root), not this node. See Agent Parameters and Server Configuration. Create Session From Settings Callable — — Same as Create Session but reads Game Name and Locale from Project Settings → Tryll Client, and sends the engine warm-up hint built from the Model Manager manifest. There are no engine settings: each model's catalog entry names its engine. This is what Auto Create Session calls for you. Is Session Ready Pure — bool True once the session has been created (connected and CreateSession succeeded). Set Session Locale Callable Locale (FString, BCP-47; empty clears it) — Changes the session language without recreating the session. Applies to every agent from its next turn (TTS language, locale template keys); content already bound to a node does not swap. Fires OnSetSessionLocaleComplete(Locale, bSuccess). Set Inference Throttle Callable Level (float, 0–1) — Reports how hard the server should yield the GPU back to your game. 0 = full speed (the default for a session that never calls it), 1 = maximum yielding. Fire-and-forget — no response, no completion event, nothing to await — so calling it every tick is fine. Never changes what is generated, only how fast. See Wire Protocol.

docs.title: Models — Tryll|Models
docs.text:
On UTryllSubsystem.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Request Download Model Callable Model Name (FString) — Kicks off a download. Progress arrives via OnDownloadProgress; completion via OnDownloadComplete. Request Load Model Callable Model Name (FString), Placement (ETryllMemoryPlacement, default Auto), Is Override (bool, default false) — Loads and pins a locally-available model. The model's catalog entry names the engine that runs it. Placement applies to this load only and is used only when Is Override is true; otherwise the session's per-model hint applies. Placement is a hint the server may downgrade. Fires OnLoadModelComplete(ModelName, bSuccess). Request Unload Model Callable Model Name (FString) — Unloads a loaded model. Fires OnUnloadModelComplete(ModelName, bSuccess). Build Engine Declarations Flat Callable (static, on UTryllRuntimeSettings) — TArray<int32> The optional engine warm-up hint as flattened (role, engine) ordinal pairs, derived from the models registered in the Model Manager. Advisory only: it never selects or gates an engine. Set User Models Catalog Path Callable (static, on UTryllRuntimeSettings, category Tryll) Relative Path (FString; empty clears) bool, Out Error (FString) Stores a project-relative custom models catalog. Returns false for a path outside the project. With auto-launch on, a running server is restarted and an open session is dropped.

Model listing is not a Blueprint node. Call the C++ UTryllSubsystem::RequestListModels(OnComplete), then read the result in its callback or bind OnListModelsComplete. See Model Management for lifecycle rules.

docs.title: Agent — Tryll|Agent
docs.text:
On UTryllAgentComponent.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Create Agent Callable — — Creates a server-side agent from the component's Workflow Asset (fails with OnError if none is assigned). Fires OnAgentReady. With bAutoCreateOnConnect (the default) it runs automatically once the session is ready (Is Session Ready, after CreateSession succeeds), not on raw connect. Destroy Agent Callable — — Destroys the server-side agent. Fires the subsystem's OnAgentDestroyed(AgentId). Send Message Callable Message (FString) — Sends a user turn. Streams back via OnAnswerText; ends with OnTurnComplete. If the agent exists but is busy (a running turn or a KV-cache operation), the message is queued instead of dropped (only the newest is kept) and OnMessageQueued fires. See Stream Answers to UI. Try Flush Pending Message Callable — bool Hands the queued message to the agent if it can accept one now. Returns true only when a message was sent. Called automatically on agent-ready, turn-complete, and cache-operation-complete. Has Pending Message Pure — bool True while a queued message is waiting for the agent. Get Pending Message Pure — FString The queued message, or empty. Is Turn In Flight Pure — bool True while a turn this component started has not completed. Get Paused Node Pure — FString The node the turn is paused after, or empty when not paused. While non-empty, Send Message fails with AgentBusy until Resume or Cancel. Cancel Callable Mode (ETryllCancelMode, default StopAndKeep) — Cooperatively stop the in-flight turn. Ends with OnTurnComplete(Cancelled). Idle cancel is a no-op. See Cancelling a turn. Resume Callable Resume Node (FString, default empty) — Resume a paused turn. Empty continues via the pending exit; non-empty jumps to that node. Fires OnResumed. See How to pause and resume a turn. Get Node Params Baseline Callable Node Name (FString) UTryllNodeParamsBase The authored params for a node. Clone it, edit fields, then pass to Change Params. Call after OnAgentReady; returns null for an unknown node. Change Params Callable Node Name (FString), Params (UTryllNodeParamsBase) — Mutate a node parameter at runtime (the agent must be idle or paused). Fires OnParamChanged. See Change Agent Parameters. Is Agent Ready Pure — bool True after OnAgentReady has fired. Get Agent Id Pure — int64 Server-assigned agent id; 0 before ready.

See UTryllAgentComponent for the full property and method reference.

docs.title: Tools — Tryll|Tools
docs.text:
On UTryllAgentComponent. Use these to answer a paused AwaitResult tool call from Blueprint.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Resume With Tool Result Callable Tool Result (FTryllToolResult: CallId, Result), Resume Node (FString, default empty) — Resumes the paused turn with one result correlated to a tool-call id. Fires OnResumed. Resume With Tool Results Callable Tool Results (TArray<FTryllToolResult>), Resume Node (FString, default empty) — Resumes with the complete result batch for one paused tool-call pass. An incomplete or duplicate batch is rejected (InvalidToolResults, 3016). Fires OnResumed. Retry Paused Tool Batch Callable — — Re-runs the retained paused batch: handlers that already produced a result are skipped, the rest run, and a fresh resume is sent. No-op without a retained batch. Has Paused Tool Batch Pure — bool True while a paused tool-call batch is retained (until a successful resume, turn end or cancel, destroy, or disconnect).

docs.title: KV Cache — Tryll|KV Cache
docs.text:
On UTryllAgentComponent. Calls are idle-only.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Prefill KV Cache Callable — — Synchronises every eligible language-model context to its reusable prefix. Fires OnKvCachePrefilled or OnKvCachePrefillError. Evict KV Cache Callable — — Releases every eligible raw language-model context while retaining the agent. Idempotent. Fires OnKvCacheEvicted or OnKvCacheEvictError. Get KV Cache Status Callable — — Reads aggregate residency and prefix status. Fires OnKvCacheStatus or OnKvCacheStatusError.

The component's KV Cache Initialization property is in the same category.

Event Payload Fires when On KV Cache Prefilled Result (FTryllKvCachePrefillResult) A prefill request completed with aggregate counts and status. On KV Cache Evicted Result (FTryllKvCacheEvictResult) An eviction request completed with aggregate counts and status. On KV Cache Status Result (FTryllKvCacheStatus) A status request completed. On KV Cache Prefill Error / Evict Error / Status Error ErrorMessage (FString) The corresponding lifecycle operation failed.

docs.title: Dialog — Tryll|Dialog
docs.text:
On UTryllAgentComponent. Both calls are strict idle-only (AgentBusy while a turn is running, paused, or during a KV-cache operation). See Seed and edit dialog history.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Append Interactions Callable Interactions (TArray<FTryllDialogInteraction>) — Appends scripted user/assistant pairs without running the graph. An empty side is omitted; both empty is skipped. Fires OnInteractionsAppended or OnAppendInteractionsError. Remove Interactions From End Callable Count (int32) — Removes whole interactions from the end of the dialog. Fires OnInteractionsRemoved or OnRemoveInteractionsError. Event Payload Fires when On Interactions Appended Count (int32) Append Interactions succeeded. On Append Interactions Error ErrorMessage (FString) Append Interactions failed. On Interactions Removed Count (int32) Remove Interactions From End succeeded. On Remove Interactions Error ErrorMessage (FString) Remove Interactions From End failed.

docs.title: Variables — Tryll|Variables
docs.text:
On UTryllAgentComponent, via Get Variables. See Agent Variables for the full model. Setters validate locally and return an FTryllError immediately for an unknown name or type mismatch — no wire round-trip. Writes are batched and flushed automatically immediately before the next Send Message / Resume / Change Params call.

The component Details panel also exposes declaration-driven Variable Overrides and a Live Agent — Variables section (dirty status + Flush Now) when a PIE agent or Tryll Chat preview agent is attached. Unchecking an override assigns the workflow declaration default on the live mirror.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Get Variables Callable (on UTryllAgentComponent) — UTryllAgentVariables The agent's variables mirror, or null when no agent is ready. Has an execution pin. Call after OnAgentReady. Set Int Variable Callable (on UTryllAgentVariables) Name (FString), Value (int64) FTryllError Assigns a declared Int variable. Set Float Variable Callable Name (FString), Value (float) FTryllError Assigns a declared Float variable. Set String Variable Callable Name (FString), Value (FString) FTryllError Assigns a declared String variable. Set Bool Variable Callable Name (FString), Value (bool) FTryllError Assigns a declared Bool variable. Set String Set Variable Callable Name (FString), Value (TArray<FString>) FTryllError Replaces a declared StringSet variable wholesale. Add To Set Variable Callable Name (FString), Element (FString) FTryllError Idempotent insert into a StringSet variable. Remove From Set Variable Callable Name (FString), Element (FString) FTryllError Idempotent removal from a StringSet variable. Reset Variable Callable Name (FString) FTryllError Restores the CreateAgent-time initial value. Is Dirty Pure — bool True when staged mutations have not been flushed yet. Flush If Dirty Callable — — Eager wire flush (same as Details Flush Now). No-op when clean. Get Int Variable Pure Name (FString) int64, bFound (bool) Current value; bFound is false if the name isn't declared. Get Float Variable Pure Name (FString) float, bFound (bool) Current value; bFound false if undeclared. Get String Variable Pure Name (FString) FString, bFound (bool) Current value; bFound false if undeclared. Get Bool Variable Pure Name (FString) bool, bFound (bool) Current value; bFound false if undeclared. Get String Set Variable Pure Name (FString) TArray<FString>, bFound (bool) Current value; bFound false if undeclared.

docs.title: Voice Input — Tryll|Voice
docs.text:
On UTryllVoiceInputComponent. Add one to an actor (optionally alongside a UTryllAgentComponent) and download an STT model in the Model Manager. See UTryllVoiceInputComponent for the full property list.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Create Voice Input Callable — — Creates the server-side STT handle. Fires OnVoiceInputCreated. Normally automatic when bCreateOnConnect is true. Destroy Voice Input Callable — — Releases the server-side STT handle. Begin Utterance Callable Agent Override (UTryllAgentComponent, optional) — Opens an utterance and starts mic capture. The final transcript routes to the override, else TargetAgent, else transcribe-only. End Utterance Callable — — Commits the utterance (push-to-talk release). Cancel Utterance Callable — — Drops the utterance without producing a transcript. Has Voice Input Pure — bool True once the handle exists. Is Utterance Active Pure — bool True while an utterance is open. Get Microphone Status Pure — ETryllMicrophoneStatus Result of the last microphone check: Unknown, Available, NoDevice or CaptureFailed. Get Microphone Status Message Pure — FString Why the microphone is unavailable; empty when it is not. Is Microphone Unavailable Pure — bool True for NoDevice or CaptureFailed. Show "type to chat"; Begin Utterance re-checks and recovers once a microphone appears.

docs.title: Events — Tryll|Events (on UTryllAgentComponent)
docs.text:
Bind these on each agent component instance. All are BlueprintAssignable, so Bind Event to … nodes work directly.

Event Payload Fires when On Agent Ready — Server confirms agent creation. On Answer Text NodeName (FString), Text (FString), bIsFinal (bool) Streaming token chunk. NodeName names the producing node (multi-sender graphs). bIsFinal is true on the last chunk before OnTurnComplete. (No bIsDelta pin — the Blueprint delegate is 3-param; the C++ agent handle carries bIsDelta separately.) On Answer Full FullText (FString) After OnTurnComplete, with the full accumulated response. On Turn Complete Status (ETryllTurnStatus), DebugInfo (FString), TokensGenerated (int32) Turn ended. DebugInfo is populated only when bEnableDiagnostics is set. On Error ErrorMessage (FString) Any agent-level error (send failure, server error response). On Param Changed bSuccess (bool), ErrorMessage (FString) A ChangeParams request completed; ErrorMessage is empty on success. On Resumed bSuccess (bool), ErrorMessage (FString) A Resume request completed; ErrorMessage is empty on success, otherwise describes AgentNotPaused (3012) or UnknownNode (3005). On Tool Call ToolName (FString), ArgumentsJson (FString) A ToolCall node on this agent with a non-RouteOnly disposition detected a call. No agent id: this component is the agent. On Tool Call With Id CallId (FString), ToolName (FString), ArgumentsJson (FString) Same call, with the id to echo in tool_results. On Tool Call Detailed Call (FTryllToolCall) Same call, including node name and disposition. Also suppresses this component's On Node Event. On Intent Classified Classification (FTryllIntentClassification) Embedding ClassifyIntent on this agent. The struct has no AgentId. On Intent LLM Classified Classification (FTryllIntentLlmClassification) ClassifyIntentLLM on this agent. The struct has no AgentId. On Paused NodeName (FString), PendingExit (FString) This agent's turn paused between nodes. Binding it suppresses this component's On Node Event for the pause. On Node Event NodeName (FString), EventType (FString), KvPairs (TArray<FTryllNodeEventKeyValue>) Generic fallback for this agent when no typed listener is bound on this component.

A typed listener on this component does not suppress the subsystem events below, and the reverse.

The KV-cache and dialog events are listed with their nodes above. One more component event sits under Tryll|Agent:

Event Payload Fires when On Message Queued Message (FString) Send Message could not hand the message over yet and queued it. Use it to show a "waiting to send" state.

docs.title: Voice — Tryll|TTS (on UTryllAgentComponent)
docs.text:
The agent's voice is a voice profile: a UTryllVoiceProfile data asset (Content Browser Tryll ▸ Voice Profile) assigned to the component's Voice Profile property (Tryll|TTS, editable, Blueprint read-only). Every speaking node of the workflow (Speak, Generate And Speak) uses it. A workflow that speaks needs one: without it the server refuses the agent with AgentVoiceRequired (3025), the component logs an error at Create Agent, and Data Validation flags the component. One workflow can serve many characters, each with its own profile.

The component's Voice Delivery row is a per-agent override of the profile's default mode. Enable its checkbox and choose neutral or one of the assigned profile's modes. It is used by the next Create Agent without modifying the shared profile asset, and a change applies immediately to a live PIE or Tryll Chat agent.

Node Kind Inputs Outputs Notes Set Voice Callable New Voice (UTryllVoiceProfile) — With a live agent, replaces its voice (idle only: AgentBusy 3004 during a turn; InvalidVoiceProfile 3023 when the model cannot use the profile, and the old voice stays) and assigns Voice Profile on success. The active delivery mode survives when the new profile defines a mode of the same name. Without an agent it only assigns Voice Profile for the next Create Agent. Fires OnVoiceChanged. Set Delivery Mode Callable Mode (FString), Intensity (float, default 1, advanced) — Switches the voice's delivery mode, for example angry. Allowed mid-turn; applies from the next sentence. neutral always works; a mode the profile does not define fails with UnknownDeliveryMode (3024) and the current mode stays. Intensity (0–1) scales the mode where the model can use it. Fires OnDeliveryModeChanged. Get Delivery Mode Pure — FString The mode last applied to the live agent; the profile's default mode (empty = neutral) before any switch. Event Payload Fires when On Voice Changed Error (FTryllError) Set Voice completed. Error.Code is 0 on success. On Delivery Mode Changed Mode (FString), Error (FTryllError) Set Delivery Mode completed. Error.Code is 0 on success, 3024 for an undefined mode, 3025 when the agent has no voice.

docs.title: Events — Tryll|TTS (on UTryllSpeakerComponent)
docs.text:
UTryllAgentComponent plays TTS audio through the UTryllSpeakerComponent on its actor, and adds one at CreateAgent if the graph speaks and there is none. Add one yourself to bind these events to react to the audio lifecycle. Every Started is followed by exactly one Finished (unless the component ends play mid-speech). The agent's Speaker property (Tryll|TTS, Blueprint read/write, set on a placed instance) picks a specific speaker; it is read at CreateAgent.

Event Payload Fires when On Tts Audio Started — The first PCM chunk of a turn is queued — speech is about to begin. Once per turn, even when several nodes speak. On Tts Audio Finished — The turn is complete and its queued audio has been handed to the audio engine (its own buffers, a few tens of ms, still play out). Also fires immediately when Stop Playback cuts speech off. Function Kind Returns Description Stop Playback Callable — Drops all queued audio and ignores further audio until the next turn announces its audio format. Fires On Tts Audio Finished if speech was playing. Does not cancel the turn — call Cancel on the agent for that. Safe to call repeatedly. Get Sample Rate Pure int32 Sample rate of the current TTS stream, in Hz. 0 before the first format announcement. Get Output Latency Ms Pure float Audio engine output buffering after the speaker's playback clock, in milliseconds. 0 without an audio device. Tryll Lip Sync subtracts it when Compensate Output Latency is on.

See Add Voice Output to an Agent for the full setup workflow.

docs.title: Functions — Tryll|Lip Sync (on UTryllLipSyncComponent)
docs.text:
Tryll Lip Sync plays the server's viseme track on a face with ARKit morph targets. See Add Lip Sync to a Character.

Function Kind Parameters Returns Description Set Intensity Callable InIntensity (float) — Scales every mouth pose. 0 keeps the mouth at rest. Bind Face Callable InFaceMesh (USkeletalMeshComponent) — Rebinds to a face mesh, for example after spawning or swapping it at runtime. Is Face Bound Pure — bool true once at least one ARKit morph target from the pose table was found on the face. Get Bound Channel Count Pure — int32 How many pose-table channels were found as morph targets. Get Active Viseme Pure — ETryllViseme The viseme showing now. Get Applied Jaw Open Pure — float jawOpen as written this frame, 0–1. Property Type Access Description Speaker UTryllSpeakerComponent Blueprint read/write The speaker whose track plays. Empty = the first one on the owner. Face Mesh USkeletalMeshComponent Blueprint read/write The face to drive. Empty = searched on the owner; a mesh named Face wins. Settings FTryllVisemeSettings Blueprint read/write Intensity, smoothing, sync offset and latency compensation; applied every tick. Poses TArray<FTryllVisemePose> Editor only The pose table. Read at BeginPlay.

docs.title: Events — Tryll|Events (on UTryllVoiceInputComponent)
docs.text:
Event Payload Fires when On Transcript Update Update (FTryllTranscriptUpdate) Each transcript update — partial and final. Read Update.Kind (SpeechStart / Partial / SegmentFinal / UtteranceFinal) and Update.Text. On Error ErrorMessage (FString) Any voice error, message only. On Error Detailed Error (FTryllError) Fires with On Error, carrying the code — e.g. MicrophoneUnavailable (4108) when there is no usable microphone, VoiceInputStarting (4109) while voice input is being (re)created. On Voice Input Created — The STT handle has been created.

See Use Voice Input and UTryllVoiceInputComponent.

docs.title: Events — Tryll|Events (on UTryllSubsystem)
docs.text:
Bind these once per connection, typically in Event BeginPlay. The tool-call, intent, pause, and node-event rows are the all agents surface. Prefer the matching events on UTryllAgentComponent when you only care about one NPC.

Event Payload Fires when On Connection Changed bConnected (bool) Transport state flipped. true means the session is ready to configure. On Error ErrorMessage (FString) Subsystem-level error (transport, protocol, model). On Agent Destroyed AgentId (int64) A server-side agent was destroyed (by DestroyAgent or session tear-down). On Create Session Complete bSuccess (bool) Response to CreateSession. On List Models Complete Models (TArray<FTryllModelInfo>), bSuccess (bool) Response to the C++ RequestListModels. On Set Session Locale Complete Locale (FString), bSuccess (bool) Response to Set Session Locale. On Get Memory Consumption Complete Snapshot (FTryllMemorySnapshot), bSuccess (bool) Response to RequestGetMemoryConsumption. Session-scoped, server-wide; never AgentBusy. Bind after a C++ call — the request itself is not a Blueprint node. See Inspect Server Memory. On Download Progress ModelName (FString), BytesDownloaded (int64), TotalBytes (int64), Percent (float) Periodic download update. Percent is 0–100. TotalBytes may be 0 when the server does not know the content length — fall back to Percent. On Download Complete ModelName (FString), bSuccess (bool), ErrorMessage (FString) Download finished or failed. ErrorMessage is empty on success. On Load Model Complete ModelName (FString), bSuccess (bool) Response to RequestLoadModel. On Unload Model Complete ModelName (FString), bSuccess (bool) Response to RequestUnloadModel. On Tool Call AgentId (int64), ToolName (FString), ArgumentsJson (FString) All-agents form of the component event. A ToolCall node with a non-RouteOnly disposition detected a call. See Define and Handle Tool Calls. On Intent Classified AgentId (int64), Classification (FTryllIntentClassification) All-agents form. Embedding ClassifyIntent with notify_client OnFound/Always. The agent id is this pin; the struct does not repeat it. See Build an Intent-Driven NPC. On Intent LLM Classified AgentId (int64), Classification (FTryllIntentLlmClassification) All-agents form. ClassifyIntentLLM with notify_client OnFound/Always. The agent id is this pin. On Paused AgentId (int64), NodeName (FString), PendingExit (FString) All-agents form. The executor paused a turn between nodes (Pause node, or a ToolCall with a pausing disposition). See How to pause and resume a turn. On Tool Call With Id AgentId (int64), CallId (FString), ToolName (FString), ArgumentsJson (FString) All-agents form of the component event. Use CallId when resuming with a result. On Tool Call Detailed AgentId (int64), Call (FTryllToolCall) All-agents form. Fired in addition to On Tool Call / On Tool Call With Id; binding it does not suppress On Node Event. On Node Event AgentId (int64), NodeName (FString), EventType (FString), KvPairs (TArray<FTryllNodeEventKeyValue>) All-agents generic fallback when no typed listener is bound on the subsystem. An agent-scope listener does not suppress this, and the reverse. On Create String Storage Complete Name (FString), bSuccess (bool) Response to CreateStringStorage. On Destroy String Storage Complete Name (FString), bSuccess (bool) Response to DestroyStringStorage. On Create Embedded String Storage Complete Name (FString), RecordCount (int32), bSuccess (bool) Response to CreateEmbeddedStringStorage. On Destroy Embedded String Storage Complete Name (FString), bSuccess (bool) Response to DestroyEmbeddedStringStorage.

String-storage requests are C++-only

The four completion events above are Blueprint-assignable, but the matching request calls (RequestCreateStringStorage and its …FromFile / …Keyed variants, RequestCreateEmbeddedStringStorage and its …FromStrings variant, and the two destroy calls) take C++ callbacks and are not exposed as Blueprint nodes — initiate them from C++. For most graphs you don't need them at all: pin a storage by relative path in the node's params and the server loads it at agent-creation time. See String Storage and Embedded String Storage.

docs.title: Assets and structs (editable in Details panel)
docs.text:
These are Blueprint-visible types, not callable nodes. You configure them on the UTryllAgentComponent's Details panel or inside a UTryllWorkflowAsset.

Type Kind Purpose UTryllWorkflowAsset UDataAsset Content-Browser asset wrapping an FTryllGraphDescription. Assign one to the component to avoid authoring the graph in C++. UTryllSpeakerComponent UActorComponent Plays streaming TTS audio from an agent. Add to the same actor as UTryllAgentComponent; found at CreateAgent, or added then if the graph speaks and the actor has none. See Add Voice Output to an Agent. UTryllLipSyncComponent UActorComponent Tryll Lip Sync: plays the viseme track on ARKit morph targets. Add next to a UTryllSpeakerComponent. See Add Lip Sync to a Character. UTryllVoiceInputComponent UActorComponent Captures the microphone and streams STT. Add to an actor; routes the final transcript to a sibling UTryllAgentComponent. Requires an STT model on disk (Model Manager). UTryllVoiceProfile UPrimaryDataAsset An agent's voice. Content Browser Tryll ▸ Voice Profile; assign it to UTryllAgentComponent::VoiceProfile. Its Details panel shows only the fields the chosen model can use (from the model catalog) and lists what the server would reject. FTryllVoiceProfileData USTRUCT(BlueprintType) The profile's fields (Voice on the asset): TtsModelName (required), SpeakerId, ReferenceVoice, VoiceDescription, Speed, Lang, Expressiveness, Prepare, bEmitVisemes (turns on the lip-sync track), DeliveryModes, DefaultDeliveryMode. FTryllDeliveryMode USTRUCT(BlueprintType) One named delivery: Name, ReferenceVoice, Instruction, Expressiveness (-1 = the profile's), SpeedScale. UTryllGenerateAndSpeakParams, UTryllSpeakParams UObject (EditInlineNew) Node params for Generate And Speak and Speak. They hold no voice settings (protocol v27): only text routing and sentence chunking. The voice is the agent's Voice Profile. ETryllViseme, FTryllVisemeEvent UENUM / USTRUCT(BlueprintType) The 15 visemes, and one track event: SampleOffset (int64), Viseme, Weight. FTryllVisemePose, FTryllVisemeChannelWeight, FTryllVisemeSettings USTRUCT(BlueprintType) A viseme's ARKit channel weights, and the lip-sync tuning settings. FTryllGraphDescription USTRUCT(BlueprintType) The full graph: Nodes, StartNode, and DefaultModelName. Exits are fields on each node's params; there is no separate routes list. FTryllVariableDecl USTRUCT(BlueprintType) Declares one Agent Variable: name, type, initial value. Editable in the UTryllWorkflowAsset's Variables array. FTryllVariableOverride USTRUCT(BlueprintType) Per-instance override of a declared variable's initial value, editable in UTryllAgentComponent::VariableOverrides (Material-Instance pattern). FTryllModelInfo USTRUCT(BlueprintType) Row returned by RequestListModels / OnListModelsComplete; fields mirror Model Management. FTryllMemorySnapshot USTRUCT(BlueprintType) Server-wide RAM/VRAM snapshot from RequestGetMemoryConsumption. ETryllMemoryTier UENUM(BlueprintType) Confidence of a memory figure: Measured, Derived, Estimated. FTryllIntentClassification USTRUCT(BlueprintType) Embedding ClassifyIntent payload: node name, intent, record id, record index, distance, not-found reason. No AgentId — the session event pin or the component scope carries it. FTryllIntentLlmClassification USTRUCT(BlueprintType) ClassifyIntentLLM payload: node name, intent, top and second probability, label probabilities, not-found reason. No AgentId. FTryllNodeEventKeyValue USTRUCT(BlueprintType) One key/value pair on On Node Event. FTryllError USTRUCT(BlueprintType) Error envelope used in some event payloads. Code matches ETryllErrorCode. ETryllInferenceEngine UENUM(BlueprintType) Names the catalog engines (LlamaCpp, SherpaOnnx, OnnxRuntime, …). Each model's catalog entry names its engine. CreateSession does not take this enum. ETryllNodeType UENUM(BlueprintType) Node type selector used inside FTryllGraphDescription. ETryllTurnStatus UENUM(BlueprintType) Turn outcome carried by OnTurnComplete (Success, Error, Cancelled, PauseTimedOut). PauseTimedOut means a pause outlived its timeout and the pausing node had no timeout exit. ETryllCancelMode UENUM(BlueprintType) Cancel mode for Cancel: StopAndKeep (chat Stop) or StopAndDiscard (rollback the interaction). ETryllKvCacheInitialization UENUM(BlueprintType) Agent-creation choice: AllocateOnly, Prefill, or DeferAllocation. FTryllKvCacheStatus USTRUCT(BlueprintType) Aggregate KV-cache applicability, residency, reusable-prefix status, eligible-node count, and optional diagnostics. ETryllModelStatus UENUM(BlueprintType) Model lifecycle state returned inside FTryllModelInfo. ETryllErrorCode UENUM(BlueprintType) Mirrors the server error codes.

docs.title: Project Settings — Tryll Client
docs.text:
Set under Project Settings → Plugins → Tryll Client (UTryllRuntimeSettings, persisted to Config/DefaultGame.ini). These drive the auto-launch / auto-connect / auto-create-session flow, so the components above create themselves with no code.

Setting Default Purpose bAutoLaunchServer true Spawn the bundled server on startup. LlamaCppBackend Vulkan llama.cpp GPU plugin (Vulkan / Auto). Passed as --llama-backend. Auto prefers CUDA on NVIDIA and ships CUDA DLLs; Vulkan skips them. Ignored when auto-launch is off. bAutoConnect true Connect once the subsystem initializes. bAutoCreateSession true Create the session from registered models once connected. GameName empty Telemetry grouping slug. StorageDataFolder TryllStorage Project-relative root outside Content/; launcher passes --storage-root. ConnectMaxAttempts / ConnectRetryDelaySeconds 20 / 1.0 Connect-retry policy.

Full per-field detail: UTryllRuntimeSettings.

docs.title: Typical Blueprint flows
docs.text:
First inference — bind OnConnectionChanged on the subsystem, call CreateSession on bConnected=true, wait for OnCreateSessionComplete, then call CreateAgent on the component. See First Inference in Unreal.

Streaming a reply — bind OnAnswerText on the agent component, append Text to your UI widget on each event, show the "done" state on OnTurnComplete. See Stream Answers to UI.

Handling a tool call — bind OnToolCall on the agent component, parse ArgumentsJson, run your game-side logic. The subsystem event is the all-agents form. See Define and Handle Tool Calls.

Speaking NPC — add UTryllSpeakerComponent to the actor alongside UTryllAgentComponent. Download a TTS model in the Model Manager. Use a UTryllWorkflowAsset with a GenerateAndSpeak (or Speak) node, create a Voice Profile asset that names the TTS model, and assign it to the agent component's Voice Profile. Call Set Delivery Mode to make the character sound angry or calm. For mouth movement, add Tryll Lip Sync and turn on Emit Visemes in the voice profile (see Add Lip Sync to a Character). Bind On Tts Audio Started / On Tts Audio Finished on the speaker component for other reactions, and call Stop Playback on it to cut the NPC off. See Add Voice Output to an Agent.

Prepare an NPC during loading — set the component's KV Cache Initialization to Prefill, or call Prefill KV Cache while the agent is idle. Evict KV Cache later to release only LLM context memory; the next Send Message restores it automatically. See Manage an Agent's KV Cache.

Save and load — ExportDialog / ImportDialog are C++ only (the snapshot is not Blueprint-exposed). Store the canonical TDLG bytes in your own save file next to variables and game state. See Save and Load Agent State.

docs.title: UTryllSubsystem::CreateSession
docs.text:
UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category = "Tryll|Session")
void CreateSession(
    FString GameName = TEXT(""),
    FString Locale = TEXT(""),
    bool    bUseProjectLocaleWhenEmpty = true);

The call takes no engine arguments, and it does not choose an engine: each model's catalog entry names the engine that runs it. Protocol v13 replaced the four per-role engine fields with an optional, advisory engines warm-up list. The subsystem still sends that list, built from the Model Manager manifest (UTryllRuntimeSettings::BuildEngineDeclarations()), so the server can start those engines early. It never gates a load.

GameName maps to the same-named UTryllRuntimeSettings field and is the session telemetry slug (and empty-name fallback for --project-name). Storage Data Folder is a launcher setting: the plugin passes --storage-root (default <Project>/TryllStorage/, outside Content/). It is not sent on CreateSession (protocol v24). CreateAgent, CreateEmbeddedStringStorage, and CreateVoiceInput fail fast if a referenced model is not already on disk — acquire models explicitly beforehand via the editor Model Manager.

To configure from the project settings asset instead of passing parameters, call CreateSessionFromSettings() — this runs automatically once connected when UTryllRuntimeSettings::bAutoCreateSession is true.

docs.title: Build a graph in C++
docs.text:
Set node parameters on a params object, then add it to the builder and create the agent from the resulting graph:

UTryllGenerateParams* P = UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeGenerateParams(this);
P->bOverrideModelName    = true;
P->ModelName             = TEXT("qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct");
P->bOverrideSystemPrompt = true;
P->SystemPrompt          = TEXT("You are helpful.");

const FTryllGraphDescription Graph =
    FTryllGraphBuilder()
        .AddNode(TEXT("gen"), P)
        .SetStartNode(TEXT("gen"))
        .SetDefaultModelName(TEXT("qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct"))
        .Build();

Subsystem->RequestCreateAgent(Graph,
    [](TSharedPtr<FTryllAgent> Agent, FTryllError Error) { /* … */ });

The typed AddXxx helpers (AddGenerate, AddRetrieve, …) are generated into TryllGraphBuilder.Nodes.h; AddNode(Name, Params) accepts any node type.

When you drive an agent through UTryllAgentComponent, author the graph as a UTryllWorkflowAsset (Content Browser → Tryll → Workflow Asset) and assign it to the component's Workflow Asset slot. A component cannot create an agent without one.

docs.title: Give an agent a voice
docs.text:
A graph with a Speak or Generate And Speak node needs a voice profile; the server refuses it with AgentVoiceRequired (3025) otherwise. On UTryllAgentComponent, assign a UTryllVoiceProfile asset to Voice Profile. With the subsystem, pass the voice as the trailing argument of RequestCreateAgent:

On a component, enable Voice Delivery to override the profile's default for that agent instance. The dropdown contains neutral and the profile's named modes; changing it also switches a live PIE or Tryll Chat agent.

FTryllVoiceProfileData Voice;
Voice.TtsModelName = TEXT("Pocket TTS (int8)");
Voice.ReferenceVoice.Path = TEXT("voices/mack.wav");
Voice.bEmitVisemes = true;
FTryllDeliveryMode Angry;
Angry.Name = TEXT("angry");
Angry.ReferenceVoice.Path = TEXT("voices/mack_angry.wav");
Voice.DeliveryModes.Add(Angry);

Subsystem->RequestCreateAgent(
    Graph,
    [](TSharedPtr<FTryllAgent> Agent, const FTryllError& Err) { /* ... */ },
    /*bEnableDiagnostics=*/false,
    /*bMaintainDialogueHistory=*/true,
    /*Variables=*/{},
    ETryllKvCacheInitialization::AllocateOnly,
    ETryllWorkload::Interactive,
    Voice);

At runtime, switch the delivery mode (allowed mid-turn, applies from the next sentence) or replace the voice (idle only):

Agent->SetDeliveryMode(TEXT("angry"), /*Intensity=*/0.8f,
    [](const FTryllError& Err) { /* 3024 UnknownDeliveryMode for an undefined mode */ });
Agent->SetVoice(OtherProfile->Voice,
    [](const FTryllError& Err) { /* 3023 InvalidVoiceProfile keeps the old voice */ });

UTryllAgentComponent::SetVoice(UTryllVoiceProfile*) and SetDeliveryMode(Mode, Intensity) wrap these and report through OnVoiceChanged / OnDeliveryModeChanged. ChangeParams cannot reach any voice field.

docs.title: Change a node parameter at runtime
docs.text:
Clone the baseline, set the field's bOverrideXxx flag along with the value, then send. The agent must be idle or paused; OnParamChanged fires on completion:

auto* Base = Cast<UTryllGenerateParams>(AgentComponent->GetNodeParamsBaseline(TEXT("gen")));
auto* Mut  = Cast<UTryllGenerateParams>(UTryllNodeParamsFactory::CloneParams(Base, this));
Mut->bOverrideSystemPrompt = true;
Mut->SystemPrompt          = TEXT("New prompt");
AgentComponent->ChangeParams(TEXT("gen"), Mut);

docs.title: Pause and resume a turn
docs.text:
FTryllAgent::Resume / UTryllAgentComponent::Resume continue a turn suspended at a Pause node or a paused ToolCall. Two events report the pause. UTryllAgentComponent::OnPaused (NodeName, PendingExit) fires for that component's agent only. UTryllSubsystem::OnPaused adds an AgentId and fires for every agent. ChangeParams is allowed while parked:

// Bound to AgentComponent->OnPaused (UFUNCTION on this class).
void AThisClass::HandlePaused(const FString& NodeName, const FString& PendingExit)
{
    // ChangeParams here is allowed — the agent is paused, not busy.
    AgentComponent->Resume(); // empty = continue via PendingExit; or Resume(TEXT("other_node")) to jump
}

See How to pause and resume a turn.

docs.title: Append or remove scripted dialog history
docs.text:
FTryllAgent::AppendInteractions / RemoveInteractionsFromEnd mutate history without running the graph. Strict idle-only (AgentBusy while running, paused, or during a KV-cache operation). Each FTryllDialogInteraction has UserMessage / AssistantMessage — empty strings omit that side; both empty → skipped server-side.

TArray<FTryllDialogInteraction> Seed;
{
    FTryllDialogInteraction Opener;
    Opener.AssistantMessage = TEXT("Welcome, traveler.");
    Seed.Add(Opener);
}
Agent->AppendInteractions(Seed,
    [](uint32 Count, const FTryllError& Err)
    {
        if (Err.IsOk()) UE_LOG(LogTemp, Log, TEXT("Appended %u interactions"), Count);
    });

Agent->RemoveInteractionsFromEnd(1); // drop last whole interaction

See Seed and edit dialog history.

docs.title: Export and import a dialog snapshot
docs.text: FTryllAgent::ExportDialog / ImportDialog capture or replace the completed dialog. These are C++ only — FTryllDialogSnapshot is not Blueprint-exposed. ToFlatBufferBytes / FromFlatBufferBytes produce canonical TDLG bytes; the game owns storage. See Export and import dialog and Save and load agent state.

docs.title: Throttle the GPU and mark background agents
docs.text:
UTryllSubsystem::SetInferenceThrottle (Blueprint-callable, Tryll|Session) reports how hard the server should yield the GPU back to your game — 0.f = full speed (the default for a session that never calls it), 1.f = maximum yielding. Fire-and-forget: no request id, no response, no completion delegate, so calling it from Tick costs nothing but the frame. It never changes what is generated, only how fast.

void AMyGameMode::Tick(float DeltaSeconds)
{
    Super::Tick(DeltaSeconds);
    // Example policy: yield harder as your own frame time worsens.
    const float Pressure = FMath::GetMappedRangeValueClamped(
        FVector2D(11.f, 20.f), FVector2D(0.f, 1.f), DeltaSeconds * 1000.f);
    GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UTryllSubsystem>()->SetInferenceThrottle(Pressure);
}

Agents nobody is waiting on should say so, so their inference is the first to give way. On UTryllAgentComponent this is the Workload property (Tryll|Agent category, editable in the Details panel); in C++ it is the trailing Workload argument to UTryllSubsystem::RequestCreateAgent:

Subsystem->RequestCreateAgent(
    Graph,
    [](TSharedPtr<FTryllAgent> Agent, const FTryllError& Err) { /* ... */ },
    /*bEnableDiagnostics=*/false,
    /*bMaintainDialogueHistory=*/true,
    /*Variables=*/{},
    ETryllKvCacheInitialization::AllocateOnly,
    ETryllWorkload::Background);

Everything else the server classifies from the graph itself, per turn — streamed Generate text is protected, spoken and buffered work absorbs the slack. See Wire Protocol and Server configuration.

docs.title: Read and write Agent Variables
docs.text:
FTryllAgent::GetVariables() returns the Agent Variables mirror. Writes update the local mirror synchronously; the wire update is batched and flushed automatically immediately before the next SendMessage/Resume/ChangeParams call:

FTryllAgentVariables& Vars = Agent->GetVariables();
FTryllError Err = Vars.SetInt(TEXT("level"), 13);
if (!Err.IsOk()) UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("%d: %s"), Err.Code, *Err.Message);
Vars.AddToSet(TEXT("quests_reached"), TEXT("lost_amulet"));
// Optional eager flush (Details "Flush Now" / UTryllAgentVariables::FlushIfDirty):
Vars.FlushIfDirty([](const FTryllError& FlushErr) { /* ... */ });

An unknown name or type mismatch returns a non-OK FTryllError immediately (no wire round-trip), using the same 3013/3014 codes the server would return.

Per-instance Variable Overrides on UTryllAgentComponent use the Material-Instance pattern (see Agent Variables). Details edits live-apply through UTryllAgentComponent::GetLiveVariables() when a PIE agent or Tryll Chat editor-preview agent is attached. Unchecking an override assigns the workflow declaration default. Helpers live in TryllVariableOverrideUtils.

Override flags

Most value fields on a UTryllXxxParams are gated by a bOverrideXxx flag; plain fields such as MinSentenceChars and FirstChunkMaxChars apply directly. (Voice settings are not node params: they live on the agent's voice profile.) For a gated field, set the flag or the value is silently ignored — the node falls back to the graph's default model / authored defaults. The clone preserves the baseline's flags, but set the flag explicitly when you start overriding a field the node didn't author.

Note

The component classes (UTryllAgentComponent, UTryllSpeakerComponent, UTryllLipSyncComponent, UTryllVoiceInputComponent) and project settings (UTryllRuntimeSettings) are also documented in the Blueprint Catalog; per-member detail is on the auto-generated class pages in the sidebar.

docs.title: Workflow Nodes
docs.text:
A Tryll workflow is a graph of nodes, each responsible for one step of the per-turn loop. Sixteen node types ship in the box; together they cover the common patterns of conversational inference (generation, retrieval, intent classification, instructions, detection, fallback, guardrails, composition, routing).

Every producing node below writes its text output into a named slot on the turn's shared blackboard, consumed by downstream nodes via input or by any template's {{slot.<name>}} tag — see Slots and inter-node value passing.

Nodes are referenced by their NodeType name on the wire protocol:

Node NodeType Exit routes Use for Generate Generate default Language-model inference. The workhorse. Generate and Speak GenerateAndSpeak default Fused LLM generation + streaming TTS. Speak Speak default TTS-only; voices its input-resolved slot (default: user_message, like every other input-bearing node). Transform Transform default Model-free: renders a Mustache template into its own slot. No inference, no wire emission — composition/rewriting glue between other nodes. Instruction Instruction default Attach a named instruction slot to the current interaction; rendered by downstream Generate via {{#instructions}} / {{slot.<name>}}. Retrieve Retrieve found, not_found Vector search over a static embedded string storage or an experimental named mutable KB. Write to Memory WriteToMemory written, failed Experimental upsert into a named mutable KB. Place Retrieve before write in the same turn. Classify Intent ClassifyIntent found, not_found Top-1 embedding similarity against a labelled KB; attaches an IntentionComponent for downstream routing. Classify Intent (LLM) ClassifyIntentLLM found, not_found Intent classification via the language model's first-token logprobs. Intent to Instruction IntentToInstruction default Look up the detected intent in a Map string storage and write the matching instruction slot. Tool Call ToolCall tool_called, no_tool_called Detect whether the model wants to call an external tool. Canned Response CannedResponse default Emit a fixed reply from a string storage without calling the model. Regex Guardrail RegexGuardrail triggered, not_triggered Regex-match an input slot (default user_message); branch the graph on pattern hits. Pause Pause default, timeout No-op checkpoint; the executor suspends the turn after this node until the client sends ResumeAgentRequest, or until pause_timeout_ms elapses (0 waits forever). Branch Branch then, else Model-free conditional routing on a turn-local slot or an agent variable — the only node that can read what another node produced this turn. Summarize Summarize default Fold ageing turns into a rolling summary that Generate-class nodes render in their system message, so a long conversation stays coherent at a fixed token cost instead of being trimmed away.

docs.title: Exit-route legend
docs.text:
Every node's reference page lists its named exits. Each exit is a typed string field on the node's params object (e.g. default_exit, triggered_exit). An empty string routes the turn to END (the default); a non-empty string must name another node in the graph. The server rejects graphs where an exit field names a missing node with error 3003 GraphCompilationFailed.

Common patterns:

  • Straight line. Generate → default → END. Minimal single-turn agent.
  • Branch on guardrail. Guardrail → triggered → CannedResponse → END; Guardrail → not_triggered → Generate → default → END.
  • Instruction then generate. Instruction → default → Generate. The instruction's text is exposed as {{slot.<name>}} and {{#instructions}} in the Generate node's Mustache template.
  • Rewrite then retrieve. Transform → default → Retrieve (input set to the Transform node's name) → Generate. See Query rewriting for RAG.
  • Retrieve then generate. Retrieve → found → Generate; Retrieve → not_found → Generate (same target). The not_found path is fine — the projection drops to the user message alone.
  • Tool-call detection. ToolCall → tool_called → END (client handles the tool); ToolCall → no_tool_called → Generate.
  • Intent classification. ClassifyIntent → found → IntentToInstruction → default → Generate; ClassifyIntent → not_found → Generate (general answer, no instruction override). See How to build an intent-driven NPC.
  • Refusal fallback. Generate (hidden classification pass, send=None) → default → Branch (Contains/Equals on the verdict slot) → then → CannedResponse → END; Branch → else → Generate (the real answer) → default → END. Catches a model's own "I can't help with that" or an unsafe verdict without shipping the refusal text verbatim.

docs.title: Params
docs.text:
Every node carries one typed params table, an arm of the NodeParams FlatBuffers union in nodes.fbs (for example GenerateParams or RetrieveParams). A NodeDescription is just a name plus those params; there is no (key, value) parameter list. Each node's reference page lists the fields of its table, their defaults and ranges, and which ones are structural. Tool definitions live on ToolCallParams.tools.

On the wire, the union discriminator is 1-based and follows the order of the NodeParams union (GenerateParams = 1 … SummarizeParams = 16). Client NodeType enums are 0-based, so a client enum value is one lower than the wire discriminator for the same node.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: When the agent is created with enable_diagnostics = true, every node contributes to TurnComplete.debug_info. Each node's reference page has a Diagnostics section listing the keys it records; the payload that holds them — the envelope, the shared prompt and engine sections, and the rules for when a key is omitted — is documented in Turn Diagnostics JSON. See also agent parameters — diagnostics.

docs.title: Branch Node
docs.text:
NodeType = Branch (NodeParams union discriminator 14)

A model-free routing node. It runs no inference, writes no slot, and never emits anything on the wire — the same cost class as Pause and Transform. It picks one of seven tests, evaluates it against a single operand (a turn-local slot or an agent variable), and takes then_exit or else_exit.

Use it to route on a value produced this turn — generated text, a Transform result, or a canned seed — which no other node can inspect (see Slots and inter-node value passing). Agent variables are the other operand under Expression, not the subject: the model proposes a value, live game state judges it (for example, checking a generated action against a currently-allowed set). If the whole predicate is over variables the game already knows the answer before the turn starts — prefer a different graph, ChangeAgentParam, or Pause + Resume(resume_node) in that case. See docs/research/workflow/conditional-routing-if-and-switch-nodes.md for the design rationale.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Param Type Default Range Structural Localizable Description test BranchTest BranchTest.NonEmpty — — — Which predicate to run. Changing this recompiles the active condition. input str empty -> "user_message" — ✓ — Slot discriminant. Empty = "user_message". Mutually exclusive with a non-empty variable. Unused under test=Expression. variable str empty — ✓ — Variable discriminant (name of a declared agent variable). Mutually exclusive with a non-empty input. Unused under test=Expression. values list[str] empty list — — — Candidate literals for Equals / EqualsIgnoreCase / Contains / Regex. Match = any element matches. Unused under NonEmpty / IsTrue / Expression. Mutable — the game can remap cases between turns without recreating the agent. condition str (multiline) empty — — — JSON filter condition used when test=Expression. Supports the retrieve filter grammar plus {"slot":"<name>"} operands. Unused under other tests. notify_client bool False — — — When true, fire OnNodeEvent("branch_taken", …) after routing.

docs.title: Exits
docs.text:
Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

Exit Param field Description then then_exit Exit taken when the test matches (or Expression is true). Empty = END. else else_exit Exit taken when the test does not match, Expression is false, or the operand is missing. Empty = END.

docs.title: Test modes
docs.text:
input and variable are mutually exclusive — set at most one; an empty input (the default) resolves to user_message. Every test but Expression reads that single resolved operand; Expression instead evaluates condition against slots and variables directly. Fields the active test doesn't use are ignored (logged at debug, never an error) — this is deliberate: input/variable are structural, so a mutation that flips test cannot also clear them.

Test Reads Needs Trim / case NonEmpty (default) resolved operand nothing else Operand trimmed of ASCII whitespace before the check; a set<string> variable checks element count instead of text IsTrue variable only a declared bool variable — rejected at Create on a slot operand or a non-bool variable n/a (boolean value, not text) Equals resolved operand values (≥ 1) Operand trimmed; byte-exact comparison against each values element. values entries themselves are never trimmed — a trailing space typed into one can never match EqualsIgnoreCase resolved operand values (≥ 1) Same as Equals, both sides ASCII-folded Contains resolved operand values (≥ 1) Operand trimmed; substring match against each values element, case-sensitive Regex resolved operand values (≥ 1, each a regex pattern) Operand trimmed; std::regex_search — matches anywhere in the operand, not a full-string match; case-sensitive, diverging from RegexGuardrail's hardcoded case-insensitive matching, because Equals vs EqualsIgnoreCase already makes case explicit in the test name Expression slots/variables named inside condition non-empty condition The filter grammar's own operand rules apply per-operand; trim for a {"slot":…} operand happens in Branch's slot-binding step (not in the shared evaluator), so a trailing space in a rendered slot never blocks a match. See Filter grammar

lt/le/gt/ge inside an Expression condition never accept a {"slot":…} operand — slots type as String and ordering requires a numeric type on both sides.

NonEmpty on an Int/Float/Bool variable, and a text test (Equals/EqualsIgnoreCase/Contains/Regex) on a StringSet variable, are rejected at Create — the former is a constant predicate (dead exit), the latter should use Expression's in operator against the set instead.

docs.title: Exit routes
docs.text:
Exit Condition then The active test matched (or Expression evaluated true). else The test did not match, Expression evaluated false or Undefined, or a simple-mode operand was missing.

Simple-mode missing operand → else, always, and it short-circuits before the test runs. A slot the graph never wrote on this path, or a variable that somehow resolves to nothing, counts as missing. Without the short-circuit, test=Equals, values=[""] would route a missing slot to then (find("") == 0); the short-circuit makes that impossible. This is logged at debug, not warn — for a routing node this is the common case, not an anomaly.

Expression missing slot → equation is Undefined → else + warning. A {"slot":…} the graph never wrote makes the filter result Undefined (Kleene three-valued logic — see Filter grammar). Branch treats Undefined like false for exit selection (else), but logs a warn and sets diagnostics operand_missing=true. Prefer a positive in(slot, allowed) with then = allowed / else = blocked: a missing slot then fails closed to blocked. Do not rely on not(eq(...)) / not(in(...)) to treat missing as a match — those stay Undefined too.

A slot that was written but is blank ("") is present, not missing — producing nodes still write their slot even when generation or rendering failed, so "absent" almost always means that node didn't run on this path, not "it ran and produced nothing".

Branch can never fail a turn: regexes and the Expression condition are pre-validated at Create/mutation time, so evaluation itself is noexcept.

docs.title: Side effects
docs.text: None. Branch is reader-only: it does not write a slot, call a model, or emit answer text. Set notify_client = true to observe routing mid-turn via NodeEvent("branch_taken", {exit, test, operand_kind, matched_value}) — the payload deliberately omits the operand's raw text, since NodeEvent has no diagnostics content-trait gating.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
When enable_diagnostics = true, this node contributes to debug_info.nodes[].diagnostics. See Turn Diagnostics JSON for the envelope.

Branch runs no model, so it emits parameters and output only. This is the block that answers "why did it go that way" — the operand text it actually compared is here and nowhere else.

Key Meaning Absent when parameters.test The test mode that ran: Equals, Contains, Regex, Expression, … — parameters.operand_kind What was read: slot, variable or expression. — parameters.operand_name Name of the slot or variable read. Empty for Expression. — parameters.values_count How many candidate values were configured. 0 for Expression. — parameters.condition The compiled filter expression, as JSON. The test mode is not Expression. parameters.notify_client Whether a branch_taken event was emitted. — output.exit The exit actually taken. — output.matched Whether the test matched. — output.matched_index 0-based index into values. -1 when no indexed value matched — including every Expression branch. — output.matched_value The configured value that matched. Empty for Expression. — output.operand_missing true when the slot or variable was never written — the case that logs a warning and falls to else. — output.operand_text The operand's raw text as compared. —

operand_missing: true and an empty operand_text are the signature of the missing-slot trap described above. An operand that was written but blank shows operand_missing: false with an empty operand_text — a different problem, in a different node.

notify_client does not gate this block

notify_client controls only whether the client receives a branch_taken event. Routing is recorded here either way.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
A refusal-fallback gate: a hidden classification Generate produces a one-word verdict, and Branch routes "UNSAFE" to a canned refusal while everything else reaches the real answer.

PythonC++Unreal 
from tryll_client.graph import (
    GraphDescription, GenerateParams, BranchParams, BranchTest,
    CannedResponseParams, SamplingOverrides, SendAnswer, HistoryRole,
)

graph = (
    GraphDescription()
    .add_node("classify", GenerateParams(
        send=SendAnswer.None_, history_role=HistoryRole.None_, output_name="verdict",
        system_prompt="Answer with exactly one word: SAFE or UNSAFE.",
        sampling=SamplingOverrides(temperature=0.0, seed=42),
        default_exit="gate",
    ))
    .add_node("gate", BranchParams(
        test=BranchTest.Contains, input="verdict", values=["UNSAFE"],
        then_exit="refuse", else_exit="answer",
    ))
    .add_node("refuse", CannedResponseParams(
        inline_strings=["I'd rather not go there."], send=SendAnswer.Whole, default_exit="",
    ))
    .add_node("answer", GenerateParams(send=SendAnswer.Streamed, default_exit=""))
    .set_start_node("classify")
)
agent = client.create_agent(graph)

# Remap the trigger word at runtime — `values` is mutable.
# Structural fields must still match create-time values.
agent.change_params("gate", BranchParams(
    test=BranchTest.Contains, input="verdict", values=["SAFE"],
    then_exit="refuse", else_exit="answer",
))

using namespace Tryll::Client;
using namespace Tryll::NodeParams;

GenerateParamsT classifyP;
classifyP.send          = Tryll::SendAnswer_None;
classifyP.history_role  = Tryll::HistoryRole_None;
classifyP.output_name   = "verdict";
classifyP.system_prompt = "Answer with exactly one word: SAFE or UNSAFE.";
classifyP.sampling      = std::make_unique<SamplingOverridesT>();
classifyP.sampling->temperature = 0.0f;
classifyP.sampling->seed        = 42;
classifyP.default_exit  = "gate";

BranchParamsT gateP;
gateP.test      = Tryll::BranchTest_Contains;
gateP.input     = "verdict";
gateP.values    = { "UNSAFE" };
gateP.then_exit = "refuse";
gateP.else_exit = "answer";
// Keep a caller-owned baseline before moving into the graph — AddBranch
// takes ownership, so reading gateP after the move is undefined.
BranchParamsT gateBaseline = gateP;

CannedResponseParamsT refuseP;
refuseP.inline_strings = { "I'd rather not go there." };
refuseP.send           = Tryll::SendAnswer_Whole;
// default_exit left empty = END

GenerateParamsT answerP;
answerP.send = Tryll::SendAnswer_Streamed;
// default_exit left empty = END

GraphDescription graph;
graph.AddGenerate("classify", std::move(classifyP))
     .AddBranch("gate", std::move(gateP))
     .AddCannedResponse("refuse", std::move(refuseP))
     .AddGenerate("answer", std::move(answerP))
     .SetStartNode("classify")
     .SetDefaultModelName("My Local Model");

auto agent = client.CreateAgent(graph);

// Remap the trigger word at runtime — `values` is mutable. Use the
// Async form from a reader-thread callback to avoid deadlocking.
BranchParamsT newGateP = gateBaseline;
newGateP.values = { "SAFE" };
agent.ChangeParamsAsync("gate", std::move(newGateP));

#include "Generated/TryllGraphBuilder.Nodes.h"
#include "Generated/TryllNodeParamsFactory.h"

UTryllGenerateParams* ClassifyP = UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeGenerateParams(this);
ClassifyP->Send          = ETryllSendAnswer::None;
ClassifyP->HistoryRole   = ETryllHistoryRole::None;
ClassifyP->OutputName    = TEXT("verdict");
ClassifyP->SystemPrompt  = TEXT("Answer with exactly one word: SAFE or UNSAFE.");
ClassifyP->DefaultExit   = TEXT("gate");

UTryllBranchParams* GateP = UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeBranchParams(this);
GateP->Test     = ETryllBranchTest::Contains;
GateP->Input    = TEXT("verdict");
GateP->Values   = { TEXT("UNSAFE") };
GateP->ThenExit = TEXT("refuse");
GateP->ElseExit = TEXT("answer");

UTryllCannedResponseParams* RefuseP = UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeCannedResponseParams(this);
RefuseP->InlineStrings = { TEXT("I'd rather not go there.") };
RefuseP->Send          = ETryllSendAnswer::Whole;

FTryllGraphDescription Graph = FTryllGraphBuilder()
    .AddNode(TEXT("classify"), ClassifyP)
    .AddNode(TEXT("gate"),     GateP)
    .AddNode(TEXT("refuse"),   RefuseP)
    .AddNode(TEXT("answer"),  UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeGenerateParams(this))
    .SetStartNode(TEXT("classify"))
    .SetDefaultModelName(TEXT("My Local Model"))
    .Build();

See the test-chat branch workflow (test-chat/src/workflows/BranchWorkflow.cpp) for the runnable version — /agent branch — and the QA scenarios scenarios.protocol.branch_routing (the Contains example above) and scenarios.protocol.branch_expression (the Expression / allowlist form, gating a generated action against a live set<string> variable).

docs.title: Canned Response
docs.text:
The Canned Response node emits a fixed reply chosen from a string storage according to its selection_strategy, and ends its turn without invoking a language model. Use it for scripted answers, refusal lines, and branches where you do not want the cost or variability of a generation pass.

NodeType: CannedResponse. Changing string_storage to a name that cannot be loaded, or to empty, returns 3007 InvalidParamValue and leaves the previous responses in force.

String storage kinds

CannedResponseNode accepts any string storage kind (List, Map, Multimap) and uses the list view — values are iterated by position. Key-aware selection (picking a response by a runtime intent key) is planned as future work.

For intent-driven response routing today, use IntentToInstructionNode to inject a tone directive and let the Generate node produce the response.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Param Type Default Range Structural Localizable Description string_storage str empty — — — Named session string storage. Mutable — rebinds the underlying storage. inline_strings list[str] empty list — ✓ — Inline response list. Structural because it materialises the underlying StringStorage at construction. selection_strategy CannedResponseSelectionStrategy CannedResponseSelectionStrategy.RoundRobin — — — How the next canned response is chosen from the storage list. output_name str empty — ✓ — Name this node's output slot is stored under. Empty = the node's own name. Structural: immutable after creation — renaming would re-wire the slot dataflow that is validated once at agent creation. send SendAnswer SendAnswer.Whole — — — Controls answer-text delivery to the client. history_role HistoryRole HistoryRole.Assistant — — — Controls whether/how this node's slot replays in later turns' projected transcript.

docs.title: Exits
docs.text:
Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

Exit Param field Description default default_exit Default exit target after emitting a canned response. Empty string = END.

Source resolution

Priority order: 1. string_storage as a relative file path under the process storage root (loaded on demand at CreateAgent time). 2. string_storage as the name of an explicitly created session storage (via CreateStringStorageRequest). 3. inline_strings authored inline (virtual / session-scoped). 4. Server default file (default_canned_responses_path in server-config.json).

docs.title: Exit routes
docs.text: Route Fires when default Always — the node never branches. Set default_exit to another node name to continue, or leave it empty to terminate the turn (END).

docs.title: Side effects
docs.text:
• Appends the chosen response to the current turn as the assistant's reply.
  • Emits one AnswerText frame (non-streaming: is_delta = false, is_final = true) with the full response.

No model inference, no KV-cache work, no network I/O beyond the AnswerText frame itself.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
When enable_diagnostics = true, this node contributes to debug_info.nodes[].diagnostics. See Turn Diagnostics JSON for the envelope.

No model runs, so the node emits a parameters section only.

Key Meaning Absent when parameters.string_storage Name of the storage the response came from. Empty for a storage registered inline rather than by name. — parameters.string_count How many responses the storage holds. — parameters.last_index 0-based index of the response chosen this time. With round_robin this is the cursor that advances turn to turn. — parameters.selection_strategy first, round_robin or random. —

The text that was actually emitted is not repeated here — read it from the node's SlotComponent in the turn's interaction snapshot, or from the answer itself.

docs.title: Classify Attributes (LLM)
docs.text:
The Classify Attributes (LLM) node scores several specialist questions in one cached batched call. Each attribute is its own prompt, the same first-token letter menu as Classify Intent (LLM), and the node writes one slot per attribute. Any attribute whose own rule fires takes triggered; otherwise the node takes default. NodeType: ClassifyAttributesLLM (union ordinal 17).

There is no shared-prompt mode. Empty system_prompt selects a kind-specific default. Choice and Score templates must reference {{intents_block}}. A Boolean template must also reference {{statement}}. history_turns defaults to 0. context_size 0 sizes the window from the rendered prompts. The node forces a unified KV cache and one sequence per attribute plus the dialog sequence. temperature 0 means 1.0 for every attribute.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Param Type Default Range Structural Localizable Description model_name str empty — ✓ — Model catalog name. Structural because the token-ID mapping is built from the model's vocabulary at construction. context_size int 0 -> auto ≥ 0.0 ✓ — KV-cache window in tokens. 0 = size from the rendered specialist prompts plus a per-attribute tail budget, else the classify default. attributes list[ClassifyAttributeDef] empty list — — — The attributes to classify. 1-16 entries, unique names. Shape, name, kind and choice id/prompt are structural; the hand-written Apply allows statement, prompt, decision and trigger edits. input str empty — ✓ — Slot name this node consumes. Empty = "user_message". history_turns int 0 0.0 – 64.0 — — Dialog turns included before the current user text. Default 0 until history quality is measured. temperature float 0.0 0.0 – 8.0 — — Softmax temperature for every attribute. 0 = 1.0 (identity). on_failure AttributeFailureRoute AttributeFailureRoute.Default — — — Exit taken when scoring fails. notify_client NotifyClient NotifyClient.Disabled — — — When to fire OnNodeEvent("attributes_classified", …). OnFound means the triggered exit was taken. output_name str empty — ✓ — Slot namespace. Empty = node name. context ContextOverrides unset — ✓ — Backend context construction. The node derives n_seq_max and n_outputs_max from the attribute count. Structural. adaptation ModelAdaptation unset — ✓ — Changes how the model behaves for this node (LoRA adapters; later control vectors). Null = base model. Structural: applied to the llama context at creation, so a change means a new context. Appended last so existing field IDs do not move.

docs.title: Exits
docs.text:
Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

Exit Param field Description default default_exit Exit taken when no attribute triggers. Empty string = END. triggered triggered_exit Exit taken when any attribute triggers, or when on_failure is Triggered and scoring fails. Empty string = END.

LoRA adapters

adaptation.loras runs this node's model with one or more fine-tuned LoRA adapters, each with a scale. See Use a LoRA Adapter for where to put the file and how to tune the scale.

docs.title: Kinds
docs.text:
Kind Slot value Trigger Choice Winning choice id. Below threshold or margin, the slot is uncertain_choice: a real choice id, or the reserved #uncertain The written choice's triggers flag. #uncertain never triggers Boolean "true" when P(A) ≥ threshold, else "false". The menu is fixed: A = True, B = False boolean_trigger: Never, True, or False Score Normalised expected level (Σ i·p_i)/(N−1), four decimals in 0.0000…1.0000 score_trigger against score_threshold in 0..1: Never, AtOrAbove, or Below

Choice needs 2–26 options. uncertain_choice names one of them, or the reserved #uncertain. #uncertain is not a letter in the menu. A real id rewrites an uncertain call to that choice and uses its triggers flag, including when that choice wins outright. #uncertain writes that token and stays on default. Boolean takes a statement and no choices. Score takes 2–26 levels from low to high; choice triggers must stay false. A score of 0.7 means 70% of the way from the lowest level to the highest, not the probability of the top level. Recalibrate any threshold that used to compare a raw level index.

triggered_exit must be set exactly when at least one attribute can trigger. Empty input never triggers and takes default. If scoring throws or the result shape does not match the attributes, every slot gets its fallback (Choice uncertain_choice, Boolean "false", Score "0.0000") and the node follows on_failure (default or triggered). There is no third exit.

docs.title: Slots, diagnostics, and the event
docs.text:
Each attribute writes <output_name>_<name> (output_name empty means the node name). Diagnostics output.classification carries status (ok, empty_input, failed), triggered, and attributes[] with name, kind, value, status, triggered, and choices[] of {id, prob, triggers}. Choice also reports top and second probability. Boolean reports p_true and p_false. Score reports expected_level, score, and entropy confidence. Probabilities are measurements, not a contract to pin in a golden file.

notify_client Always emits attributes_classified on every scored turn. OnFound emits it only when the triggered exit is taken. The payload is a flat string map: exit, status, per-attribute kind/value/status/triggered, prob.<choice_id>, and triggered_by.

Shape, name, kind, and choice id/prompt are structural. Statement, prompt, thresholds, margins, and trigger flags can change after creation.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Python 
from tryll_client._generated.node_params import (
    AttributeKind,
    BooleanTrigger,
    ClassifyAttributeChoice,
    ClassifyAttributeDef,
    ClassifyAttributesLLMParams,
    ScoreTrigger,
)
from tryll_client.graph import GraphDescription

graph = GraphDescription()
graph.add_classify_attributes_llm("attrs", ClassifyAttributesLLMParams(
    history_turns=0,
    default_exit="reply",
    triggered_exit="hold",
    attributes=[
        ClassifyAttributeDef(
            name="topic",
            kind=AttributeKind.Choice,
            choices=[
                ClassifyAttributeChoice(id="world", prompt="ordinary story talk"),
                ClassifyAttributeChoice(id="meta", prompt="about the software", triggers=True),
            ],
            uncertain_choice="world",
        ),
        ClassifyAttributeDef(
            name="software",
            kind=AttributeKind.Boolean,
            statement="The message is about software or instructions.",
            boolean_trigger=BooleanTrigger.True_,
        ),
        ClassifyAttributeDef(
            name="hostility",
            kind=AttributeKind.Score,
            choices=[
                ClassifyAttributeChoice(id="calm", prompt="no insult or threat"),
                ClassifyAttributeChoice(id="violent", prompt="a threat of harm"),
            ],
            score_trigger=ScoreTrigger.AtOrAbove,
            score_threshold=0.7,
        ),
    ],
))

Graphs authored against the proof-of-concept fields (independent_prompts, choice_ids, code_style, context.kv_unified, context.flash_attn) do not load. Move each specialist prompt onto the attribute, put triggers on the choice that should take triggered_exit, and drop the shared-prompt knobs.
