  • ToolCall reports the tools it offered. Turn diagnostics now include a flattened echo of the tool signatures the model actually saw, one line per tool plus a line per described parameter — so "why didn't it call my tool" is answerable from the inspector. See Tool Call.

docs.title: Storage and packaging
docs.text: • Project-relative storage folders in Unity. StorageDataFolder accepts a path relative to the project root (e.g. Assets/StreamingAssets/StorageData), which the client absolute-ifies in the editor and rewrites onto Application.streamingAssetsPath in a player build. One value works in both, with no runtime code of your own. Note the prefix match includes the trailing slash — keep a subfolder in the path, or it resolves next to the executable and breaks only in a shipped build. See Ship storage folders for builds.

docs.title: New and expanded documentation
docs.text:
• Design an NPC prompt — measurement-backed recipes for a role-play system_prompt: give the character one line of their own dialogue, never label your example lines, keep the rule list short, name what you are banning, control length with a length rule — plus what we tested and found no effect from, and how model choice changes the answer.
  • Build an immersion guard — a three-stage guard (pattern, general, world) that keeps out-of-character and out-of-world player lines away from the NPC, drops the rejected turn from history, and hides its own latency.
  • TTS Models — the two shipped voices and the full family support matrix, including which families cannot be loaded and why. Check this before adding any voice.
  • Docs for AI coding agents. Both plugins ship an AGENTS.md at their root carrying the graph/slot mental model and the ways Tryll differs from a cloud LLM SDK — attach it to Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or Codex before asking for Tryll code. Agents that fetch docs themselves can start from llms.txt on the docs site.
  • The site was restructured. The how-to guides are grouped into ten task areas with a collapsible sidebar to match, the reference splits into Client API (what your code calls) and Workflows and data (what you declare), concepts are ordered as a reading path, and release notes are now one page per version. The home page and Getting Started also state the real hardware requirements up front.

docs.title: Breaking changes and behavior changes
docs.text:
• RetrieveParams gained fields mid-table — rebuild every client. retrieval_mode and rrf_k were inserted before the existing source / filter / exit fields. FlatBuffers vtable slots are positional, so a client built against the v0.5.0 schema talking to a newer server (or the reverse) would decode subsequent fields into the wrong slots. Rebuild your integration against the new schema and upgrade both ends together; mismatched peers are rejected at connection time with 5004 ProtocolVersionMismatch. See Wire Protocol and Retrieve.
  • Telemetry now defaults to off, not on. If you relied on the previous default being enabled, enable it explicitly. See Telemetry.
  • The per-component diagnostics authoring checkbox is retired. Chat and the Agent Log now request diagnostics per-create through a transient override and a shared lease, so observing an agent no longer means editing — and dirtying — the component or asset. The runtime and wire fields are unchanged; remove any workflow that toggled the authored checkbox to get diagnostics.
  • Inline graphs are deprecated. TryllAgentComponent.InlineGraphDescription and InlineVariables are temporary and will be removed in a future release. Author the graph as a Workflow Asset, declare its variables there, and assign it to WorkflowAsset; the Inspector now warns when no asset is assigned. Building a TryllGraphDescription in code and creating an agent from it directly — with no component — remains fully supported. See TryllAgentComponent.
  • Unity voice input now waits for the session. TryllVoiceInputComponent previously created its handle on the raw TCP connect edge, before session creation completed, so the microphone silently failed to come up on first play. It now gates on session readiness and re-drives creation when the session completes, matching the agent component and Unreal. No API change; the failure just stops happening.
  • Unity Chat snapshots variable overrides at Start. Editing a component's variable overrides while a Chat agent is running does not reach that agent — press Stop then Start to pick up new values. Unreal differs deliberately: it keeps a transient preview link that applies edits live. See Test an agent in the editor.

docs.title: v0.7.0
docs.text:
This release makes an agent's dialog persistable and its language, placement, and voice something you choose. A full-fidelity dialog snapshot drops into the save file you already own, one session language drives speech, recognition, content files, and prompt directives together, and every model can be told whether its weights belong in RAM or VRAM. A pause can now time out instead of soft-locking an agent, two expressive SNAC voices (Orpheus and Maya1) join the public catalog with natural-language voice direction, and tool calling gains measured model rankings, prompt recipes, and in-editor testing. Memory stops being a guess — a Memory window in both editors reports the server's live RAM and VRAM with a confidence tier on every figure — and LLM intent classification graduates: described labels instead of a labelled corpus, a visible Intent block in the turn inspector, and Lab checks that assert the label a turn resolved.

The four engine dropdowns are gone, components now require a Workflow Asset, and the schema changed — see Breaking changes and behavior changes before upgrading.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Save and load agent dialog. Export a full-fidelity snapshot while an agent is idle, store the canonical TDLG bytes inside your own save container, and import it into a fresh session with Strict compatibility. Tryll still writes no save files. See Save and load agent state.
  • One session language for the whole stack. Set a BCP-47 locale and speech output, speech-recognition hints, per-language content files, and the {{language}} prompt keys all follow it — changeable mid-session without tearing the session down. See Ship an agent in another language.
  • Choose where each model runs. Per-model RAM / VRAM placement, authored in the Model Manager or passed when you load a model yourself. A hint by design: a machine that cannot honour it loads the model the other way and reports what it actually did. See Choose where models run.
  • Engines come from the catalog. The four engine dropdowns are gone from Project Settings in Unity and Unreal. The catalog records which engine runs each model — which also fixes model listing showing no STT, TTS, or embedding models in a project that never touched those settings.
  • Pauses can time out. pause_timeout_ms gives a Pause a deadline and timeout_exit lets the character answer anyway, instead of an unanswered pause leaving the agent busy forever. The server also warns when a pause outlives its stall threshold.
  • Two expressive voices, plus voice direction. Orpheus 3B FT (Q4_K_M) and Maya1 3B (i1-Q4_K_M) are public catalog voices, and tts_voice_description / tts_delivery_instruction let you brief a voice's identity and its delivery in natural language. See TTS Models.
  • Fit a whole cast on one GPU. A guide to the two levers that actually decide whether five NPC agents fit in limited VRAM — sizing every LLM node's context_size, then evicting the agents nobody is talking to. See Run many agents on a small GPU.
  • Tool calling, measured. Exact-accuracy tables for the catalog on game-shaped suites and a BFCL slice, schema and prompt recipes that survived those sweeps, and a way to exercise a ToolCall workflow in the editor without Play/PIE. See Compare tool-call models and Design a tool-call prompt.
  • See what the server is actually using. A Memory window in Unity and Unreal reports live RAM and VRAM for the whole server process — resident models, per-agent KV, and the part nobody can attribute — with a confidence tier on every figure, so an estimate never reads as a measurement. See Inspect server memory.
  • Intent classification without a corpus. Describe each intent in a sentence and ClassifyIntentLLM routes the line off its own first-token logprobs — no embedding model, no labelled knowledge base, nothing to ship — with a measurement-backed prompt guide, an Intent block in the turn inspector, and Dialog Lab checks that assert the accepted label. See Classify intent without a knowledge base and Design an intent-classifier prompt.
  • Classifier and tool-call nodes size their own window. ClassifyIntentLLM and ToolCall now default to 2048 tokens instead of inheriting a generator-sized 8192 — the cheapest VRAM saving in the release, and it needs no authoring.

docs.title: Save and load
docs.text:
• ExportDialog / ImportDialog on every client. Both are strict idle-only — no turn running, not paused, no KV-cache operation in flight. Export returns a DialogSnapshot; ToFlatBufferBytes / FromFlatBufferBytes (encode_flatbuffer / decode_flatbuffer in Python) produce the canonical TDLG bytes. Import replaces the whole dialog and is atomic: a failed import leaves the existing dialog untouched. Unreal exposes this in C++ only — the snapshot is not Blueprint-exposed. See Export and import dialog.
  • The snapshot is dialog, and only dialog. Not agent variables, not UI transcripts, not KV-cache bytes, not agent IDs. The save-slot pattern — quiesce every agent, snapshot each one alongside variables and game state, recreate the agents in a fresh session, import, then warm the ones you actually need — is written up end to end in Save and load agent state. Import never prefills; call PrefillKvCache yourself during the loading screen.
  • Strict by default. Import checks the snapshot against the agent's create-time graph and refuses a mismatch; AllowGraphMismatch opts out. Snapshots that would overflow the 1 MiB frame cap fail rather than being truncated.
  • Unity coroutine wrappers. TryllAgentCoroutines wraps export, import, variable sync/flush, and KV prefill: it retries AgentBusy at a polite interval and bounds every wait with a wall-clock deadline, so a dropped connection fails your save UI with Timeout instead of hanging it.

docs.title: One language for the session
docs.text:
• locale on CreateSession, and SetSessionLocale after it. A BCP-47 tag (de, pt-BR, zh-Hans-CN) that becomes the default tts_lang on every GenerateAndSpeak / Speak, the language hint handed to multilingual STT models, the per-language file lookup, and the locale / language / language_code Mustache keys. Empty leaves every one of those at its previous behavior; a malformed tag is rejected with 2004 InvalidLocale. Unity and Unreal add a Project Settings → Tryll Client → Language picker that lists only what your registered models can serve.
  • Translations live beside the file you link. A loc/<language>/ folder next to a linked storage file supplies the translated version — deathonset/loc/pt-BR/lore.json, then loc/pt/, then the file you linked. You always link the default file; a folder with no loc/ is language-neutral; and fallback is per file, so a partially translated game works. This covers knowledge bases and their sidecars, canned responses, guardrail patterns, intent maps, hotwords, and reference-voice WAVs.
  • {{language}}, {{locale}}, {{language_code}} in templates. Available wherever Mustache rendering is — Generate, GenerateAndSpeak, ToolCall, Transform. The section collapses to nothing when no language is set, so one template works localized and unlocalized.
  • A helper for the offerable set. ListModels reports a languages list per model, and TryllLanguages (Unity) / UTryllLanguages (Unreal, Blueprint-callable) intersect them across your pipeline. HasLanguageInfo tells "no overlap" apart from "the catalog didn't say" before you show a player an empty menu.
  • A mid-session switch is not retroactive. Speech output, the template keys, and the next file load follow it from each agent's next turn; a knowledge base, canned lines, or classifier prompt already bound to a node does not — those are structural. Send the change between turns, not mid-sentence.
  • tts_lang resolution is now layered: the node's own value, then the session locale, then the model's catalog default. Set the node param only to override one character — a French witness in a German playthrough.

docs.title: Models: placement, engines, and GPU backend
docs.text:
• memory_placement per model. Auto / RAM / VRAM, authored on a registered model in the Model Manager or passed when you load a model yourself. The reason to reach for it: your renderer and Tryll's language model compete for the same VRAM, and moving a large model to RAM trades generation speed for graphics headroom. It is a hint on purpose — you author it on your machine and ship it to someone else's.
  • load_model() reports what happened. The Python client returns a result carrying placement and backend instead of None, so a VRAM request that could not be honoured is visible rather than guessed at. Purely additive — existing calls that ignore the return value are unaffected. Unity and Unreal log a warning naming both placements and the backend; their completion events keep their (model name, success) signatures, because a model cannot be moved after it loads.
  • The session declares engines as a hint, not a gate. CreateSession takes an optional list of the (role, engine) pairs you expect to touch, replacing the four engine arguments. It may be empty, incomplete, or wrong, and loading a model it never named works normally. What it buys is timing: engine start-up is paid at session creation instead of on first use — worth asking for when a backend is slow to initialise. See Choose where models run.
  • Pick the llama.cpp GPU API in Project Settings. Tryll Client → Llama.cpp backend (Vulkan default, or Auto), passed to an auto-launched server as --llama-backend. A Vulkan player build skips the CUDA DLLs; Auto copies them and prefers CUDA on NVIDIA. Standalone / C++ / Python set engines.llama_cpp.backend in server-config.json (committed default "vulkan") or pass the flag. Players need neither the CUDA Toolkit nor those DLLs on PATH, and speech and embedding stay on the CPU package. See Auto-launch the server and Server configuration.
  • Shared model assets. The SNAC 24 kHz decoder is the first: it has its own download record, is pulled once for whichever parent needs it, and survives deleting a parent model. ListModels reports ModelStatus.Incomplete when a parent is waiting on a shared asset, with dependency details. The catalog also gained dependencies and structured tts_capabilities (voice presets, inline tags). See Model Management.
  • Fixed: telemetry reported the wrong GPU backend. gpu_backend_active was read from build-time flags that are never set in our builds, so every install reported cpu — including machines where Vulkan was serving every token. It now reads the live device registry. If you have been comparing performance data across machines, the backend field in older data is not trustworthy.

docs.title: Fitting a cast on one GPU
docs.text:
• Run many agents on a small GPU — the two levers, in the order worth pulling. A KV cache is allocated at its full context_size the moment the context is created, so the cost is deterministic, short replies save nothing, and a sizing change is measurable in seconds rather than in playtests. Then evict the agents nobody is talking to. Worked through with numbers from a five-agent, nine-context demo on a 16 GB card.
  • ClassifyIntentLLM and ToolCall now default to a 2048-token window. Left at 0, they no longer inherit the model variant's context_size or the server's default_n_ctx (commonly 8192) — the two nodes whose prompts are small got the small default. Generate and GenerateAndSpeak are unchanged, so budget per node: a classifier at 2048 is a small slice of an 8192 generator. See Estimate memory footprint.
  • A per-node context table, for when the window itself is the problem. Generate, GenerateAndSpeak, ClassifyIntentLLM and ToolCall take an optional structural context table: kv_cache_type per context (overriding the catalog's model-load default, with Inherit keeping it), a veto-only offload_kqv, and escape-hatch batch sizes. Leave it unset unless you are tuning a large window — at a right-sized 2048 a q4_0 KV override is usually not a measurable VRAM win, because the dtype delta only shows up around 8192. See Models and inference engines.
  • The sizing trap is silent. When a prompt exceeds its window, the token-budget projection trims the oldest turns and keeps working — so an under-sized classifier quietly loses the history it needs to resolve "And that one?". Leave headroom, and re-check that intents still fire after tightening one.
  • An immersion guard costs two extra contexts per agent. Build an immersion guard now says so up front and points at the sizing guide before you add one to a project already close to its VRAM budget.
  • Memory estimates cover SNAC voices. llama.cpp SNAC voices are GGUF backbones that follow the same RAM/VRAM placement as a language model, plus a ~50 MB CPU decoder — unlike Sherpa STT/TTS, which stay RAM-only. See Estimate memory footprint.

docs.title: Memory inspection
docs.text:
• A Memory window in both editors. Window → Tryll → Memory in Unity, Window → Tryll → Tryll Memory in Unreal: resident models, per-agent KV, and the unattributed remainder, on demand. Refresh only — no poll, no graph. It reuses the shared editor session and auto-launches the bundled server the way Model Manager does, needs no agent, and does not wait for registered models to download. Closing it releases the lease without killing the server. See Inspect server memory.
  • The snapshot is server-wide, not per-connection. Every session on that process is in the numbers — Chat, Model Manager, Play-in-Editor, a Python client, your QA harness. A row you do not recognise is not a bug in the window. That is the opposite of the Agent Log, which sees only your own connection.
  • Every figure carries a confidence tier. Measured (the engine or the OS said so), Derived (computed from measured inputs), Estimated (a calibrated band, rendered with a leading ~ and an estimate basis on hover). The column is always visible on purpose: an estimate must never look like a measurement.
  • What the tables actually answer. Devices split into ours / other / free, and other is the editor and the compositor rather than a Tryll leak. KV is listed per agent, sorted background-first, with evicted and never run called out separately — background KV is the reclaim signal, because nobody is waiting on it. Context used is headroom to the limit, not memory growth: the buffer is allocated at the full context_size the moment the context is created. And memory-mapped model files are resident pages Tryll never allocated, so a VRAM-placed model often surfaces under unattributed instead of its own RAM column — the window says so when that happens.
  • GetMemoryConsumption on every client. TryllClient::GetMemoryConsumption (C++), client.get_memory_consumption() (Python), RequestGetMemoryConsumptionAsync (Unity), and UTryllSubsystem::RequestGetMemoryConsumption (Unreal C++, with a Blueprint completion event to bind) all return the same snapshot. Session-scoped — it must follow CreateSession — but the numbers cover the whole process, and it never fails with AgentBusy.
  • The server monitor gained the matching panel. Same collector, same numbers, over GET /api/memory; the browser view keeps its sparkline and stacked bars, which the editor window does not have. monitor.memory_tick_interval_ms sets the live sampling interval — 0 disables periodic sampling and the panel still loads on demand. See Server configuration.

docs.title: Voice output
docs.text:
• Orpheus and Maya1 are public catalog voices. Orpheus 3B FT (Q4_K_M) gives eight named English speakers (speaker_id 0–7) plus inline tags such as <laugh>; Maya1 3B (i1-Q4_K_M) takes a natural-language voice description, with two catalog presets as a starting point. Both download through the normal Model Manager, including the shared SNAC decoder. Heavier quants stay internal.
  • tts_voice_description and tts_delivery_instruction. Two new mutable params on GenerateAndSpeak and Speak: a stable speaker identity (age, accent, pitch, timbre) and a sustained delivery direction for this synthesis call. They are independent of tts_voice (a reference WAV) and speaker_id (a preset index) — four distinct knobs, and square-bracket [emotion] text is not a supported control. Model-native <tag> tokens that a catalog lists may reach the synthesizer; unknown tags are stripped from the audio copy only and never rewrite history.
  • A control the model does not advertise now fails instead of being silently ignored — Orpheus and Maya1 reject a speed other than 1.0. The full per-family control matrix, and the attribution each set of weights requires, are in TTS Models.
  • Unity: ask the speaker whether it is still talking. TryllSpeaker gains HasPendingAudio (true while decoded audio is still queued) and StopPlayback(). Combined with TurnComplete, HasPendingAudio is the signal a hands-free voice loop needs before re-opening the microphone, so the mic does not transcribe the tail of the character's own answer. AudioSource.isPlaying is not that signal — the streaming clip loops silence between turns. See TryllSpeaker.

docs.title: Turn control
docs.text:
• pause_timeout_ms on Pause. 0 still waits forever. A finite budget makes the failure recoverable: with timeout_exit authored the graph continues from that exit and the turn ends normally; without it the turn ends with TurnStatus.PauseTimedOut, keeping the partial interaction so the conversation stays intact. Prefer authoring a timeout_exit for anything player-facing, so the character says something. Both params are structural.
  • The deadline is server wall-clock. A minimised or alt-tabbed game stops pumping its main thread, so the deadline can elapse while your game is suspended. Make the timeout branch harmless — "shrug and answer without the tool" — rather than something that only makes sense the instant it fires.
  • pause_timeout_ms on ToolCall covers pauses that node triggers, inheriting the server's workflow.tool_call_pause_timeout_ms when left at 0. There is no timeout exit on this node — expiry ends the turn.
  • An unresumed pause is loud before it is fatal. The server logs a warning naming the parked node once a pause outlives workflow.pause_stall_warn_ms (15 s by default), and your client logs one immediately when nothing it holds can resume the pause at all.

docs.title: Tool calling
docs.text:
• Compare tool-call models — exact accuracy for the catalog across seven game-shaped suites and a BFCL slice, at greedy decoding. The two corpora do not rank models the same way, so the page is built for choosing by job (commands, log queries, parallel calls) rather than for crowning a winner. Models whose tool_call_support is unsupported are rejected at agent creation and are not in the tables.
  • Design a tool-call prompt — measurement-backed schema and prompt recipes. The headline finding: small models fail at restraint, not extraction. Give "the player did not narrow this down" a real enum value, list it first, and mark the parameter required — the value a pressured model reaches for becomes the right answer. Claims are marked Tested / Hint / no effect, so you can skip what did not pay off.
  • Test tool calls in Chat and the Dialog Lab — register a handler on the scene agent component in edit mode, talk to it in Chat, then script Lab runs with canned results or against the live handler. No Play/PIE.
  • Dialog Lab live tools are opt-in. A Lab step with no canned ToolResults entry still means the model must not call that tool, even when the variant's scene agent has a RegisterTool handler. Tick Use live tools on the variant only when the run should exercise it; canned results still win. See Compare dialog variants in the Lab.
  • Diagnostics answer "why didn't it call my tool". parameters.tools[] echoes the signatures the model actually saw, output.tool_calls[] carries each detected call with its raw arguments, output.parse_fallback flags a call the native template parse missed, and engine.chat_turn.has_grammar shows whether require_call actually constrained the sampler. See Tool Call.

docs.title: Intent classification
docs.text:
• notify_client is now a three-state enum. Disabled / OnFound / Always on ClassifyIntent and ClassifyIntentLLM, replacing the bool. Always also fires on every not_found path, carrying not_found_reason and the rejected top-1 — which is how you see a deflection that didn't happen.
  • Typed callbacks, and a separate LLM event. ClassifyIntentLLM now emits its own intent_llm_classified event with the full probability vector, subscribed via SetOnIntentLlmClassified / IntentLlmClassified / OnIntentLlmClassified / set_on_intent_llm_classified. Both classification callbacks now take a structured event object instead of a positional argument list. A typed subscriber swallows the generic OnNodeEvent fallback.
  • Richer classification diagnostics. The embedding classifier records ranked topk[] candidates, the winner, and a runner_up with its margin — the number to watch when a classifier is unstable, because a margin near zero means small rewordings will flip the route. The LLM classifier records the label ids in letter order alongside the probability vector.
  • ClassifyIntentLLM without a knowledge base, end to end. Classify intent without a knowledge base rebuilds the gate-guard NPC with one language model and no corpus: a sentence per intent, no embedding pass, nothing on disk. It opens with a table for choosing between the two classifiers — many intents and pre-labelled data still favour embedding ClassifyIntent; a label set you are still designing favours this one, because writing a sentence is a far shorter loop than authoring twenty phrases and rebuilding an index.
  • system_prompt is a Mustache template, and there is no default. It renders against exactly two variables — {{intents_block}} (the letter-prefixed label list) and {{letters}} — and none of the Generate variables (user_message, slot.<name>, var.<name>, instructions, knowledge) resolve there. Leave it empty and the node sends an empty system message: the model is asked for a letter having never been shown what the letters mean, and nothing fails loudly. A template that fails to parse is sent verbatim, literal {{intents_block}} included. Verify the substitution in input.prompt[] after any edit. See Classify Intent (LLM).
  • Design an intent-classifier prompt — claims marked Tested / Hint / no effect, like the NPC and tool-call prompt guides. The mechanism decides what matters: the node reads the logits at the end of the prompt and never generates, so "think step by step", "explain your reasoning" and "answer in JSON" are paid for in prefill and then discarded unread. What pays off is mutually exclusive descriptions — overlap is the top cause of a collapsed margin — an explicit catch-all placed last, because models carry strong, model-specific positional bias over the answer letter and that bias has to be re-checked when you change classifier models, and tuning threshold only after the overlap is fixed.
  • intents_ids and intents_prompt, spelled out. intents_prompt is the text the model reads, rendered as A. <first>, B. <second>, …; intents_ids is never shown to it and only supplies the label attached on a win. They pair positionally — entry 0 is letter A — must have equal counts and 2–26 unique ids, and each letter must be a single token for that model. A comma inside a description silently becomes an extra label, so use dashes or semicolons. All of it is validated at agent creation.
  • An Intent block in the turn inspector. One subsection per classifier execution, with the decision in the header — ask_wing · found, or not_found · below_threshold — and not_found coloured as a warning rather than an error, because it is usually correct behaviour. Embedding classifiers get the funnel line, a winner card or the rejected pick, and a top-k table that dims rows beyond the threshold; LLM classifiers get a probability bar per candidate and the predicted_letter / top_prob / second_prob / margin_result strip, with the winning or rejected label shown in words so you never map a letter by hand. notify_client does not gate the block — a classifier left at Disabled still appears, it just produces no Agent Log event. See Turn Inspector.
  • Dialog Lab can assert the label. Intent is passes when an addressed classifier on that turn accepted the exact id; Intent not found passes only when every addressed classifier took not_found. Leave the node name empty to address every classifier that ran, or name one to scope the check. Labels compare exactly and case-sensitively — they are identifiers, not prose. A missing or mis-typed classifier fails with intent unavailable rather than skipping, so a green suite cannot come from a classifier that never ran, and seeded steps refuse these checks before Run: a seeded turn is injected without running the graph, so there is no classification to assert. See Compare dialog variants in the Lab.
  • A rejected pick is now recorded. Both classifiers add output.classification.rejected_intent — the label the scorer or the search chose when routing rejected it — and the embedding node adds rejected_distance beside it, which is what turns a bare not_found into "it wanted ask_wing, at 0.31, against a 0.25 threshold". The classified text is now input.query on both kinds (output.classification.query is kept for one release), and the LLM probs[] vector is documented as positionally aligned with parameters.intents_ids[], equal length on found.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
• Turn Diagnostics JSON — a new reference for the whole TurnComplete.debug_info payload: the envelope, the per-node parameters / input / output / engine sections, the turn-level tool-call and interaction snapshots, and the rules for why a given key is absent. Every node reference page now carries a Diagnostics section listing the keys it records.
  • The turn inspector's Raw JSON is verbatim. The editors add no keys, rename none, and drop none — so the reference above describes exactly what you see in the panel and exactly what arrives on the wire. Raw JSON is also the one block the Route breadcrumb's node scope does not narrow; it always shows the whole turn. See Turn Inspector.
  • Two server flags trim the payload. include_engine_diagnostics drops the engine sections and include_interaction_in_diagnostics drops the end-of-turn interaction snapshot — which is why the inspector's tool-call block can show calls with no results.

docs.title: Server operations
docs.text:
• Log flushing is configurable. log_flush_on (default "warn") flushes the log file as soon as a message at that level or higher is written, and log_flush_every_ms (default 5000) flushes on a timer so a quiet server does not leave the file minutes behind. A running server's log is now readable without waiting for process exit. See Server configuration.
  • Startup states standalone vs managed idle-exit. The server logs Standalone mode: server will not self-exit or Managed mode: self-exit after <N>s of idle right after logging starts, instead of announcing the mode only when --idle-shutdown-timeout was on the command line.
  • Fixed: a managed server could finish its idle exit and never actually leave. An open monitor event stream kept the HTTP listener from shutting down, so the process stayed alive with both the game port and the monitor port refusing connections — Dialog Lab then failed with "the target machine actively refused it" and would not relaunch. Subscribers are now closed before the listener is joined, and the Unity and Unreal launchers treat an owned process that is alive but no longer accepting as dead and start a fresh one.

docs.title: Editor fixes
docs.text:
• Chat honors a cleared Agent Component. Clearing the Chat window's Agent Component (or Voice Component) to None now sticks. Start and Compare in Lab refuse with the usual assign warning instead of silently restoring the previous scene object.
  • Dialog Lab shows the seed it actually uses. Typing 0 into Repeats or base seed still raises the value to 1 (seed 0 means random on the wire). The field now displays 1 instead of keeping the typed 0.

docs.title: Breaking changes and behavior changes
docs.text:
• The schema changed — rebuild every client. CreateSession, the TTS nodes, the classification nodes, the pause params, and the LLM nodes' new context table all changed shape this release, and a server-wide memory snapshot call was added. Rebuild your integration against the new schema and upgrade both ends together; mismatched peers are rejected at connection time with 5004 ProtocolVersionMismatch. See Wire Protocol.
  • ClassifyIntentLLM and ToolCall default to a 2048-token context. With context_size left at 0 they previously fell back to the model variant's window, then the server's default_n_ctx — commonly 8192. Most projects simply get the VRAM back; a node whose classifier prompt or tool-schema block genuinely needs more than 2048 tokens must now set context_size explicitly. Generate and GenerateAndSpeak are unchanged, and context_size is structural, so this is a graph edit rather than a runtime one. See Run many agents on a small GPU.
  • ClassifyIntentLLM has no built-in system_prompt, and an empty one fails quietly. Every client leaves the field empty by default and the node passes it through verbatim, so an unauthored classifier sends an empty system message and asks the model for a letter whose meaning it was never shown. Author a template containing {{intents_block}}. See Design an intent-classifier prompt.
  • A component now requires a Workflow Asset. TryllAgentComponent.InlineGraphDescription / InlineVariables and UTryllAgentComponent::InlineGraphDescription / InlineVariables are removed — deprecated in v0.6.0, gone now. Author the graph as a Workflow Asset and assign it; declare variables on the asset. Building a TryllGraphDescription in code and creating an agent from it directly — TryllClient.RequestCreateAgentAsync / UTryllSubsystem::RequestCreateAgent, with no component — remains fully supported. If you still want a component around a code-built graph, put the graph on a transient Workflow Asset (ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<TryllWorkflowAsset>() / NewObject<UTryllWorkflowAsset>()) and assign that. See TryllAgentComponent and Unreal C++ API.
  • The four engine dropdowns are gone, and nothing replaces them. Unity's InferenceEngine / SttEngine / TtsEngine / EmbeddingEngine runtime settings and Unreal's Engine / SttEngine / TtsEngine / EmbeddingEngine project settings are removed; the session's engine set is derived from the models you registered. If you build sessions by hand, the four engine arguments are replaced by one optional engines list. This also fixes a real bug: three of the four defaulted to Mock and ListModels filtered by them, so a project that never touched them saw no STT, TTS, or embedding models in the Model Manager at all. Model listing is now engine-agnostic.
  • notify_client is an enum, not a bool. ClassifyIntent and ClassifyIntentLLM take Disabled / OnFound / Always; the old true becomes OnFound. The IntentClassified callback signature changed to a structured event object on every client, and ClassifyIntentLLM now reports through the separate intent_llm_classified event — code that relied on intent_classified firing for an LLM classifier must subscribe to the new one.
  • Unity RemoveInteractionsFromEnd reports the count. Its completion callback is now Action<uint, TryllError> (was Action<TryllError>), matching AppendInteractions.
  • enable_diagnostics is structural. It is fixed for the agent's lifetime and cannot be turned on for an agent that already exists. The editor tooling handles this for you — Chat enables it on the agent it creates, and the Agent Log holds a lease so agents created while it is open request it too. See Agent Parameters.
  • device_preference is removed from models.json. A catalog that still declares it fails to load, with a message naming the replacement (memory_placement). Every shipped entry said "auto", so it decided nothing; "directml" was accepted there and never implemented, and is gone too.
  • engines.llama_cpp.n_gpu_layers is deprecated and ignored. It applied one value to every model in the process, which cannot be right once different models want different memory. Offload is now decided per model from its placement. A server that still finds the key warns once at startup — remove it.
  • Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 is replaced by v3. Update model_name in any voice-input config; the v2 entry is no longer in the catalog.
  • Dialog Lab live tools are opt-in. A variant whose scene agent has a RegisterTool handler no longer exercises it implicitly — a step with no canned ToolResults entry asserts that the model must not call that tool. Tick Use live tools on the variant to restore handler execution. See Test tool calls in Chat and the Dialog Lab.
  • loc is a reserved folder name inside storage folders. Do not use loc/ for your own content; it is the per-language lookup root. If your build pipeline filters what gets staged, make sure it keeps **/loc/** — a missing translation folder degrades silently to the default language rather than failing the build. See Ship storage folders for builds.

docs.title: New error codes
docs.text:
• 2004 InvalidLocale — CreateSessionRequest.locale (or a later SetSessionLocale) is not a well-formed BCP-47 tag. Expected language[-script][-region]; the message names what was wrong.
  • 3017 ModelLanguageUnsupported — a node would rely on the session language but its model does not support it. Pick a model that covers the language, set the node's own tts_lang, or change the session locale. Not raised when the model declares no languages at all.
  • 3018 DialogSnapshotInvalid — the snapshot is malformed, missing required fields, or has inconsistent tool call / result data. Import leaves the existing dialog unchanged.
  • 3019 DialogFormatUnsupported — the snapshot's format_version is newer than this server, or the file identifier is not TDLG.
  • 3020 DialogGraphMismatch — Strict import: the snapshot's graph signature does not match the agent's create-time graph.
  • 3021 DialogSnapshotTooLarge — the encoded snapshot would overflow the 1 MiB frame cap. Tryll never truncates.
  • 3022 DialogUnsupportedComponent — an unknown component type on export, or an unknown union arm on import.

See Error Codes for the full list.

docs.title: v0.8.0
docs.text:
This release is about characters that remember and characters you can watch talk. A new Summarize node folds old turns into a rolling summary, so a long conversation keeps its thread instead of being trimmed away. Experimental mutable knowledge bases let an agent write what it learns into a named store, retrieve it later, and save it with the game. A server-side viseme track drives lip sync on ARKit faces in Unity and Unreal, and on MetaHumans. Voice turns are now sent by your client, hotword biasing works on the models that support it, and Japanese, Chinese and other scripts that put no space after a full stop now start speaking mid-answer. The server also gains deployment modes, one process-wide storage root, and a user model catalog that survives updates.

Voice input, intent events, storage folders, model management and node parameter validation all changed, and the schema changed. See Breaking changes and behavior changes before upgrading.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Long conversations stay coherent. Put a Summarize node last in a graph. Turns older than a hot window are folded into a rolling summary that every generating node reads. The cost per turn stays fixed, and nothing the player said is silently trimmed. See Keep long conversations coherent.
  • Agents that write their own memory (experimental). Named, session-scoped knowledge bases that a graph writes with WriteToMemory and reads with Retrieve. Your client can query and edit them, and they save with the game. A Knowledge window in both editors lets you inspect them.
  • Lip sync. emit_visemes on GenerateAndSpeak streams a viseme track aligned to the audio. TryllLipSync (Unity) and Tryll Lip Sync (Unreal) play it on ARKit blendshapes, and a separate plugin drives MetaHuman faces. See Add lip sync to a character and Add lip sync to a MetaHuman.
  • Hotwords that actually bias recognition. A per-model Hotword biasing switch, per-phrase scores, and a clear list of the STT models that support it. A lexicon given to a model with biasing turned off now fails with an error instead of doing nothing. See Bias voice input with hotwords.
  • Speech starts sooner, in more languages. Sentence ends in CJK, Devanagari, Arabic, Urdu and Ethiopic scripts now close a TTS chunk. Before this, a Chinese or Japanese reply stayed silent until the model had finished writing. The new first_chunk_max_chars parameter shortens the wait for the first audio on any voice.
  • Add your own models without editing the shipped catalog. Point the project at a user catalog file and it survives every Tryll update. A broken user catalog is skipped instead of stopping the server. See Use your own local model.
  • Deployment modes and one storage root. The server runs as Tryll Dev, Client Dev or Client Prod, and storage, models, logs and saves each resolve from one process-wide root. Unity and Unreal keep that content in <Project>/TryllStorage/, outside Assets/ and Content/. See Server configuration.
  • Per-NPC events. Tool-call, intent, pause and node events now fire on the agent itself, so each NPC can listen for its own events without filtering by agent id.

docs.title: Long conversations
docs.text:
• New Summarize node. Place it last in a graph. When trigger_tokens (default 1024) or trigger_turns is crossed, it folds every interaction older than keep_recent_turns (default 3) into a summary of at most max_summary_tokens (default 256). Every Generate-class node in the agent then renders that summary as untrusted dialogue data and replays history only from the fold boundary. A large backlog is folded in chronological chunks.
  • It runs beside the character, not as the character. The node uses its own context (context_size 0 resolves to 2048) on the agent's default model and an instruction-only prompt, never the persona. It never emits answer text. Summary tokens count toward TurnComplete.tokens_generated. system_prompt and template are overridable, and set notify_client for a summarized event.
  • The summary is part of the dialog snapshot. ExportDialog / ImportDialog carry it, so a saved conversation resumes with its summary intact. Turn diagnostics record each fold, or the reason one was skipped.
  • Keep long conversations coherent walks through choosing the trigger and the hot window. Projection and token budgets explains where the summary sits in the prompt.

docs.title: Memory and saves (experimental)
docs.text:
• Named mutable knowledge bases. EnsureMutableKb gets or creates a session-scoped store under a schema registered in data/schemas.json. The handle writes, deletes, clears, queries, lists, reports stats, and exports or imports one store. C++, Python, Unity and Unreal all ship handles. Every write is embedded straight away, so the first write to a new store and eager loads are slow.
  • WriteToMemory upserts from a graph. It writes its input slot to storage_name, with an optional per-turn id template, and exits written or failed. Empty input is a no-op that still exits written. Put a Retrieve before the write if the model should see what was already there.
  • Retrieve reads a named store. Set source_kind to name mode and give storage_name and schema in place of embedded_string_storage. {{var.npc_id}}-style store names resolve at agent creation, which is how each NPC gets its own memory from one shared graph. Unity's [TryllSchema] picker lists the registered schemas. See Retrieve.
  • Game memory and dialog files. SaveGameMemory / LoadGameMemory write and read every store at once as a text-only TMKB file, and vectors are rebuilt on load. LoadGameMemory takes an explicit Now or Lazy embed timing. SaveDialog / LoadDialog write dialog to a file and carry your save_id. A later load warns when the memory and dialog files came from different saves. See Save and load agent state.
  • The process owns where saves land. Save paths resolve through the server's saves settings (enabled, root, allow_absolute_paths) or --disable-saves / --save-root / --allow-absolute-save-paths. A relative path joins saves.root, or the storage root if no save root is set. Unity and Unreal auto-launch allow absolute paths, and a player build passes persistentDataPath / ProjectSavedDir() as the save root (or Save Data Folder from Project Settings). See Server configuration.
  • A Knowledge window in both editors. Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Knowledge (Unity) and Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Tryll Knowledge (Unreal) show stores on the left (with ensure and session save/load), records in the middle (Filter or Query), and write, delete, clear and per-store TMKB export/import on the right.

docs.title: Lip sync
docs.text:
• emit_visemes on GenerateAndSpeak. Off by default and mutable. When on, the node sends one viseme event per synthesized sentence: 15 Oculus visemes timed in samples from the start of that node's audio. Speak does not emit visemes. See TTS and voice output.
  • Unity: TryllLipSync. Add it next to a TryllSpeaker and it drives ARKit blendshapes from the viseme track against the speaker's playback clock, compensating for output latency. It exposes Intensity, smoothing and attack/decay, BindFace(), and live status for debugging. TryllAgent.OnTtsVisemes exposes the raw events. See TryllLipSync.
  • Unreal: Tryll Lip Sync component. UTryllLipSyncComponent drives ARKit morph targets on non-MetaHuman faces. It has Blueprint-callable SetIntensity and BindFace, and pose and settings structs you can author. The speaker gains GetOutputLatencyMs and OnTtsVisemes. See the Blueprint catalog.
  • MetaHuman lip sync (Unreal, separate plugin). TryllMetaHumanLipSync drives a MetaHuman face either from Epic's realtime speech-to-animation model (Neural, the default) or from Tryll's viseme track (Viseme). It is off by default, and it needs a one-time Set Up in Project Settings before Play or packaging will run. See Add lip sync to a MetaHuman.
  • C++ and Python receive the same events through SetOnTtsVisemes / set_on_tts_visemes (TtsVisemeEvent).
  • The Agent Log shows the voice track. TTS format and TTS visemes rows appear in the timeline beside the text. See Use the Agent Log.

docs.title: Voice output
docs.text:
• Sentence splitting understands more scripts. CJK, Devanagari, Arabic, Urdu and Ethiopic sentence ends close a chunk without a following space, and closing quotes stay with their sentence. … counts as a full stop. min_sentence_chars is now a width: a CJK character counts as two, so the default of 12 is about six CJK characters. A number such as 3.14 is no longer split after the 3.. Text that never ends a sentence is cut at a 16 KiB cap, with a warning.
  • first_chunk_max_chars on GenerateAndSpeak and Speak. Default 0 (off). When set, only the first chunk may also end at a comma, semicolon, colon or em dash, and it is cut at the next space once it reaches that width. It never cuts before 5 words or min_sentence_chars. 48 reduced the model-side wait before the first audio by about 40% in our measurements. Listen to it with your own voice first, because a clause can end on a falling tone. See Speak and Generate and Speak.
  • Raw PCM for your own audio pipeline. TryllSpeaker.OnTtsPcm (Unity) and UTryllSpeakerComponent::OnTtsPcm (Unreal) hand you every decoded buffer, for example to feed your own spatializer. The Unity speaker also exposes OnTtsFormat, ConsumedSamples and QueuedSamples. See TryllSpeaker.
  • Unity speaker fixes. A TryllAgentComponent with an empty Speaker slot now reuses the TryllSpeaker already on the GameObject instead of adding a second one, which also left a lip-sync component following a silent speaker. A speaker that is disabled and re-enabled now plays again.
  • speed is checked the same way at creation and at runtime. ChangeAgentParam now enforces the 0.1–3.0 range too, as CreateAgent already did.

docs.title: Voice input
docs.text:
• Your client sends the voice turn. The server now only transcribes. On UtteranceFinal, send the text yourself with SendText, send_message_async, or the agent component's SendMessage. Unity and Unreal voice components do this for you when a target agent is set, and drop the final if that agent already has a turn in flight. In Python, use send_message_async from the transcript callback, because the blocking send_message deadlocks on the reader thread. See Use voice input.
  • Hotword biasing you can switch per model. The Model Manager has a Hotword biasing control (Default / Off / On) on STT models. In code, pass hotword_hints (Python) or placementHints with .hotwords (C++) to CreateSession. The shipped catalog turns biasing on for Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3.
  • Better lexicons. Write plain words, one phrase per line. Append :<score> to boost a single phrase. Pretokenized lexicons still work. The default hotwordsScore stays 1.5, and the guide's recommended ranges moved up. Transducer and streaming Zipformer models support hotwords, but CTC-family models do not. An unsupported model now logs a warning at voice-input creation instead of ignoring the lexicon silently. See Bias voice input with hotwords.
  • Unity voice component sets hotwords. TryllVoiceInputComponent gains hotwordsStoragePath (a Storage Data Folder file picker; leave it empty to disable) and hotwordsScore. See TryllVoiceInputComponent.

docs.title: Intent classification
docs.text:
• ClassifyIntentLLM takes an intents array. Author id/prompt pairs as entries (ClassifyIntentEntry in Python, TryllClassifyIntentEntry in Unity, FTryllClassifyIntentEntry in Unreal), so a description can contain a comma. The comma-separated intents_ids / intents_prompt pair is deprecated and kept for one release. If intents is empty, the node falls back to it. Setting both is a graph-creation error. Unreal binary assets were not migrated, so copy the values out of the inspector to use the array. See Classify Intent (LLM).
  • The classifier prompt is checked up front. system_prompt must be a Mustache template that parses and references {{intents_block}}. Otherwise CreateAgent and ChangeAgentParam fail, where previously the template was sent anyway and classification quietly broke. {{letters}} is now optional. See Design an intent-classifier prompt.

docs.title: Tool calling
docs.text:
• Tool Call diagnostics say why a parse failed. When output.parse_fallback is true, output.parse_failure reports whether the model attempted a call and got the syntax wrong (malformed_call), answered in prose (no_call), or used a chat template that declares no call marker to check against (unclassified). output.parse_error gives the parser's reason and the byte where it stopped. The Unity and Unreal turn inspectors show both under the parse-fallback chip. See Tool Call diagnostics.
  • Fix tool-call text in answers. What to check when a reply shows raw tool-call markup such as <|tool_call>… instead of dialogue: a speech node told to call a tool on a turn that skipped ToolCall, an unparsed call sent under mode = call_or_answer, or leaked replies replaying from history.
  • Unity: async tool handlers. RegisterTool on TryllAgent / TryllAgentComponent accepts Func<TryllToolCall, Task<string>>. The paused batch is held until every handler completes on the main thread, and results that already succeeded are kept across a retry. Synchronous handlers are unaffected.
  • Dialog Lab treats a tool-call mismatch as a check failure. A missing, unexpected or wrong-name call now completes the turn as an amber CheckFail with its diagnostics, and the rest of the script keeps running. See Test tool calls in Chat and the Lab.

docs.title: Retrieval
docs.text: • Query rewriting and HyDE for RAG. A second rewrite recipe writes a short hypothetical passage instead of a keyword query (HyDE). It works better when your knowledge base stores statements rather than questions. The page includes a table for choosing between the two recipes by how your chunks are written, and advice on re-checking threshold and keeping a Keywords: line for Hybrid retrieval.

docs.title: Models and catalogs
docs.text:
• User model catalog. Set Project Settings → Tryll Client → Custom Models → Catalog (Unity) or Project Settings → Plugins → Tryll Client → Models (Unreal) to a JSON file inside the project. You can also call TrySetUserModelsCatalogPath / SetUserModelsCatalogPath before the server launches. Setting it while an auto-launched server is running restarts that server. A packaged game stages the file under Server/data/user-catalog/, with relative chat templates beside it. A standalone server takes user_models_catalog_path / --user-models-path or a models.d folder (--user-models-dir), and tryll_server --check-catalogs validates them. A broken user file is skipped, and a duplicate name loses to the shipped entry. See Use your own local model and Model Management.
  • Runtime model management is explicit. When a model must be acquired: call RequestDownloadModel, wait for a successful OnDownloadComplete, then call RequestLoadModel. Call RequestLoadModel alone to pin a model that is already staged, or create the agent and let the server load on demand. See Pin and unpin models.
  • A broken models.json stops the server. A missing file, a parse error, or the retired device_preference key now exits the server with an error, the same way a broken server-config.json already did. Before, it logged a warning and served an empty catalog.

docs.title: Server, storage and deployment
docs.text:
• Deployment modes. --mode (or the mode key) selects tryll-dev, client-dev or client-prod. The mode sets the default roots, the log file, whether models can be downloaded, and which developer features run. The monitor, debug commands and STT debug dumps work only in Tryll Dev. Client Dev and Client Prod refuse to start without a config file. Unity and Unreal auto-launch the server in Client Dev. See Run the Tryll server and Server configuration.
  • One storage root per process. Relative storage paths resolve against --storage-root / storage_root, or the mode's default. Models and logs follow --models-root / models_root and --log-dir / logs_dir. The session no longer carries a storage folder, and ConnectionReady reports the server's mode.
  • TryllStorage in Unity and Unreal. Storage defaults to <Project>/TryllStorage/, outside the engine asset folders. Unity copies it into StreamingAssets/Tryll/ in the build output. Unreal stages it next to the packaged project, so you no longer need Additional Non-Asset Directories to Copy. See Ship storage folders for builds.
  • Client Dev logs per project. Each run writes one log file under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Tryll\projects\<project-key>\logs\, not inside the plugin package. The deployment mode, not log_mode, now picks the file name: a per-run tryll_<timestamp>.log in Tryll Dev and Client Dev, a rotating tryll.log in Client Prod. Crash dumps always go to the logs folder.
  • Usage telemetry in Client Dev. Host ID, hardware inventory and session-started events always send in Client Dev. Activity telemetry is a separate lane (activity_enabled, default true). See Telemetry.

docs.title: Client APIs
docs.text:
• Events per agent. Unity TryllAgent / TryllAgentComponent and Unreal UTryllAgentComponent raise tool-call, intent, pause and generic node events for that agent only, with the payload alone (ToolCallDetailed, IntentClassified, IntentLlmClassified, Paused, NodeEvent and the tool-call variants in Unity, and their On… counterparts in Unreal). Bind these when you care about one NPC. The session events remain the all-agents surface. A typed listener suppresses only its own scope's generic NodeEvent. See TryllAgentComponent and the Blueprint catalog.
  • Unity: code-created agents receive their own answers. TryllAgent has public SetOnAnswerText, SetOnTurnComplete, SetOnError, SetOnTtsAudioFormat and SetOnTtsAudio, matching C++, Unreal and Python. Register them before SendMessage, and pass null to clear. TryllSpeaker.HandleFormat / HandleAudio are public, so you can wire playback without a component. See TryllAgent.
  • Unity and Unreal error enums list every server code. TryllErrorCode / ETryllErrorCode are now generated from the server's list, so new codes appear without a client release lagging behind.
  • Unity/Unreal: an oversized request fails on its own. A command too large to send now fails that request with 5003 FrameTooLarge (or 3021 DialogSnapshotTooLarge for a dialog import), and the connection stays up.
  • Unity/Unreal: an empty send is not a turn. SendMessage("") does nothing, so a leftover empty string never reaches the server as a malformed request.
  • Unreal plugin builds on UE 5.8 as well as 5.7. Play-in-Editor still waits for the model check and resumes when it passes.
  • Play-in-Editor pause warning. If no OnPaused is bound, a pause nothing can resume now logs its warning in PIE, and the subsystem's OnNodeEvent receives paused events. Previously the editor's own subscription hid both.

docs.title: Agentic coding
docs.text:
• Agentic coding with Tryll. How to have an AI coding agent build Tryll agents: AGENTS.md, and prompt advice from real runs.
  • Tryll MCP plugin (Unreal 5.8). A separate TryllMCP plugin, off by default, gives an AI coding agent four tools through the Unreal editor's MCP server: describe node types, and validate, write and read a whole workflow asset. It requires Epic's experimental Model Context Protocol and Toolset Registry plugins.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text:
• Chat voice input is one menu. Off, Chat (Chat owns speech-to-text) or Actor component. Unity drives the scene TryllVoiceInputComponent in Play Mode. Unreal copies that component's STT model, VAD and hotwords into Chat's own handle, so it works without PIE. Unity push-to-talk with a Voice Component no longer sticks, and a quick release no longer starts the microphone after the utterance has ended. See Test an agent in the editor.
  • One status bar and banner across every window. Chat, Model Manager, Memory, Dialog Lab, Agent Log and Knowledge show connection state the same way. A dropped connection or failed session offers Retry. Failed model loads, unloads, downloads and Dialog Lab import errors appear on an inline banner. Destructive confirms stay as dialogs.
  • Windows follow the host editor theme, including Unity's light skin. Chat bubbles match Dialog Lab, and status colours are the same in every window.
  • Layouts persist. Inspector and list widths, the Model Manager columns (now resizable), and the Unity Dialog Lab and Agent Log settings survive an editor restart and stay with the project. Collapsing an inspector no longer saves a zero width or leaves a gap.
  • Chat and Agent Log follow the tail only when you are near the bottom, so scrolling up mid-stream no longer jumps back on every token.
  • Model Manager opens even when registered models are missing. It lists the catalog first, then prompts you to download.
  • Fixes. Restoring several Tryll windows at once no longer wedges Chat on a duplicate session. The Unity Memory and Agent Log windows no longer throw on editor start. Entering Play in Unity with an editor window connected now logs a reconnect warning instead of a socket-thread crash. Dialog Lab per-variant agents keep their assignment across a scene unload. Unreal icons that rendered as empty boxes are fixed.
  • The Unreal TryllUnrealDemo project packages again after the editor saves it. Its .uproject description had a non-ASCII dash. When the editor rewrote the file, which it does on its own or on an engine-version switch, it saved it as UTF-16. UnrealBuildTool then failed on byte 0 with JsonReaderException: '0xFF' is an invalid start of a value, and packaging and project-file generation both stopped. The descriptor is now ASCII-only. A copy from an earlier release that already shows this error needs re-saving as UTF-8 without a BOM, in any text editor. A version-switch copy can also be left with an engine GUID in EngineAssociation; set it back to your version, such as "5.8". Keep your own .uproject and .uplugin text ASCII-only for the same reason.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Tryll in Ten Minutes is the new starting point: what Tryll is, why it runs on the player's machine, agents as workflows, the building blocks, and how a team works with it. Architecture at a Glance becomes the engineer's view.
  • Docs are versioned. Each minor release is published under /vX.Y/ with a version switcher. The plugin version is in package.json, the .uplugin, or AGENTS.md.
  • Samples compile against the current API. Every CreateSession sample is free of the engine arguments that v0.7.0 removed, and the C++, Python, Unity and Unreal graph samples use the real builder and parameter types.
  • Corrections that may change how you integrate. The code did not change in these cases; the earlier docs were wrong:
    • Speak voices its input slot, which defaults to user_message. It does not voice the last answer. Behind a Generate, set input to that node's output.
    • A ToolCall pause times out after 2000 ms by default, inherited from the shipped workflow.tool_call_pause_timeout_ms, and the turn ends with PauseTimedOut. Set pause_timeout_ms if your tool handlers are slow.
    • An exit that names a missing node fails with 3003 GraphCompilationFailed, not 3008. An empty exit is valid and ends the turn.
    • An unknown or missing model in a graph fails CreateAgent with 3003, not 4002. A second SendMessage during a live turn returns 3004 AgentBusy.
    • tts_voice is rejected, not ignored, on every voice except Pocket TTS.
    • Unloading a model drops its pin straight away, but the model stays resident until every agent using it is destroyed.
    • A streamed answer ends with an empty terminator frame (is_final = true, text = ""), so a handler that prints the final chunk prints an empty line.
    • duration_s in turn diagnostics includes paused time. Subtract paused_duration_s to get running time.
    • The Python client needs Python 3.11 or later.

docs.title: Breaking changes and behavior changes
docs.text:
• The schema changed — rebuild every client. Voice input, the TTS and classifier nodes, the new Summarize, WriteToMemory and lip-sync messages, mutable knowledge bases, and session setup all changed shape. Rebuild your integration against the new schema and upgrade both ends together. Mismatched peers fail at connect: the client rejects the server's protocol version with 5004 ProtocolVersionMismatch. See Wire Protocol.
  • Packaged games are not yet shippable to players. Unity and Unreal player builds still launch the server in Client Dev until a Client Prod build exists, and Client Dev always sends usage telemetry (see below). Do not ship those builds to end users.
  • Client Dev usage telemetry cannot be turned off. telemetry.enabled = false does not stop the usage lane in Client Dev. The server keeps it on and warns. True opt-out exists only in Tryll Dev (--disable-telemetry, or TRYLL_SERVER_MODE=tryll-dev for an auto-launched server). include_user_content now defaults to true (was false). It applies only to activity events, so set it to false if slot text and tool arguments must not leave the machine. See Telemetry.
  • Voice turns are client-sent. BeginUtterance no longer takes an agent id, and the server no longer starts a turn from a transcript. Send UtteranceFinal text yourself (see Voice input). A busy rejection is now an AgentBusy error only, with no TurnComplete after it.
  • vad_min_silence_ms defaults to 1000 (was 500). This applies when the field is omitted, and in Unity TryllVoiceInputComponent.vadMinSilenceMs. Speech now needs a longer pause before a segment closes. Set it back to 500 if you depended on the faster cut.
  • A lexicon on a model with hotword biasing off is refused with 4106 HotwordBiasDisabled instead of being ignored. CTC-family STT models are no longer described as supporting hotwords.
  • Stricter node parameters. Schema ranges and enums are enforced at agent creation and on mutation. A graph that used to load with an out-of-range value now fails with 3003 GraphCompilationFailed, and an out-of-range ChangeAgentParam returns 3007 InvalidParamValue. sampling.max_tokens is fixed at creation (3006 ParamNotMutable). It defaults to 758 and must be at least 1 and less than the node's context size. A failed string_storage or retrieve/classify filter rebind returns 3007 and leaves the previous value in force. threshold on Retrieve and ClassifyIntent accepts a cosine distance up to 2.
  • ClassifyIntentLLM.system_prompt must reference {{intents_block}}. An empty, unparsable or incomplete template now fails CreateAgent and ChangeAgentParam. Its parameter order also changed (system_prompt, intents_ids, intents_prompt, intents). Unity and Unreal assets load by name and are unaffected.
  • Intent payloads no longer carry the agent id. Unity TryllClient.IntentClassified and IntentLlmClassified are now Action<ulong, T>, called with (agentId, classification), which matches Unreal's session delegates. AgentId is removed from TryllIntentClassification, TryllIntentLlmClassification, FTryllIntentClassification and FTryllIntentLlmClassification.
  • The storage folder is process-wide. CreateSession no longer takes a storage data folder, and relative paths resolve against the server's storage root. Unity and Unreal default to <Project>/TryllStorage/, and a storage path under Assets/ or Content/ is rejected. Move existing storage content there. See Ship storage folders for builds.
  • Config and CLI removals, with no aliases. models_download_dir is replaced by models_root. crash_dump.dir and --crash-dump-dir are gone, and crash dumps always use the logs folder (logs_dir / --log-dir). log_mode no longer chooses the log file name. The committed server-config.json sets no root keys.
  • local_path must be inside the storage root. A catalog variants[].local_path that resolves outside the process storage root is ignored with a warning, so the old C:/models-style example no longer loads. Use a relative path such as "LocalModels". Client Prod ignores local_path entirely. Every variant of a model must now name the same engine.
  • Runtime model helpers removed. Unreal UTryllSubsystem::RequestModel and OnModelReady are removed. Replace them with the explicit download / load sequence under Models and catalogs; Blueprint graphs need the node and event replaced by hand. Unity TryllClient.RequestDeleteModel / DeleteModelComplete are no longer public, so delete downloaded files from Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Model Manager.
  • Unreal TryllVoiceInputComponent.bWaitForAgentReady is removed. Voice input is now created as soon as the session is ready. If you relied on the delay, set bCreateOnConnect to false and call CreateVoiceInput() from the agent's OnAgentReady.
  • A dialog snapshot written after a fold cannot be imported by an older server. It fails there with 3022 DialogUnsupportedComponent. Snapshots from agents that never summarized are unaffected, and this release reads every older snapshot.
  • A broken models.json stops the server instead of starting with an empty catalog.

docs.title: New error codes
docs.text:
• 4106 HotwordBiasDisabled — a voice input supplied a hotwords lexicon for a model on which this session turned hotword biasing off.
  • 4107 InvalidHotwordsScore — hotwords_score is not a finite, non-negative number.
  • 6009 ModelManagementDisabled — DownloadModel or DeleteModel in a deployment mode that does not manage models (Client Prod). Ship every model with the game.
  • 8101 StorageBusy — a mutable-KB export, import, save or load was refused because an agent is not strictly idle.
  • 8102 SchemaMismatch — the store already exists under a different schema.
  • 8103 MaxRecordsExceeded — the schema's max_records cap is reached.
  • 8104 UnknownSchema — the schema name is not in schemas.json, or that file failed to load.
  • 8105 MutableKbSnapshotInvalid — the TMKB snapshot is malformed, missing fields, or has an unsupported format version.
  • 8106 StorageSnapshotTooLarge — a store or game-memory snapshot exceeds its size cap.
  • 8107 InvalidEmbedTiming — LoadGameMemory was called without Now or Lazy.
  • 8108 UnknownMutableKb — the named store does not exist. Call EnsureMutableKb first.
  • 8109 SavesDisabled — SaveGameMemory / SaveDialog refused because saves are disabled for this process. Loads still work.

See Error Codes for the full list.

docs.title: v0.9.0
docs.text:
This release gives every character its own voice. The voice moves off the speaking nodes and onto the agent as one voice profile. One workflow can then serve a whole cast, and game code can switch a character's delivery mode (angry, calm, whisper) mid-turn. LLM nodes can now load LoRA adapters, a new ClassifyAttributesLLM node scores several traits of a line in one call, and prompts can be localized through your game's own string tables. Qwen3-TTS clones a voice in ten languages, and new Use Cases and Model Benchmarks sections help you choose a design and a model.

The voice move, the classifier changes and the LoRA field all change the schema, and existing workflows need manual migration. See Breaking changes and behavior changes and Migrate to the agent voice before upgrading the plugin.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• One voice per agent. A voice profile holds the TTS model, the speaker or reference clip, speed, language, lip sync and named delivery modes. Every speaking node of the agent uses it, so one workflow can drive many characters, each with its own voice. See Add voice output to an agent.
  • Delivery modes. Define moods such as angry, calm or whisper on a profile and switch between them from game code at any time, even mid-turn. The new mode applies from the next sentence. See Delivery modes.
  • LoRA adapters on LLM nodes. Load a GGUF LoRA adapter trained for the node's model, with a scale, on any generating or classifying node. A small adapter can teach a small model a narrow job. See Generate.
  • Score several traits in one call. ClassifyAttributesLLM asks up to 16 specialist questions about a line in one batched call, with choice, true/false and 0–1 score answers written to slots.
  • Localized prompts from your string tables. Tick Localized on a prompt and Unity or Unreal resolves it through your own localization system before the agent is created. A language change updates live agents. See Localize prompts with your localization system.
  • Qwen3-TTS. Voice cloning from a 3–10 s reference clip, in 10 languages, on the same GPU backends as the language models. See TTS models.
  • Use Cases and Model Benchmarks. New docs sections that start from what the player experiences (Use Cases) and from how catalog models perform on Tryll's own jobs (Model Benchmarks).

docs.title: Agent voice
docs.text:
• Voice profiles. A VoiceProfile holds the TTS model (tts_model_name, now required), the base identity (speaker_id, reference_voice or voice_description), speed, lang, emit_visemes and named delivery modes. Unity has a Voice Profile asset (Create → Tryll → Voice Profile) assigned to the Voice field of TryllAgentComponent. Unreal has a Tryll Voice Profile data asset assigned to the agent component's Voice Profile. Python passes create_agent(graph, voice=...), and C++ sets AgentCreateOptions::voice. See Voice Profile, TryllVoiceProfile and the Blueprint catalog.
  • Delivery modes. A profile defines named moods. Switch with set_delivery_mode (Python), SetDeliveryMode (C++), SetDeliveryModeAsync (Unity) or Set Delivery Mode (Unreal), with an optional 0–1 intensity. neutral is built in. What a mode can change depends on the model: a reference clip (Pocket TTS, Qwen3-TTS), a delivery clause with a low/medium/high intensity word (Maya1), or only speed (Supertonic 3). Orpheus modes must be empty. See Delivery modes by family and Clone a voice, where "one clip per mood" is now one delivery mode per mood.
  • Per-agent delivery override. Unity TryllAgentComponent (OverrideVoiceDelivery / VoiceDelivery) and Unreal UTryllAgentComponent (Voice Delivery) can start one agent in a different mode without editing the shared profile asset. Changing it also switches a live agent in Play or in Chat.
  • Change the voice at runtime. set_voice / SetVoice / SetVoiceAsync / Set Voice replace the whole profile, model included, while the agent is idle. The new profile is checked and its clips are prepared before the swap, and if anything fails the old voice stays. The active mode is kept when the new profile defines it. Otherwise the new profile's default mode applies, and the acknowledgement carries a warning. See Change the voice or its delivery at runtime.
  • The voice is checked once, when it is set. A field the model cannot use fails with 3023 InvalidVoiceProfile and names the field. A missing TTS model is now 3023. A non-empty lang on a fixed-language voice (Pocket TTS, Orpheus, Maya1) is now rejected instead of silently ignored.
  • Clips are prepared up front. By default every reference clip in a profile, including each mode's clip, is prepared when the voice is set, so switching mood adds no delay. Set prepare to Lazy to prepare each clip on first use. See Clip preparation.
  • Speak nodes emit visemes. emit_visemes is on the voice, so every speaking node of a lip-synced character sends a viseme track, including Speak lines such as scripted refusals.
  • One audio stream per turn. The audio format is announced once per turn, by the first speaking node, and viseme offsets count from it across every speaking node of the turn. See Audio stream per turn.
  • Agents that never speak load no TTS model, even if they have a voice.
  • Model capabilities drive the editors. ListModels reports expressiveness and num_speakers for TTS models, and every shipped TTS model declares its capabilities. The Unity and Unreal profile editors show only the fields the chosen model accepts. See Model Management.
  • Maya1 delivery keywords match whole words. unhappy no longer resolves to the happy clause.
  • Diagnostics show the agent's voice. It appears under tts on GenerateAndSpeak and under a new voice section on Speak, with delivery_mode and intensity. The old tts_lang / tts_voice keys are now lang / reference_voice. See Turn Diagnostics JSON.

docs.title: Migrate to the agent voice
docs.text:
No migration helper ships. Unity drops the removed node fields from a workflow asset the next time it is saved, and Unreal drops them when an old asset loads. So record the values first.

Before upgrading the plugin, write down the TTS values of every Speak or GenerateAndSpeak node in every workflow asset: Tts Model Name, Speaker Id, Speed, Tts Lang, Tts Voice, Tts Voice Description, Tts Delivery Instruction and Emit Visemes. Also note any game code that sets these fields on node params (for example a per-character speaker or speed) or changes them with ChangeParams / ChangeAgentParam.

Unity projects, after upgrading:

  1. Create one voice profile per character: Create → Tryll → Voice Profile.
  2. Fill it from your notes: Tts Model Name, Speaker Id, Speed, Lang (was Tts Lang), Reference Voice (was Tts Voice), Voice Description and Emit Visemes. Tts Model Name is now required. A node that left it empty used the first TTS model in the catalog, usually Supertonic 3 (int8). Turn a Tts Delivery Instruction into a delivery mode with that Instruction, and select it from code with SetDeliveryModeAsync.
  3. Assign the profile to the Voice field of each TryllAgentComponent whose workflow speaks. For characters spawned at runtime, set TryllAgentComponent.Voice before the agent is created. Replace code that patched SpeakerId / Speed into cloned node params with one profile per character.
  4. Re-save each workflow asset so it no longer carries the removed fields.
  5. Replace runtime voice changes made with ChangeParams by SetVoiceAsync (identity) or SetDeliveryModeAsync (mood).

Unreal projects, after upgrading:

  1. Create one Tryll Voice Profile data asset per character and fill it from your notes, as for Unity. Check Emit Visemes for characters with lip sync. It now also covers Speak nodes, so lines from a Speak node move the lips too.
  2. Assign the profile to the Voice Profile property of each UTryllAgentComponent whose workflow speaks.
  3. Open and re-save each workflow asset, and recompile Blueprints that read or set TTS fields on node params. They must not touch a removed field.
  4. Replace runtime voice changes made with Change Params by Set Voice (identity) or Set Delivery Mode (mood).

Python and C++ code:

  1. Move the tts_* fields, speaker_id, speed and emit_visemes off SpeakParams / GenerateAndSpeakParams into a VoiceProfile. tts_lang becomes lang, tts_voice becomes reference_voice, tts_voice_description becomes voice_description, and tts_delivery_instruction becomes a DeliveryMode with that instruction.
  2. Pass it at creation: client.create_agent(graph, voice=profile) in Python, AgentCreateOptions::voice in C++.
  3. Replace change_param / ChangeParams calls on voice fields with set_voice / SetVoice or set_delivery_mode / SetDeliveryMode.

If two speaking nodes in one workflow had different voice settings, choose one. An agent now has exactly one voice.

docs.title: LoRA adapters
docs.text:
• An adaptation table on every LLM node. Generate, ToolCall, ClassifyIntentLLM, ClassifyAttributesLLM, GenerateAndSpeak and Summarize take a list of GGUF LoRA adapters (loras), each with a scale (1 = as trained, 0 = off), up to 8 per node. Paths are relative to the storage root, like voice clips. An escaping path fails with 3009 StorageOutsideRoot, and a missing file with 3010 StorageFileNotFound. See Generate.
  • An adapter must be trained for the node's model. A file made for another model fails agent creation.
  • Adapters are fixed at creation. Changing adaptation on a live agent returns 3006 ParamNotMutable. Workflows without it run on the base model as before.
  • Unity has a file picker for adapter paths, and the workflow validator flags an absolute or .. path as an error and a missing or non-.gguf file as a warning.

docs.title: Classification
docs.text:
• New ClassifyAttributesLLM node. One node scores up to 16 specialist prompts in one cached, batched call. A Choice attribute writes a label and can trigger per option. A Boolean attribute writes true / false for one statement. A Score attribute writes a normalised 0–1 level. Any trigger takes triggered_exit, otherwise the node takes default_exit. A Choice that misses threshold or margin writes uncertain_choice, which is one of its choice ids or the reserved #uncertain. Empty input never triggers. Engine failure follows on_failure. Slots are named <output_name>_<attribute>, and notify_client emits attributes_classified with every measurement.
