docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Selects an upstream inter-node slot ("input"-style fields: GenerateParams::Input, GenerateAndSpeakParams::Input, RetrieveParams::Input, SpeakParams::Input, ClassifyIntentParams::Input, ClassifyIntentLLMParams::Input, ToolCallParams::Input).

In the editor this renders as a two-kind dropdown — "User Message" plus one "Slot <X>" entry per slot reachable upstream of the owning node on some path — no free-text mode. Empty Value = "user_message" (every input-bearing node, including Speak, shares this default).

Implicitly converts to/from FString so it is mostly drop-in where a slot-name string was used before.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Names a node's effective output slot ("output_name" fields). Empty = the node's own name.

In the editor this renders a rename-commit widget: grammar ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) + reserved-name ("user_message") enforcement, uniquify against existing names/slots, and propagation of the old slot name into every input selector and {{slot.<old>}} template tag in the graph on commit.

Implicitly converts to/from FString so it is mostly drop-in where a slot-name string was used before.

    const FTryllGraphDescription & Graph,

When the graph has a ticked field, duplicate its params onto Outer and replace those strings with provider text. OutOwned is every duplicate, including when resolution fails, so the caller can root or destroy them. A graph with no ticked field is copied by value and OutOwned stays empty.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Plays a TTS viseme track as ARKit curve values, in step with audio playback.

Engine-object free so any consumer can drive it: UTryllLipSyncComponent writes the curves to morph targets, and a MetaHuman integration can push the same curves through Epic's ARKit mapping.

Per turn: BeginTurn (from UTryllSpeakerComponent::OnTtsTurnStarted), then AddEvents for each viseme frame (OnTtsVisemes). Every frame: Tick with the playback clock's played samples, then read GetCurves().

What it does, as in the Unity client's TryllLipSync: * the active viseme's pose, scaled by the event weight (loudness); * a smoothstep cross-fade over AttackDecayMs into each new viseme; * Intensity scales everything; * exponential smoothing at SmoothingPerSecond, ClosureSmoothingPerSecond while p/b/m or f/v is showing (a ~70 ms closure never lands at the slow rate); * the track is read ahead by the delay that smoothing adds, so tuning it does not move sync; * rest once the last shape of a turn has been held MaxHoldMs.

docs.text:
Plain C++ handle for a server-side VoiceInput (STT) session. Created by UTryllSubsystem after a successful CreateVoiceInputResponse. The Unreal counterpart to the C++ Tryll::VoiceInput and the Unity TryllVoiceInput.

Ownership: typically held as TSharedPtr<FTryllVoiceInput> by UTryllVoiceInputComponent. Lifetime: deterministic — the owning component releases the shared_ptr; this triggers UTryllSubsystem::RequestDestroyVoiceInput().

All callbacks are invoked on the game thread (from UTryllSubsystem::Tick).

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Per-agent NodeEvent surfaces. No AgentId pin: the component is the agent. Session-level equivalents on UTryllSubsystem stay the "all agents" escape hatch. Actor component: manages one Tryll server-side agent. Attach to any Actor; Blueprint users bind to the delegates and call SendMessage().

The graph comes from WorkflowAsset — a designer-authored data asset in the Content Browser. CreateAgent fails if no asset is assigned. To build a graph in C++ without an asset, use FTryllGraphBuilder and UTryllSubsystem::RequestCreateAgent.

The component auto-creates an agent once the session is ready (if bAutoCreateOnConnect) — it queues until OnCreateSessionComplete if it spawns before the session is configured. It auto-destroys the agent on EndPlay.

docs.title: function FindToolHandler
docs.text:
const FTryllToolHandler * UTryllAgentComponent::FindToolHandler (
    const FString & ToolName
) const

Look up a registered tool handler without going through an agent, or nullptr when this component has none for that name. Lets an external driver that runs its own agent — the Dialog Lab — invoke the same game-side handler this component would have used, instead of simulating it with authored data.

A handler that keeps per-conversation state must be told when the dialogue restarts, and such a driver's agent is not this component's, so none of the delegates here fire for it. The convention is a parameterless UFUNCTION() named ResetToolState on the handler's component, which the driver dispatches by name. The Chat panel and the Dialog Lab both run their own agent and dispatch it at each new conversation. In-game callers need nothing extra: the handler binds OnAgentReady and OnInteractionsRemoved itself.

The returned pointer is owned by this component's handler map and is invalidated by RegisterTool / UnregisterTool. Call it, do not store it.

docs.title: function SendMessage
docs.text:
void UTryllAgentComponent::SendMessage (
    const FString & Message
)

Send a user-turn message to the agent. Streaming tokens arrive on OnAnswerText; the turn ends with OnTurnComplete + OnAnswerFull. No-op if the agent is not yet ready (IsAgentReady() == false).

The message is queued, not dropped, when the agent exists but cannot accept it yet. An agent refuses a send with AgentBusy while a turn is running or a KV-cache operation is in flight — and a cache operation is exactly what happens when a game prefills the agent the player has just selected. Without queueing, a message typed during that window is silently lost and the player must retype it, which is the worst available outcome. The queue is flushed automatically when the agent becomes ready, when a turn completes, and when a cache operation finishes.

Only the most recent message is held: if two are sent before either reaches the agent, the newer line is the one the player meant. OnMessageQueued fires when a send is deferred.

docs.title: function SetDeliveryMode
docs.text:
void UTryllAgentComponent::SetDeliveryMode (
    const FString & Mode,
    float Intensity=1.f
)

Switch the voice's delivery mode, e.g. "angry". Allowed mid-turn; applies from the next sentence. "neutral" always works; a mode the profile does not define fails with UnknownDeliveryMode (3024) and the current mode stays. Intensity (0..1) scales the mode where the model can (speed scale, Maya1 clause strength, Chatterbox expressiveness). OnDeliveryModeChanged reports the result.

docs.title: function SetVoice
docs.text:
void UTryllAgentComponent::SetVoice (
    UTryllVoiceProfile * NewVoice
)

Change the agent's voice. With a live agent this sends SetAgentVoice (idle-only: AgentBusy 3004 during a turn; InvalidVoiceProfile 3023 when the model cannot use the profile, and the old voice stays) and assigns VoiceProfile on success. Without an agent it only assigns VoiceProfile for the next CreateAgent. OnVoiceChanged reports the result either way.

docs.title: function TryFlushPendingMessage

bool UTryllAgentComponent::TryFlushPendingMessage ()

Hands the queued message to the agent if it can accept one now. Safe and cheap to call repeatedly; returns true only when a message was actually handed over.

Called automatically on agent-ready, turn-complete and cache-operation-complete. It is public because a KV-residency policy that drives prefills through FTryllAgent directly — rather than through this component — closes a busy window this component never observed, and should nudge the queue when it does.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: LLM-driven text generation + streaming TTS synthesis in a single fused node. Streams LLM tokens, segments them into sentences, synthesizes each sentence on a dedicated TTS strand, and emits PCM frames via OnTtsAudio callbacks. The voice (model, speaker, delivery mode, visemes) belongs to the agent: CreateAgentRequest.voice. Agent creation fails without one (3025).

docs.title: variable FirstChunkMaxChars
docs.text:
int32 UTryllGenerateAndSpeakParams::FirstChunkMaxChars;

Time-to-first-audio knob. When > 0, the FIRST chunk may also end at a comma, semicolon or colon followed by a space, or at an em dash, and is cut at the next space once it is this wide, so speech starts sooner. Neither cut fires before 5 words or min_sentence_chars. Later chunks keep whole sentences. No effect on text without spaces (CJK). 0 = off. 48 is the measured starting point: about 40% less model-side wait on Supertonic and Pocket. Check how it sounds with your voice before shipping it.

docs.title: Public Attributes
docs.text: Type Name float BusyRetrySeconds = 0.5f int32 HotSetSize = 2 float PrefillDebounceSeconds = 0.35f bool bEnabled = true

docs.title: Public Functions
docs.text: Type Name UTryllAgentComponent * GetActiveAgent () const void Register (UTryllAgentComponent * Agent, bool bStartsResident)  void RegisterAll (bool bStartResident)  void RestoreAll ()  void SetActiveAgent (UTryllAgentComponent * Agent)  virtual void TickComponent (float DeltaTime, ELevelTick TickType, FActorComponentTickFunction * ThisTickFunction) override UTryllKvResidencyPolicy ()  void Unregister (UTryllAgentComponent * Agent)

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Keeps only the agents currently in use holding language-model KV cache, evicting the rest to reclaim VRAM.

This is a memory-for-latency trade, and it should be opt-in. With every agent's contexts resident, switching between agents is nearly free. Evicted, the first message to an agent also pays context allocation and a full prefill — on the order of a second or two — in exchange for a large VRAM saving. That is the right trade on a GPU that would otherwise not fit and the wrong one on a GPU with headroom, which is why bEnabled exists rather than this being unconditional. Drive it from a graphics-quality or "low VRAM" setting.

Why this is in the plugin rather than in your game. Nothing here is game-specific, and every part of it is a mistake waiting to be made: forgetting the debounce turns scrubbing through a character list into one uncancellable prefill per entry; forgetting the hot set punishes the most common interaction pattern there is; and forgetting that cache operations are idle-only produces intermittent AgentBusy failures that look like server bugs.

Correctness never depends on this. The server transparently restores an evicted context before the next send, so a badly tuned policy costs time to first token, not behaviour.

Usage. Add to any Actor, call Register for each agent that should participate (or RegisterAll), and call SetActiveAgent whenever the player's focus moves. Agents that must always stay warm — a background summariser that runs after every turn, say — should simply not be registered: evicting one guarantees a restore on its next turn, which is strictly worse than never evicting it.

For creation-time behaviour, pair this with UTryllAgentComponent::KvCacheInitialization = DeferAllocation on the agents it manages. That is where most of the saving comes from: a context costs its full context_size the moment it is created, so never allocating it is worth more than evicting it later.

docs.title: variable BusyRetrySeconds
docs.text:
float UTryllKvResidencyPolicy::BusyRetrySeconds;

Seconds to back off after an operation was refused with AgentBusy.

docs.title: variable HotSetSize
docs.text:
int32 UTryllKvResidencyPolicy::HotSetSize;

How many agents keep their contexts resident, including the active one.

Two is the useful default: "go back to the one I was just using" is the commonest pattern, and a hot set of one punishes it with a full restore every time. One maximises the saving.

docs.title: variable PrefillDebounceSeconds
docs.text:
float UTryllKvResidencyPolicy::PrefillDebounceSeconds;

Seconds an agent must stay active before its prefill starts.

Not cosmetic: a prefill cannot be cancelled once started, so the only way to avoid paying for agents the player merely passed over is not to start.

docs.title: variable bEnabled
docs.text:
bool UTryllKvResidencyPolicy::bEnabled;

Whether the policy evicts at all. When false nothing is evicted, so toggling at runtime is safe; call RestoreAll afterwards to warm what was evicted.

Agents created with DeferAllocation stay that way — creation mode is structural. Turning the policy off mid-session restores what it evicted; it cannot undo an allocation that never happened.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Works out which languages your game can actually offer, from the models it actually uses.

The rule is an intersection: a language is offerable only if every model in the pipeline covers it. A game with a 31-language voice but an English-only recognizer can offer exactly one language for hands-free play - and the point of this library is that you find that out from the catalog instead of from a bug report.

Blueprint-callable, so a settings menu can populate itself without C++.

Whether Model covers Locale (a tag like "de-DE" or a bare code like "de").

Returns true for a model that declares nothing: without a catalog claim we have no evidence either way, and the server applies the same rule - it withholds the language hint rather than refusing to load the model.

static TArray< FString > UTryllLanguages::OfferableLanguages (
    const TArray< FTryllModelInfo > & Models

Languages every model in Models declares, sorted.

A model that declares nothing is skipped, not treated as restrictive - an empty list means "the catalog didn't say", and letting unknown shrink the result would hide languages that work.

An empty return therefore means one of two things: the declared sets genuinely do not overlap, or nothing declared anything. Call HasLanguageInfo to tell those apart before telling a player there are no languages available.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Moves a character's mouth with its voice. Plays the server's viseme track (the agent's voice profile needs Emit Visemes on) on a face with ARKit morph targets, in step with the audio the Tryll Speaker is playing.

Only the morph targets its pose table names are written; everything else on the mesh (blinks, brows, expressions) is left to the character's animation. Written morph targets override the AnimBP's value for that name while non-zero, and return to it at rest.

Requires a UTryllSpeakerComponent: it is the audio, the playback clock and the source of the viseme track.

inline bool UTryllModelManifest::Set (
    const FString & ModelName,
    const FString & ModelType,
    ETryllModelRegistration Registration,
    const TArray< FString > * Languages=nullptr,
    const ETryllInferenceEngine * Engine=nullptr,
    const ETryllMemoryPlacement * Placement=nullptr,
    const ETryllHotwordBias * Hotwords=nullptr
)

Set (or clear) a model's registration. Setting None removes the entry so the manifest only holds models the project actually selects. Does not persist; callers invoke TryUpdateDefaultConfigFile() to write DefaultGame.ini. Returns true when this call actually changed the manifest, so a caller knows whether to write DefaultGame.ini.

Reported from here rather than compared by the caller, and that is the point. Callers used to decide for themselves — the Model Manager's catalog refresh skipped the whole call whenever cached languages matched the server, which meant a stale cached engine was never corrected. Every manifest written before the engine field existed therefore kept the enum default and silently pre-warmed nothing. Only this method knows what it caches, so only this method can say whether a write mattered; adding a field later cannot reintroduce the same bug.

docs.text:
virtual TArray< FString > UTryllNodeParamsBase::GetExitTargetOptions () const

Dropdown options for fields tagged with FlatBuffers (exit). Walks the Outer chain to find the enclosing FTryllGraphDescription (typically owned by a UTryllWorkflowAsset), then returns: [""] + node names from that graph.

The leading empty string represents END (turn finishes after this node); Unreal's Details panel renders it as a blank entry in the dropdown.

Bound via UPROPERTY meta=(GetOptions="GetExitTargetOptions") on every codegen-emitted exit field. When the params UObject is not part of an editable graph (orphaned / runtime-constructed), returns just [""].

docs.title: variable PauseTimeoutMs

int32 UTryllPauseParams::PauseTimeoutMs;

Wall-clock budget for this pause, in milliseconds. 0 = infinite: wait for ResumeAgentRequest or CancelRequest however long that takes (the shipped default, so existing graphs are unaffected). A finite budget is the right choice whenever nothing guarantees the client will resume. Structural: resolved once at agent creation.

Exit taken when pause_timeout_ms elapses. Empty = end the turn with TurnStatus.PauseTimedOut, keeping the partial interaction. docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: Project-level settings for the Tryll Client plugin. Edit in Project Settings → Plugins → Tryll Client. Persisted to <YourProject>/Config/DefaultGame.ini under [/Script/TryllClient.TryllRuntimeSettings].

docs.title: variable ConnectMaxAttempts
docs.text:
int32 UTryllRuntimeSettings::ConnectMaxAttempts;

Max number of attempts when establishing a session via UTryllSubsystem::Connect. 1 disables retry. The first call counts as attempt 1.

Sized as a cold-start backstop: after the launcher hands off a still-warming server (see ServerReadinessTimeoutSeconds), the worker retries connect+hello until the server is ready. ConnectMaxAttempts x (ConnectionReadyTimeoutSeconds + ConnectRetryDelaySeconds) must comfortably exceed a realistic cold start; it then bounds the failure (a clear error) instead of retrying forever.

docs.title: variable ConnectRetryDelaySeconds
docs.text:
float UTryllRuntimeSettings::ConnectRetryDelaySeconds;

Constant delay between connect attempts.

docs.title: variable ConnectionReadyTimeoutSeconds
docs.text:
double UTryllRuntimeSettings::ConnectionReadyTimeoutSeconds;

Per-attempt bound on how long the connection worker waits for the server's ConnectionReady hello after the TCP connect succeeds. Without this the read was unbounded: a server that accepts the socket but has not finished starting (cold-start "ConnectionReady-late") would hang the worker forever. On timeout the worker reports ConnectFailed, which consumes one attempt and re-drives the connect via the retry budget above.

docs.title: variable GameName
docs.text:
FString UTryllRuntimeSettings::GameName;

Integration identifier sent to the server on every session for telemetry grouping. Use a short, stable, lowercase slug — e.g. "my-game" or "tryll-roleplay-demo". Leave empty to omit (server defaults to "unknown" when telemetry is enabled).

docs.title: variable LlamaCppBackend
docs.text:
ETryllLlamaCppBackend UTryllRuntimeSettings::LlamaCppBackend;

llama.cpp GPU plugin for an auto-launched server. Vulkan (default) is portable and skips CUDA DLLs in a packaged build. Auto prefers CUDA on NVIDIA when those DLLs were staged. Passed as llama-backend; ignored when bAutoLaunchServer is false.

docs.title: variable Locale
docs.text:
FString UTryllRuntimeSettings::Locale;

Session language as a BCP-47 tag ("de", "de-DE", "pt-BR"). One setting the whole voice + text stack derives from, so a language menu does not have to reach into every agent: * TTS : the default for the agent voice's Lang (a voice profile that sets its own Lang still wins). * STT : language hint for multilingual recognizers (Whisper, Canary). * Files : node storage paths prefer loc/<locale>/ siblings when they exist, so localized knowledge bases and canned lines are a folder layout rather than code. * Text : templates can read the language key to write a "reply in X" instruction.

Empty leaves every one of those at its pre-locale behaviour. This is the value used at session start; to change language later call UTryllSubsystem::SetSessionLocale, which reaches existing agents' voice and template keys but not content already bound to a node. FInternationalization::Get().GetCurrentCulture()->GetName() is the usual source.

docs.title: variable SaveDataFolder
docs.text:
FString UTryllRuntimeSettings::SaveDataFolder;

Folder an auto-launched sidecar passes as save-root for SaveGameMemory / SaveDialog relative paths. Empty in the editor omits the flag (relative saves stay under the session storage root). Empty in a packaged build uses ProjectSavedDir().

docs.title: variable ServerBuildVariant
docs.text:
EServerBuildVariant UTryllRuntimeSettings::ServerBuildVariant;

Which bundled server build to launch. Only honored when both Default and Release variants are present; otherwise the single present variant is always used. The editor hides this unless both resolve.

docs.title: variable ServerPort
docs.text:
int32 UTryllRuntimeSettings::ServerPort;

Known port for the shared editor server. Every in-editor launcher (PIE, the chat panel, the model manager panel) probes this port before spawning and reuses whatever it finds there, so one warm server survives across PIE sessions and multiple open tool windows instead of each spawning its own. Packaged/player builds ignore this and always pick a free ephemeral port.

docs.title: variable ServerReadinessTimeoutSeconds
docs.text:
double UTryllRuntimeSettings::ServerReadinessTimeoutSeconds;

Seconds the launcher waits synchronously for a freshly spawned server's port to start accepting before it stops blocking the game thread and hands off to the asynchronous connect path. Kept short deliberately: a cold start (DLL paging + first-run antivirus scan of the freshly built exe) can take much longer, and the server is warming, not dead — so on timeout the launcher no longer kills it; the connection worker keeps retrying (see ConnectMaxAttempts) until the server is ready.

docs.title: variable StorageDataFolder
docs.text:
FString UTryllRuntimeSettings::StorageDataFolder;

Process-wide storage root for knowledge bases, voices, guardrails, and models. Must sit inside the project and outside Content/ — Unreal packs Content/ into .pak archives the server cannot read. Default is TryllStorage next to the .uproject.

Editor: relative to FPaths::ProjectDir(). Packaged: always <packaged project dir>/TryllStorage/ (staged NonUFS by TryllClient.Build.cs). An absolute path is kept as-is. Empty omits storage-root and the server uses its mode default (<project-dir>/TryllStorage in client-dev).

docs.title: variable TextProviderClass
docs.text:
TSubclassOf<UTryllTextProvider> UTryllRuntimeSettings::TextProviderClass;

Resolves Text IDs on Localized prompt fields. None (the default): Localized fields cannot be used and Locale above is the session language. Set (for example to TryllStringTableTextProvider, which reads Unreal string tables and follows the game culture): its current language becomes the session language, ahead of Locale, unless CreateSession is given a locale.

docs.title: variable UserModelsCatalogPath
docs.text:
FString UTryllRuntimeSettings::UserModelsCatalogPath;

Optional project-relative path to a custom models catalog JSON. Any file name. Empty means this project adds no extra models.

Stored relative to the project directory, for example "Content/Tryll/my-models.json". An auto-launched server receives the resolved file as user-models-path. A path outside the project is rejected. Leave empty when you are not adding models.

The first auto-launch runs from UTryllSubsystem::Initialize, before BeginPlay. Set the path from your GameInstance Init, or from Project Settings, so that first process sees the file. SetUserModelsCatalogPath while a server is already running restarts it; an open session is dropped.

A packaged build copies the catalog saved here to Server/data/user-catalog/ and rewrites relative chat_template_file values so they sit beside that copy. A different file chosen from code in a packaged game is used only when it is already a loose file inside the project directory.

docs.title: variable bAutoConnect
docs.text:
bool UTryllRuntimeSettings::bAutoConnect;

Connect to the server automatically once the subsystem initializes. The built-in connect-retry (ConnectMaxAttempts / ConnectRetryDelaySeconds) covers the brief window while the launched server comes up. Turn off to call Connect() yourself (e.g. from a loading screen).

docs.title: variable bAutoCreateSession
docs.text:
bool UTryllRuntimeSettings::bAutoCreateSession;

Configure the session automatically once connected, using the engine fields below. Mirrors bAutoLaunchServer, but for session setup: leave on for the simple "it just works" path; turn off to configure the session yourself (e.g. during a loading screen, or to run multiple sessions with different engines).

docs.title: variable bAutoLaunchServer
docs.text:
bool UTryllRuntimeSettings::bAutoLaunchServer;

Spawn the bundled tryll_server.exe on Initialize. Set false to run a server yourself.

docs.title: variable bEnablePlayModeModelGuard
docs.text:
bool UTryllRuntimeSettings::bEnablePlayModeModelGuard;

Editor-only. When true (default), the Play-In-Editor model guard verifies that every registered required model is downloaded before Play starts — it briefly vetoes Play, connects to the server, downloads anything missing (with a progress toast), then resumes Play automatically. Turn this off to enter Play immediately with no pre-flight check (e.g. when you provision models yourself, or to bypass the guard while debugging). No effect in packaged builds, where the guard does not exist.

docs.text:
TArray< FString > UTryllRuntimeSettings::GetLocaleOptions () const

Choices for the Locale dropdown: the languages the project's registered models declare (UTryllModelManifest), never a hardcoded list - so the menu can only ever offer something the project can actually load. Plus an empty entry, because "no session language" is a meaningful choice rather than a missing value.

A union across registered models, not an intersection: registering an English-only model for one character must not collapse the whole menu to English. Per-model mismatches surface on the model picker and at agent creation, where they are actionable.

Fallback, not the primary path. In the editor, FTryllRuntimeSettingsCustomization replaces this row with a combo that annotates each entry with a catalog model count ("German (de) - 7 models") while still storing the bare code. GetOptions cannot do that: it writes the selected string into the property, so an annotated entry would be stored as the locale. This stays for any surface that renders the property without that customization.

The (role, engine) ordinal pairs this project expects to use, derived from the registered models in UTryllModelManifest and deduped.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: Standalone TTS-only node. Voices its input-resolved slot (any upstream node's output — Generate, CannedResponse, etc. — or user_message itself), segments it into sentences, and synthesizes each on a dedicated TTS strand, emitting PCM frames via OnTtsAudio callbacks. Unlike GenerateAndSpeak it runs no LLM inference, so it can voice canned/scripted lines or any upstream-produced answer without paying for a generation pass. The voice belongs to the agent (CreateAgentRequest.voice); agent creation fails without one (3025).

docs.title: variable DefaultExit
docs.text:
FString UTryllSpeakParams::DefaultExit;

Default exit target — routes here after synthesis completes. Empty string = END. Graph exit "default" — target node name; empty = END.

docs.title: variable FirstChunkMaxChars
docs.text:
int32 UTryllSpeakParams::FirstChunkMaxChars;

Time-to-first-audio knob. When > 0, the FIRST chunk may also end at a comma, semicolon or colon followed by a space, or at an em dash, and is cut at the next space once it is this wide, so speech starts sooner. Neither cut fires before 5 words or min_sentence_chars. Later chunks keep whole sentences. No effect on text without spaces (CJK). 0 = off. Check how it sounds with your voice before shipping it.

docs.title: variable Input
docs.text:

Upstream inter-node slot this field consumes. Empty = context default.

docs.title: variable MinSentenceChars
docs.text:
int32 UTryllSpeakParams::MinSentenceChars;

Minimum width of the text since the last cut before a sentence end closes a chunk; a CJK or other 3–4-byte character counts as 2. The default 12 is two or three English words. Lower values reduce first-utterance latency at the cost of more, smaller TTS calls.

Slot name this node voices. Empty = "user_message" (same default as every other input-bearing node). Structural: immutable after creation — rebinding would re-wire the slot dataflow that is validated once at agent creation. Set to true to override the inherited Input value.

docs.text:
Reads Unreal string tables (FText::FromStringTable) and follows the game culture. Opt-in: pick it in Project Settings → Tryll Client → Text Provider.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Detailed tool-call event carrying the full owning FTryllToolCall value object (node name and disposition included) alongside the agent id. Fired in addition to — never instead of — OnToolCall / OnToolCallWithId, so a manual handler can tell whether to send results for await_result or plain-resume for other pausing dispositions. ClassifyIntentLLM — event_type="intent_llm_classified". Subscribing swallows OnNodeEvent. Pause typed event — fired for NodeEvent event_type="paused" (the executor paused the turn between nodes; ChangeAgentParam is allowed while paused). Generic NodeEvent fallback — fired for any event_type without a typed delegate (or when the typed delegate has no subscribers). KvPairs preserves wire order. Game-instance subsystem: one TCP session to the Tryll server. Manages the socket connection on a background thread (FTryllConnection) and drains the event queue on Tick(), dispatching to registered agents and delegates.

Default (zero-wiring) path — driven by UTryllRuntimeSettings: * bAutoLaunchServer → spawns the bundled tryll_server.exe on Initialize. * bAutoConnect → Connect() on Initialize (connect-retry covers server startup). * bAutoCreateSession → on Connected, CreateSessionFromSettings() sends the game name, locale and the manifest-derived engine hint. UTryllAgentComponent / UTryllVoiceInputComponent then create themselves once IsSessionReady() — they queue until OnCreateSessionComplete if they spawn earlier. So the common case is: download models in the Model Manager, add the components, press play. There is no engine to pick: each model's catalog entry names it.

Manual path — turn those flags off to drive the session yourself: * Connect() — open TCP session to ServerHost:ServerPort. * OnConnectionChanged(bConnected=true) — bind to continue; or poll IsConnected(). * CreateSession(GameName, Locale) — configure explicitly (overrides settings). Completion arrives on OnCreateSessionComplete; IsSessionReady() is true thereafter. * CreateAgent — attach a UTryllAgentComponent (auto-creates once the session is ready) or call RequestCreateAgent(). * SendMessage(Text) — drive one turn; chunks on OnAnswerText, the turn ends with OnTurnComplete(Status). * RequestDestroyAgent / Disconnect — tear down when done.

All delegates fire on the game thread from Tick(); it is safe to touch UObjects and UI directly from callbacks.

void UTryllSubsystem::Connect ()

Open a TCP session to ServerHost:ServerPort. Asynchronous — completion is reported via OnConnectionChanged(bConnected=true). Errors fire OnError. Calling Connect() while already connected is a no-op.

docs.title: function CreateSession
docs.text:
void UTryllSubsystem::CreateSession (
    FString GameName=TEXT(""),
    FString Locale=TEXT(""),
    bool bUseProjectLocaleWhenEmpty=true
)

Send CreateSessionRequest. Must be called after Connected and before CreateAgent. Result is delivered via OnCreateSessionComplete delegate.

Parameters:

  • GameName Integration identifier for telemetry grouping (e.g. "tryll-roleplay-demo"). Leave empty to omit; the server defaults to the project name, then "unknown", when telemetry is on. Pass UTryllRuntimeSettings::GameName to drive this from the project settings asset.
  • Locale Session language as a BCP-47 tag (e.g. "de", "pt-BR"). See UTryllRuntimeSettings::Locale for everything it drives. Empty uses the project setting unless bUseProjectLocaleWhenEmpty is false; a malformed tag is rejected with InvalidLocale (2004).
  • bUseProjectLocaleWhenEmpty When true, an empty Locale adopts the text provider's current language, then UTryllRuntimeSettings::Locale. Set false with an empty Locale to explicitly disable session language. The four engine parameters this took through protocol v12 are gone. The engine set is derived from the models registered in UTryllModelManifest — each model's catalog entry already states which engine runs it, so there is nothing for a caller to choose, and nothing that can drift out of step with the models the project references.

Storage root is process-wide (set when the server launches via storage-root), not per session — protocol v24 removed CreateSessionRequest.storage_data_folder.

docs.title: function CreateSessionFromSettings
docs.text:
void UTryllSubsystem::CreateSessionFromSettings ()

Configure the session from project settings (UTryllRuntimeSettings): game name, locale, and the engine warm-up hint derived from UTryllModelManifest. Storage root is process-wide (set at server launch).

This is the "use settings" path. It runs automatically once connected when UTryllRuntimeSettings::bAutoCreateSession is true; call it yourself if you connected with that flag disabled and still want the settings-driven config. To override settings, call CreateSession() with explicit parameters instead.

    bool bEnableDiagnostics=false,

  • bEnableDiagnostics When true the server populates TurnComplete.debug_info.
  • bMaintainDialogueHistory When true (default) the agent keeps its full dialogue history; when false the history is discarded after each turn (stateless agent — for classification/routing/tool-picking agents).
  • Voice The agent's voice (protocol v27). Required when any node speaks (FTryllGraphDescription::UsesTts): the server fails creation with AgentVoiceRequired (3025) without one. Unset for a silent agent.

docs.title: function SetSessionLocale
docs.text:
void UTryllSubsystem::SetSessionLocale (
    FString Locale
)

Change the session language without tearing the session down. Pass an empty Locale to clear it.

Applies to every agent, existing and future, from its next turn: TTS language and the locale template keys are read per turn, not captured at agent creation. A new voice input picks up the new STT language hint; one already open keeps its recognizer. Storage paths re-resolve on the next load, but content already bound to a node (a Retrieve KB, canned lines) does NOT swap - those params are structural, so switching authored content still means recreating agents.

Not turn-atomic: a turn already running may render its prompt under the old locale and synthesize under the new one.

Completion is broadcast via OnSetSessionLocaleComplete.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: Rolling conversation summary. Every time the history since the last fold crosses a trigger, this node compresses the older interactions (everything outside keep_recent_turns) into a SummaryComponent. Generate-class projection then renders that summary at the end of its system message and replays history only from covered_through + 1, so a long dialogue stays coherent at a fixed token cost instead of being trimmed away. Place it last in the graph, after the node that produced the player-facing reply.

Changes how the model behaves for this node (LoRA adapters; later control vectors). Null = base model. Structural: applied to the llama context at creation, so a change means a new context. Appended last so existing field IDs do not move.

The node always runs under its own instruction-only system prompt, never a character persona; point this at a plain instruct model when the character itself runs on roleplay-fine-tuned weights. Empty = the built-in default. Set to true to override the inherited Template value.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Actor component: owns one FTryllVoiceInput (STT) handle and drives it from the system microphone. The Unreal counterpart to the Unity TryllVoiceInputComponent.

Capture model: on-demand. The microphone opens on BeginUtterance() and closes when the final transcript arrives (or on End / Cancel). The component ticks to drain captured PCM and forward it to the server.

Audio: the device-native sample rate is declared to the server, which resamples to the STT model's expected rate. Multi-channel input is downmixed to mono. If the default device's rate changes under a live voice input, the next BeginUtterance recreates the voice input with the new rate (VoiceInputStarting).

Microphone check: CreateVoiceInput() and every BeginUtterance() first check that a default capture device exists. Without one the voice input is not created (no STT model is loaded), GetMicrophoneStatus() says why, one warning is logged, and each call raises OnErrorDetailed with ETryllErrorCode::MicrophoneUnavailable (except automatic creation, which may run before listeners bind: read GetMicrophoneStatus() at start-up). A later BeginUtterance() that finds a microphone creates the voice input and raises ETryllErrorCode::VoiceInputStarting for that call; so does one that finds the device's sample rate changed.

All delegates fire on the game thread.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Data asset that stores a Tryll workflow graph description. Equivalent to a Unity ScriptableObject holding node and wire lists.

Usage: * In the Content Browser: right-click → Tryll → Workflow Asset. * Edit nodes and routes in the Details panel. * Assign this asset to a UTryllAgentComponent's WorkflowAsset property.

Programmatic alternative: populate FTryllGraphDescription directly in C++ using FTryllGraphBuilder and pass it to UTryllSubsystem::RequestCreateAgent.

Editor / cook: IsDataValid + PreSave(IsCooking) fail when the graph references a model that is not marked Production in the Tryll Model Manifest (so packaging cannot silently omit it).

docs.title: enum ETryllHotwordBias
docs.text:
enum ETryllHotwordBias {
    Default = 0,
    Off = 1,
    On = 2
};

Per-model build selection for this project. Ordinals match the Unity client's TryllModelRegistration so a shared manifest stays interchangeable. Whether this project wants hotword biasing on an STT model. Mirrors the wire HotwordBias enum.

Unlike ETryllMemoryPlacement this is not a hint the server can quietly downgrade. Biasing requires beam-search decoding, which a recognizer fixes when it is constructed, so the answer decides which recognizer a session is served — and two sessions that disagree about one model hold two of them.

docs.title: enum ETryllMemoryPlacement
docs.text:
enum ETryllMemoryPlacement {
    Auto = 0,
    Ram = 1,
    Vram = 2
};

Where a model's weights should live. Mirrors the wire MemoryPlacement enum.

Always a hint: a machine that cannot honour it loads the model the other way and reports what it did. That matters here because this value is authored on a developer's machine and shipped to players' machines — a VRAM choice that suits a 24 GB card is not a promise an 8 GB card can keep.

Which GPU API provides VRAM (CUDA / Vulkan) is deliberately not expressible: that is the host's decision, not the project's.

docs.title: enum ETryllVariableOp
docs.text:
enum ETryllVariableOp {
    Assign = 0,
    AddToSet = 1,
    RemoveFromSet = 2,
    Reset = 3
};

Mutation applied to one declared agent variable in a batched UpdateAgentVariablesRequest. Mirrors Tryll::VariableOp (wire enum) — ordinal values must stay in sync.

Assign: overwrite; value must match the variable's declared type. AddToSet/RemoveFromSet: target must be StringSet; value carried in StringValue (idempotent — a no-op success if already present/absent). Reset: restore the CreateAgent-time initial value; no value fields are read.

    Int = 0,
    Float = 1,
    String = 2,
    Bool = 3,
    StringSet = 4
};

Wire type of one declared per-agent variable. Mirrors the Tryll::VariableValue union member that carries the value (VarInt/VarFloat/VarString/VarBool/VarStringSet).
